domains.name: Patient access, booking, queue & ETA
domains.summary: Patient Access turns a WhatsApp 'Hi', a desk walk-in or a web visit into a confirmed booking, one token and an honest wait range, and keeps every desk, doctor screen, lobby TV and patient in sync within seconds. It covers the booking rules engine (auto, review or hybrid per visit type; slot or token sessions; walk-in interleave; solo mode), the integrity fixes that must land before real patient data (no double booking, no double check-in, compare-and-set queue moves, sessions that cross midnight), the ETA engine built from real consult timings with display modes, leave-home alerts and delay/no-show/waitlist automation, SSE live queue and lobby display, the Patient Access Edge (WhatsApp bot flows, branded booking site and widget, patient web, aggregator) and the gated Expo app. 60 stories in 12 epics, 469.0 engineer-days in total, against 424 tracker days for the 48 in-scope tasks (Areas Booking, Queue & ETA, Front desk, Aggregator, Patient app) plus 113 days for 9 closely-coupled WhatsApp/real-time/ETA tasks this domain also delivers (T-091, T-094, T-120, T-162, T-164, T-165, T-166, T-177, T-189), i.e. 537 tracker days overall.
open_questions: Ownership overlap with the comms/WhatsApp domain: this spec also claims T-120 (Edge skeleton), T-162 (booking conversation), T-165 (dependants), T-166 (chat registration) and T-189 (Edge GA) because the brief places bot conversation logic in patient-edge. If the comms domain also specs them, dedupe at merge: Comms keeps sending, templates, webhooks, STOP and reminders scheduling (T-145, T-170); ACC keeps conversation flows and Core internal APIs.

Also claimed from other Areas because they are the ETA/live-queue core of this domain: T-094 (SSE + /queue/board, Area 'Caching & real-time'), T-091 (ETA simulator, Area 'AI/CDS'), T-164 (ETA accuracy, Area 'Observability'), T-177 (Solo preset, Area 'Owner admin'). The shared browser SSE client T-095 stays with Frontend.
T-248 has two halves: cross-facility delay propagation (ACC-056) is here; 'portable favourites' (Rx favourites across facilities, RX-01) belongs to the Clinical domain.

T-128 (duplicate-merge suggestions and undo) and T-086 (phone validation) touch the patient registry; if another domain owns core/patient, move ACC-030/ACC-028 there. T-279 (Emirates ID) and T-294 (Iqama, Hijri-first) may belong to a GCC/market domain; T-318 (help and training) is owned by Product & Design in the tracker; T-286 (call-centre console) by Hospital; T-256/T-257 by Patient App. They are specced here because their Area is in scope.
Migration numbering: this spec uses V300-V338 for Core and a separate V1..V8 sequence for the patient-edge database. Please reserve the V300-V349 band for ACC or renumber at merge.

Event names: this spec uses comms.notification.requested.v1 for the command to the Comms Gateway (doc 06 calls it 'notification.requested'). Align the final name with the comms and events (T-079) owners.
Depends_on uses tracker ids (T-xxx) for work in other domains because their story ids were not available when this was written; map them to PLT-/COM-/CNS- story ids at merge.
DEC-37 (offline at MVP): ACC-034 is designed as Phase 2; pull into Phase 1 if a tier-2 clinic joins the pilot. Founder decision due 14 Dec 2026.
DEC-38 (kiosk ban): self check-in is phone/QR only (ACC-033) and the lobby display is read-only (ACC-023). Confirm the prototype 'kiosk' wording is removed (T-327).
DEC-41 / DEC-07 (patient app 'soon' vs Phase 3): ACC-059/ACC-060 start with a recorded go/no-go. Founder confirmation due 30 Nov 2026.
FRD PAT-07 / SYS-06 want waitlist self-join and auto-offers at MVP, the tracker keeps T-232 in Phase 2 (ACC-027). Decide whether to pull it into Phase 1 together with DEC-37.
DEC-28 / FRD PERSONA-12: the FRD removed call-centre features; ACC-057 keeps T-286 in Phase 5 as a hospital-chain re-scope with no CTI. Confirm with the founder.
CEO-13 / DEC-27: gender-of-doctor filter for KSA is deferred (ACC-014 keeps the attribute only).

Review SLA and expiry for 'requested' bookings: the spec escalates after the SLA (default 10 min) instead of auto-declining. Confirm with pilot clinics; the prototype shows 10-60 min SLAs by request type.

Red-flag/emergency phrase lists (ACC-009 triage flags, ACC-051 emergency redirect) need clinical sign-off per language (EN, HI, KN, TE, AR) before go-live; who owns the list (ACC or the clinical safety officer)?
Overbooking: the spec never allows overlapping slots (EXCLUDE); extra patients come in as walk-in tokens under the session cap. Confirm no pilot clinic needs deliberate double-booking of slots.
Region model: tenants and licence_registry only know IN/KSA today; phone validation (ACC-028), emergency numbers and the lobby languages need the region record from EP09 (UAE, Qatar).

epics.title: Visit and booking integrity (make it safe)
epics.goal: Before any real patient data, a slot can be booked once, an appointment checked in once, and a visit moved only along legal steps, even with two desks working at the same time.

epics.title: Clinic day, schedules, leave and reasons
epics.goal: Calendars match how clinics really run: evening sessions past midnight, part-day leave, patients told automatically when staff change their booking, and one coded reason list everywhere.

epics.title: Booking rules engine and workflow configuration
epics.goal: Clinics set their booking and queue rules once (auto-accept, review or hybrid; caps; slot or token sessions; walk-in interleave; solo mode) and never accept routine bookings by hand.

epics.title: Queue events and ETA engine
epics.goal: Patients and staff see an honest wait range (within +/-10 min for at least 80% of visits) built from real consult timings, shown the way each doctor chooses.

epics.title: Live queue over SSE and waiting-room display
epics.goal: Every desk, doctor screen and lobby TV shows the same queue within 2 seconds of any change, without polling.

epics.title: Delay, pause, no-show and waitlist automation
epics.goal: Everyone affected by a delay, pause, no-show or freed slot knows within a minute, without the receptionist phoning anyone.

epics.title: Front desk v2
epics.goal: The desk registers a walk-in in under 45 seconds by keyboard, finds the right family member in under 10 seconds, and only handles exceptions while patients check themselves in.

epics.title: Patient Access Edge and WhatsApp booking
epics.goal: A patient says 'Hi' on WhatsApp and is booked in under a minute with buttons, manages the booking in chat, and knows when to leave home, through a separate public-facing service that holds no PHI beyond what it relays.

epics.title: Clinic-branded booking and patient web
epics.goal: Patients book and manage bookings on the clinic's own web page or widget and follow the live queue on the web, under the same rules as WhatsApp.

epics.title: Aggregator (web and shared WhatsApp number)
epics.goal: New patients find opted-in Nabd clinics by specialty, language, area, next slot and live wait, and book into the clinic's own queue, without Nabd ever steering a clinic's patients elsewhere.

epics.title: Multi-facility doctors and call centre
epics.goal: A doctor who works at several facilities is never double-booked across them, delays propagate to every facility, and chains can book centrally.

epics.title: Patient app (gated, Phase 3)
epics.goal: If the go/no-go signals pass, patients and caregivers get a fast native app for what WhatsApp does badly: caregivers, records, consent and payments, plus booking and live queue.

domains.name: Owner admin, setup & reporting
domains.summary: ADM turns a clinic owner's first hour and every morning after into product: self-serve trial with a demo clinic and a signed DPA gate before real data, a resumable setup wizard with solo / single-specialty / multi-specialty / hospital presets, Excel and old-software import, no-lock-in full export with a deletion certificate, staff, roles and departments, multi-branch lite (FRD SYS-24), the regional calendar (state holidays, Hijri, prayer times, Ramadan), licence reminders and a compliance health card, plan entitlements and self-service plan changes, the Control Plane extraction, time-based owner dashboards, live operations, a reports library with scheduled delivery, and HR basics. 58 stories, 322.5 engineer-days in total. Tracker effort for the in-scope tasks is 227 days (219 excluding T-356, which belongs to COM); the extra ~104 days are prototype scope with no tracker task (HR basics, India holiday calendar, go-live check, staff admin UI, live operations, departments, tax and productivity reports) plus splitting the 25-day trial and Control Plane tasks into deliverable stories.
open_questions: T-356 (post-visit feedback, NPS and complaints queue) belongs to COM (recall, reviews and feedback). ADM-041 shows an NPS tile only when COM's feedback data exists; please confirm COM owns it.

T-357 has three parts. ADM covers delegations (ADM-019) and the tenant lifecycle console (ADM-020). The part where the desk sees guardian age-18 reviews that are due belongs to IDC and is covered by IDC-012.
T-334 has three parts. ADM covers the traffic-light compliance health card (ADM-033). The per-facility versioned privacy notice and the grievance contact belong to IDC and are covered by IDC-025.

T-332 (multi-branch lite, area Tenancy), T-305 (preset role bundles, area Auth) and T-271 (Hijri, prayer times and Ramadan, area i18n/RTL) are filed under other areas, but the ADM brief puts them in ADM's scope. ADM has specced them (ADM-022..027, ADM-017, ADM-029..031). The Platform/Trust and i18n PSEs should not duplicate them; please confirm.

Cross-branch double-booking of a doctor who works at two branches (prototype: 'schedules are checked against each other') is a scheduling rule and belongs to ACC (it relates to T-247, the unified doctor calendar). ADM-022 only copies the schedule.
T-381 (ward duty roster) depends on DEC-15 (build or partner for hospital modules), which is deferred to month 12. ADM-058 is specced but stays behind the ipd entitlement.

DEC-10 and DEC-34 (pricing model: free Solo Starter; per-clinic vs per-doctor) are still open. ADM-034 (pricing_basis) and ADM-004 (on_trial_expiry) are designed so that either answer works. Commercial still needs to confirm trial length (14 days assumed) and the free-plan visit cap.
DEC-35 (WhatsApp pricing: markup vs fair-use allowance) changes how usage is shown on the plan page (ADM-037). Usage data depends on T-365 (per-tenant cost attribution).

DPA signing method: is an OTP click-through enough in each market, or must India use Aadhaar eSign and KSA Nafath? ADM-002 treats OTP as the baseline and the others as optional. Counsel needs to confirm.

Offboarding (ADM-016) gives the clinic every record in the export and keeps nothing, including the 8-year GST invoices. Counsel needs to confirm that a processor may delete these once the controller holds them.
Migration numbers V300-V336 and cp/V1-V14 are placeholders reserved for ADM. Data & Infra needs to confirm a numbering scheme across domains so numbers do not collide.
Rollups (T-112) and the OLAP pipeline belong to the Data domain. ADM-041 adds time-KPI columns, and ADM-045 assumes the Data domain picks the OLAP store (ClickHouse or a Postgres analytics replica).
Tax registrations, invoice series and per-branch fee overrides are FIN's (T-107, T-306). ADM-024 only owns the branch settings orchestration and UI.
The import story ADM-013 writes drug and stock lists through the Pharmacy domain's StockCommands. The Pharmacy PSE should confirm that API exists by Phase 1.
DEC-29 ('corporates') is open. If it means employer billing, a corporate-accounts epic is needed. ADM has not specced it.

epics.title: Self-serve trial, DPA gate and provisioning
epics.goal: A clinic owner goes from the website to a working demo clinic in under 5 minutes, and no real patient data can enter a tenant until a plan and a signed DPA exist.

epics.title: Setup wizard, facility presets and go-live
epics.goal: A non-IT owner sets up a clinic in under an hour with a preset that matches how the clinic runs, and goes live as soon as the true blockers are cleared.

epics.title: Data import and no-lock-in export
epics.goal: A clinic brings its old patient list in on day one and can take everything out, any time, without a support ticket.

epics.title: Staff, roles and departments
epics.goal: Every new clinic starts with correct role bundles, and the owner manages staff, access, delegations and departments from one screen.

epics.title: Multi-branch lite (FRD SYS-24)
epics.goal: An owner with 2-3 branches runs them with one login, adds a branch in under 15 minutes, keeps per-branch schedules, fees, invoice series and WhatsApp routing, and links a patient across branches only explicitly.

epics.title: Regional calendar
epics.goal: Schedules, messages and package validity follow local holidays, Hijri dates, prayer times and Ramadan hours without manual work.

epics.title: Compliance health and licences
epics.goal: The owner sees one traffic-light card for compliance, and no clinician with a lapsed licence can be booked online or sign.

epics.title: Plans, entitlements, self-service plan changes and the Control Plane
epics.goal: Plan tiers are real (modules and seats enforced), operators can switch a feature off for one tenant in under a minute, owners change plan themselves, and the operator plane runs as its own service with no PHI.

epics.title: Owner dashboards, live operations and daily summaries
epics.goal: Each morning the owner sees the time metrics that matter, can act on live problems during the day, and gets a summary on WhatsApp at close.

epics.title: Reports library and scheduled delivery
epics.goal: The owner and accountant get trustworthy money, patient and team reports from rollups, with drill-down, audited exports and scheduled delivery.

epics.title: HR basics for small teams
epics.goal: Small clinics run split shifts, simple attendance, leave and a monthly payroll file for the accountant, without a payroll engine; hospitals get a ward duty roster later.

domains.name: Clinical, e-prescription, AI safety & specialties
domains.summary: CLN owns everything a clinician touches during and around a consult: the Phase 0 clinical-safety baseline (CORS fix, CSO and hazard log, versioned safety dictionary, licence-based signing), the consult workspace (solo phone flow, shared templates, ICD-10, referrals, signed procedure consent, results inbox), nursing inbox and task handoff, the e-prescription chain (licensed drug master, coded generic-first Rx, signed QR PDF, validity/refills, pharmacy routing, ABDM/DHA/Wasfaty), the Clinical Intelligence service (licensed rules first, governed opt-in AI suggestions), all nine FRD specialty profiles, and teleconsultation under TPG 2020. 60 stories, 476 engineer-days, against 439 tracker effort-days for the 42 in-scope tasks; the difference is mainly 3 gap stories with no tracker task (results inbox, ABDM e-Rx bundle, Wasfaty prescriber submission) and the split of 25-day tasks into buildable stories.
open_questions: T-091 (ETA simulator) is tagged AI/CDS but is the ETA model offline tuner; it belongs to ACC (Patient access, booking, queue & ETA). Not covered here.

T-280 (DHA e-Rx) is owned by the GCC squad in the tracker; CLN-029/030 specify it. Confirm Clinical owns the e-Rx submission and Money & Pharmacy/GCC own the dispense-eligibility UI (CLN-030 module core/pharmacy).

T-293 (Wasfaty + SFDA RSD) covers only the dispense side and belongs to the pharmacy domain; CLN-031 adds the missing prescriber-side Wasfaty submission with no tracker task. Add a tracker task or fold into T-293?

No tracker task owns the doctor results inbox (prototype doctor.results); CLN-015 specifies it and depends on T-220/T-221 (Diagnostics & Interop). Confirm ownership split for critical-value escalation timers (lab) vs acknowledgement (clinical).
No tracker task maps signed prescriptions to an ABDM PrescriptionRecord FHIR bundle; CLN-028 specifies it on top of T-234/T-235. Confirm with Diagnostics & Interop.

T-092 (H-07) wording is ambiguous: 'max-age' could mean the patient's age (adults refused) or the age of the weight reading. CLN-003 implements both; CSO to confirm staleness windows (30 days under 2 y, 90 days otherwise).
CLN-005 depends on staff.is_clinician from T-305 (Platform & Trust). If T-305 is not merged by S2, Clinical adds the column and hands it over; confirm.
Rx revocation conflicts with the V51 'signed is final' trigger. CLN-023 proposes a SECURITY DEFINER revoke function or a separate rx_revocations table; CSO and Data/Infra to choose.
DEC-32 (pharmacy model sequencing) is open until Jan 2027; CLN-025 keeps external mode as default and works for any outcome. T-178's 'clinic pharmacy default' applies only to hybrid/in_house tenants.
DEC-42 (AI prescription suggestions) is open until May 2027; CLN-040/041 are built opt-in, entitlement-gated and can be cut without affecting CLN-032..039.
SaMD position (RM D5, doc06 D11): counsel opinion for India CDSCO draft and SFDA MDS-G010 must land before CLN-040 starts; if it requires clinical evaluation, CLN-040 grows.
Licensed KB (T-199/CLN-018) must be signed by S5 or CLN-019..021 and CLN-032 slip and MF-51 stays on the CSO dictionary. Budget owner?
ICD-10-AM (UAE/KSA) and a GCC drug KB with DHA/SFDA codes are separate purchases needed before CLN-029/031; confirm timing with DEC-27.
Teleconsult video partner (CEO-18) not chosen; CLN-058/059 keep it behind an adapter per region. Need partner shortlist with in-region hosting for India and GCC.
Migration numbers are written as V1xx placeholders; final numbers are assigned at merge to avoid collisions with other domains (current max V85).
Specialty module: dental code currently lives in clinical/dental; CLN-042 creates core module `specialty` and moves dental over time. Confirm with Core Backend (ADR-02 module map).

epics.title: Clinical safety baseline (Phase 0 exit gate)
epics.goal: No real patient data enters Nabd until safety rules fire from the UI, are content-reviewed by a named CSO, and only licensed clinicians can sign.

epics.title: Consult workspace, notes, consent and results
epics.goal: A doctor (or a solo doctor on a phone) goes from 'call next' to a signed note, signed Rx, consent and referral without retyping, and never misses a result.

epics.title: Nursing: clinical inbox and task handoff
epics.goal: Clinical questions from patients reach a nurse (not the receptionist) with an SLA, and doctor-to-nurse tasks are acknowledged and escalated when overdue.

epics.title: e-Prescription: drug master, signed Rx, validity, routing and national e-Rx
epics.goal: A doctor writes a coded, generic-first Rx in < 90 s (< 30 s repeat), the patient gets a verifiable QR Rx any pharmacy can check, and national e-Rx rails are plugged in per market.

epics.title: Clinical Intelligence: licensed rules first, governed AI suggestions second
epics.goal: Interaction, duplicate-therapy, allergy, pregnancy and renal checks run on a licensed KB in < 1 s with sources, only severe alerts interrupt, and any AI output is opt-in, labelled, in-region and audited.

epics.title: Specialty profile framework and the nine FRD specialty workspaces
epics.goal: One Doctor persona whose home, quick actions, fields and templates change by specialty profile (GP, DERM, DENT, PED, ENT, ORTH, GYN, HOM, AYU), gated by entitlement, with no change to the consult shell per profile.

epics.title: Teleconsultation through a compliant partner
epics.goal: A clinic that switches teleconsult on can sell a prepaid video visit, run it through a partner room with identity and consent checks, and issue an e-Rx that obeys India TPG 2020 / GCC telehealth rules.

domains.name: Messaging & engagement
domains.summary: COM turns Nabd's outbound-only WhatsApp plumbing (messaging module, V44 outbox, V46/V47) into a governed two-way patient channel: persist-then-ack webhooks with STOP honoured in under a minute, a separate Comms Gateway (ADR-01) with one notification contract, branded senders (shared Nabd number first, clinic numbers via embedded signup in Phase 2), quality-aware throttling, send windows with quiet hours and KSA prayer times, India DLT SMS fallback, the reception shared inbox, the WhatsApp booking conversation on the Patient Access Edge, and the engagement module (recall engine, reviews, feedback, complaints, referral rewards). It matters because WhatsApp is how patients book, get reminded and come back, and every one of those messages must be consented, PHI-free on the lock screen and on time. 59 stories, 359 engineer-days, against 288 tracker days for the 30 in-scope tasks; the gap is mostly scope the tracker does not size (email, preferences, quiet hours and prayer windows, cost ledger, a recall engine that T-296 sizes at 8 days but needs about 21).
open_questions: Overlap with ACC (Patient access, booking, queue & ETA): T-120 (Edge skeleton), T-162, T-165, T-166, T-189 and T-317 are Area=WhatsApp so they are specified here (COM-034 to COM-042), but ACC may also claim the Patient Access Edge and booking flow. Coordinator: keep one owner per story; COM keeps bot-flows/comms, ACC keeps booking rules (EP10, T-161) and ETA/leave-now (EP11/EP13).

T-304 and T-346 (package card/nudges, buy package in WhatsApp) are Area=WhatsApp but tracker-owned by Money & Pharmacy. Specified here as COM-044/COM-045; the billing domain may prefer to own them, in which case COM only provides templates and sending.
T-135 (WhatsApp chaos test suite) belongs to the QA/CI domain; COM-010 provides the provider stub and virtual-patient harness it needs and lists T-135 in tracker_refs for traceability.

T-373 (KSA pack, 25 days) belongs to the GCC/KSA domain; COM-024 covers only its 'notifier skips prayer windows and Friday prayer' criterion. The PDPL pack, Mada/STC Pay and gender-of-doctor default stay with that domain.

Message-sending consumers that belong to other domains and depend on COM-004/COM-023: T-170 is here, but T-171 delay broadcast, T-232 waitlist auto-offer and T-302 staff reschedule notices belong to ACC; T-215 refill reminders belongs to Money & Pharmacy; T-191 owner daily WhatsApp summary belongs to the owner/reporting domain; T-344 nurse triage inbox belongs to Clinical (COM-032 publishes the clinical tag it consumes); T-179 secure links, T-237 DSR engine, T-137 consent capture and T-297 caregiver proxy belong to the consent/identity domain.
Cross-domain depends_on use tracker task ids (T-xxx) because other domains' story ids are not known yet; the coordinator should map them to story ids.
DEC-35 (WhatsApp cost: allowance vs markup, needed 16 Nov 2026): COM-015 keeps allowance and markup as plan data so either answer works; confirm before the owner usage page ships.
DEC-27 (KSA at MVP vs Phase 5): prayer-window sending (COM-024) ships dark for India and switches on per region; Arabic flows (COM-049) stay Phase 4 unless a KSA customer is signed.

DEC-12 / RM D8 (utility templates only, no marketing campaigns): review requests (COM-056) and referral messages (COM-059) may be classified MARKETING by Meta. Decide whether to send them only with marketing consent (COM-013 handles re-categorisation) or drop them in markets where that consent is rare.
T-259 voice reminders (COM-048) conflicts with FRD SYS-03 ('voice-call channel dropped'). A founder decision is needed before Phase 3.
T-229 pre-visit intake (COM-047) is R2 in the roadmap but deferred to Phase 3 in FRD RCP-06. It is built behind a per-clinic flag; confirm the phase.
Meta Tech Provider status vs BSP for embedded signup (COM-017) and the Indian SMS BSP choice (COM-026) are procurement dependencies with lead times. Both need an owner and a date.

Claim-check design (COM-004): events carry ids only and Comms fetches render params from Core/Edge at send time. This needs ADR sign-off because it adds a synchronous Comms->Core call on every send, within the 3 s and window budgets.
Shared inbox access path (COM-030): staff-web reaches Comms through Core /v1/inbox/** (Core keeps staff auth and audit). Confirm this, rather than having Comms validate staff JWTs directly.

Migration numbering: Core migrations are written V1xx__*.sql and need real numbers at merge (other domains also add migrations after V85). Comms and Edge have their own Flyway sequences (comms/V1.., edge/V1..).

epics.title: Two-way WhatsApp foundation inside Core
epics.goal: Inbound messages, STOP and delivery states are stored, deduplicated and acted on before any patient data flows, using the existing messaging module.

epics.title: Comms Gateway as its own service
epics.goal: Meta secrets, the public webhook and bursty sending live in a separate deployable with its own database that talks to Core only by contract (ADR-01).

epics.title: Sender identity and template lifecycle
epics.goal: Every message comes from a verified sender that shows the clinic's name, using PHI-free templates that move cleanly through Meta review, first on the shared Nabd number and later on the clinic's own number.

epics.title: WhatsApp quality monitoring, throttling and priority lanes
epics.goal: A campaign or bad template can never get a clinic's number restricted or delay an appointment reminder.

epics.title: Send windows, quiet hours, prayer times and patient preferences
epics.goal: Messages go out only when they are useful and welcome: inside their window, outside quiet hours and prayer times, in the patient's language and to the people the patient chose.

epics.title: SMS fallback, India DLT and email
epics.goal: Patients without WhatsApp, or when WhatsApp fails, still get OTPs and reminders through compliant SMS, and documents can go by email.

epics.title: Reception WhatsApp shared inbox
epics.goal: Reception answers patient chats from one screen, within WhatsApp's 24-hour rules, with canned replies, assignment and a full audit trail.

epics.title: WhatsApp booking conversation on the Patient Access Edge
epics.goal: A patient types 'Hi' and is booked in under a minute, for themselves or a child, without the desk and without public traffic touching Core.

epics.title: Patient journeys on WhatsApp: reminders, packages, check-ins, intake and languages
epics.goal: The messages around a visit (before, after and between) reduce no-shows and desk calls, in the patient's language.

epics.title: My records and privacy on WhatsApp
epics.goal: A patient or caregiver can see visits, prescriptions, reports and bills and raise privacy requests from WhatsApp, with nothing medical in a message body.

epics.title: Recall engine (engagement module)
epics.goal: Patients come back when their treatment says they should: the doctor sets it in one tap, rules send a booking link, and the desk calls the ones who do not book.

epics.title: Reviews, feedback, complaints and referral rewards
epics.goal: Clinics earn reviews fairly, hear every patient's feedback, resolve complaints within an SLA, and reward patients who bring friends, within ethics and platform rules.

domains.name: Frontend foundation
domains.summary: FEF delivers the frontend foundation every persona works in: safe sessions (silent refresh, httpOnly-cookie BFF, CSP, patched Next.js), one generated API client with TanStack Query and SSE so desks agree within 2 s, a design system and Dark/Light themes from the prototype tokens, next-intl with Indian languages and Arabic RTL, print layouts for invoices and receipts, an installable staff PWA, and Playwright journeys J1-J15 with axe and visual regression. It also ports the prototype's persona shells into staff-web and patient-web so feature squads build into one consistent frame. 63 stories, 397 engineer-days in total (51 in Phase 0, 297 in Phase 1, 11 in Phase 2, 33 in Phase 4, 5 in Phase 5), against 290 days of tracker effort for the 36 tracker tasks covered (241 days for the 28 tasks whose Area is Frontend foundation, i18n/RTL or Design & prototype); the difference is mainly the persona shells and patient-web shell (37 days, no tracker task yet), split stories for the BFF and CSP, and realistic sizing of the component library.
open_questions: Belongs to ACC (Patient Access): T-127 family on phone lookup, T-128 duplicate-merge UI, T-142 keyboard-driven registration/check-in (built on FEF's command palette and shortcut framework, FEF-034), T-148 lobby token display (uses FEF live-board primitives in FEF-023 and the shared SSE client FEF-020), T-149 board move/reassign, T-175 exceptions inbox and T-025 'Mark reminded' relabel. They are tagged Team=Frontend in the tracker but their Area is Front desk/WhatsApp; please confirm ACC owns them so they are not dropped.

Belongs to the owner/reporting domain: T-196 owner ops dashboard (uses FEF chart kit FEF-026). Belongs to Platform & Trust: T-239 audit screen and T-357 delegations/guardian reviews/tenant lifecycle UI (Frontend-team tasks with Area Audit & privacy / Owner admin).

Shared with QA & CI: T-067 and T-160 are referenced by FEF-049/FEF-050/FEF-051 because the brief puts Playwright J1-J15 and visual regression in FEF scope; QA keeps the pipeline stage, preview envs (T-065) and the release safety report. T-326 (front-end performance budget gate) is left to QA & CI; FEF stories carry their own LCP/bundle NFRs.

Taken into FEF although the Area is elsewhere: T-016 (Caching & real-time), T-032 and T-117 (Billing & Tax), T-095 (Caching & real-time, backend T-094 is ACC), T-144 (Billing & Tax) and T-318 (Front desk; help and tours live in every persona shell). Money & Pharmacy and ACC to confirm, or move them back.

The persona-shell epic FEF-E12 and the patient-web shell have no tracker tasks (37 days without a T- reference). Propose adding tracker tasks for: shell framework, reception, doctor, nurse, solo, billing/pharmacy/lab, owner, hospital shells and the patient-web shell.

Hosting decision needed: ADR-06 says the BFF must run in-region because PHI passes through it, but staff-web is on Vercel today. Is the whole staff-web moving into the regional stack (FEF-009 assumes yes for /api/* and authenticated HTML), and who provisions it (Data & Infra)?

Staff UI languages for the India pilot: T-154 only requires extraction. FEF assumes English + Hindi staff catalogues for Login/Arrivals/Consult/Checkout; Kannada and Telugu staff UI only if pilot clinics ask. Confirm with the founder (B-79).

Encrypted consult drafts (FEF-005/FEF-035) use a per-session in-memory key, so drafts cannot be recovered after the browser is fully closed. Accept this trade-off in the DPIA, or allow a BFF-wrapped key that survives restarts for the same signed-in user?
Default theme: T-313 says follow prefers-color-scheme with a per-user override. Should the default for staff instead stay Dark (brand 'dark-first') with Light opt-in? Design works either way.

Digit style for Arabic UI (Latin vs Arabic-Indic) is a clinic setting per ADR-11; what is the default for KSA, UAE and Qatar clinics? FEF keeps clinical values (vitals, doses) in Latin digits regardless.

Invoice PDF rendering: FEF plans react-pdf in the in-region BFF; Money & Pharmacy may prefer Core-side rendering (headless browser in the worker) so WhatsApp/secure-link PDFs can be produced without a staff session. Decide before S6.

Small Core changes inside FEF stories need an owner: /v1/me/preferences + staff_preferences (core/iam), /v1/me/push-subscriptions + web_push_subscriptions and the push sender (core/realtime), and the invoice document endpoint (core/billing). FEF can write them with Platform & Trust / Money & Pharmacy review, or hand them over.
Native-speaking clinician reviewers for Hindi, Kannada and Telugu (and Arabic in Phase 4) must be contracted before S7, otherwise clinical catalogue keys block release (T-190 AC).

The ~170 backend endpoints missing from api/openapi.yaml block full codegen (FEF-014). QA's T-089 makes the spec authoritative, but each owning squad must document its endpoints; FEF keeps a temporary augmentation file until then.

epics.title: Phase 0 session safety and stabilisation
epics.goal: Staff never get logged out mid-task, sessions cannot be stolen by script, and the framework has no known critical CVEs before the first real patient record.

epics.title: Monorepo and shared packages
epics.goal: The frontend becomes a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo with shared api-client, domain, ui, tokens, i18n and config packages so staff-web, patient-web and the later Expo app share one typed foundation.

epics.title: Data layer: generated client and TanStack Query everywhere
epics.goal: Every screen reads and writes through packages/api-client and TanStack Query, so caching, cancellation and errors behave the same everywhere and the 60 effect workarounds disappear.

epics.title: Real-time staff screens over SSE
epics.goal: Every desk, nurse station and doctor sees the same queue within 2 seconds without polling, through one shared server-sent-events connection per browser.

epics.title: Design system, theming and accessibility
epics.goal: The prototype's design language (nb.css tokens, components, light and dark themes, charts) becomes a tested, accessible package that every app uses.

epics.title: Feature architecture: route groups and no more god components
epics.goal: Pages are thin, features live in their own folders with hooks and reducers, and a render error never blanks a doctor's screen.

epics.title: Fast, safe forms: validation, keyboard and autosave
epics.goal: Desk and consult forms are schema-validated, keyboard-first and never lose work, so walk-ins take under 45 s and nothing typed is lost on a shared PC.

epics.title: Languages, scripts and RTL
epics.goal: Staff UI is extraction-complete and patients read every message in Hindi, Kannada, Telugu (then more Indian languages and Arabic RTL), with clinic-correct dates, money and calendars.

epics.title: Print and documents
epics.goal: Every printed or shared document (token slip, Rx, invoice, receipt) has a tested layout for A4, A5 and 80 mm thermal paper and can be shared as a PDF by secure link.

epics.title: Installable staff app and push
epics.goal: Staff install Nabd on tablets and phones like an app, and doctors get a 'patient ready' push within 5 seconds, without ever caching PHI on the device.

epics.title: End-to-end journeys, accessibility and visual regression
epics.goal: Every core journey J1-J15 is automated in a real browser with time targets, role sweeps, axe and visual baselines per language, theme and device.

epics.title: Persona app shells: porting the prototype into staff-web and patient-web
epics.goal: Each persona gets the prototype's navigation, landing page and responsive shell in the real app, so feature squads port their screens into a consistent frame.

epics.title: Prototype as the living spec
epics.goal: The clickable prototype shows every option of the end product, consistent with the FRD, in both themes, three languages and every device width.

domains.name: Billing, tax, packages & insurance
domains.summary: FIN makes every bill correct, collectable and compliant: atomic and idempotent payments, server-side pricing with reasoned discounts, gapless invoice series per GSTIN/VAT number, a tax engine that taxes after discount (GST now; UAE VAT, KSA nationality-aware VAT and ZATCA Fatoora, Qatar no-VAT via adapters), refunds and credit notes with maker-checker, payment links/QR/mandates with reconciled settlement, the money side of treatment packages and memberships, doctor payouts, and insurance from a Phase 1 claim pack to India TPA/NHCX, UAE DHPO/Shafafiya and KSA NPHIES via middleware partners, plus IPD running and discharge bills. 60 stories, 468 engineer-days in total, against 505 tracker effort-days for the 32 in-scope tasks (the gap is mainly the Malaffi half of T-295 and the bilingual-Rx half of T-270, which belong to other domains).
open_questions: DEC-27 (KSA timing: FRD says KSA at MVP, plan says Phase 5). FIN-048/049 (KSA VAT + simplified invoice with ZATCA QR) are sized to be pulled into Phase 1-2 as 'KSA lite' if the founder chooses option B or C; FIN-050/051 (Fatoora Phase 2) must precede any KSA tenant whose wave is notified (Wave 25: SAR 187,500+ by 1 Feb 2027).

DEC-31 (insurance depth). All claims stories (FIN-037..044, FIN-053..057) are designed as adapters on a middleware partner ('buy, not build'). Which partner per market (India NHCX/TPA, UAE DHPO/Shafafiya, KSA NPHIES)? Estimates assume a partner API; building direct rails would roughly double FIN-040..044 and FIN-053..055.

DEC-43 (doctor referral fees vs fee-splitting ethics). FIN-033 ships revenue share for visiting consultants; FIN-034 keeps referral fees behind a per-market compliance flag, default off in India and KSA. Confirm option A and which markets counsel clears.
CEO-07 / RSK-03: written GST opinion on splitting mixed package bundles at list-price ratio is a release gate for FIN-025 in India. Who commissions it and by when?
CEO-08: KSA VAT point on package sales (full VAT at sale vs per session/instalment). FIN-026 stores tax_point to support both; needs a ZATCA adviser ruling before KSA instalments ship.

CEO-06 vs scope: FRD says no IRP e-invoicing for Indian clinics (below INR 5 Cr); the domain scope lists 'e-invoice IRP for B2B'. FIN-011 builds the IRP adapter dark behind a flag (P2). Confirm whether any target tenant (nursing homes, corporate B2B) needs it, or drop the adapter part.
QA-13: tax-advisor confirmation that an invoice-level discount is allocated pro rata across lines (including exempt lines) before tax. FIN-008 makes the allocation strategy pluggable.

Refund approval rights: RBAC matrix says receptionist Refund/Discount = N, FRD BIL-08 says owner approval only above a set amount. FIN-013 implements maker-checker always plus owner-only above threshold; confirm whether a billing-desk role may approve small refunds.

UAE payment gateway not chosen (FRD SYS-08 names only Razorpay for India and Tap or HyperPay for KSA). Pick one for UAE (Network International, Checkout.com, Tap) before FIN-024 is extended to the UAE.

UPI AutoPay limits: RBI e-mandate debits above the no-additional-authentication limit need patient authentication each time; FIN-027 falls back to payment links for those instalments. Confirm acceptable UX for high-value packages.
Chartered accountant (India), UAE tax adviser and ZATCA adviser engagements are needed to sign golden packs (FIN-010, FIN-045, FIN-048). Budget and owners?

Region model: tenants.region allows only IN/KSA and currency is derived from it in CheckoutService.currencyFor and DayCloseService. AED/QAR need the regions reference model (T-109, DEC-25) before FIN-006 can set currency correctly for GCC tenants.
Qatar: no tracker task exists. FIN-045 covers only the Qatar invoice/no-VAT variant; insurer claim formats in Qatar are unverified (doc01). Confirm whether Qatar is in the roadmap at all.

Belongs to other domains (referenced as dependencies by tracker id because their story ids are not known here): T-031 Idempotency-Key filter (platform), T-043 api-client (frontend foundation), T-179 secure links (consent & identity), T-297/T-256 caregiver model, T-314 tenant integration secrets, T-109 regions model, T-321 coded reason list, T-051 MFA step-up, T-224/T-234 code sets and FHIR mapping, T-287 IPD admissions (hospital), T-272/T-290 UAE/KSA cells, T-268 Arabic RTL.

Billing-adjacent tracker tasks outside the 'Billing & Tax'/'Insurance' areas that FIN assumes other domains own: T-346 buy package in WhatsApp and T-304 package cards (WhatsApp/engagement), T-324 package reports and T-244 revenue/payer-mix reports (owner reporting), T-191 owner daily summary, T-192 Rx QR to pre-filled bill and T-210 offline billing (pharmacy), T-056 Rx-only OTC gate for QA-14 (pharmacy), T-198 queue-billing-packages SQL cycle (platform). T-373 belongs to the KSA/GCC domain; FIN-024 covers only its Mada/STC Pay part. T-295's Malaffi feed belongs to interoperability; FIN-057 covers Shafafiya only. T-270's bilingual Rx belongs to clinical/e-Rx; FIN-045 covers invoices.

FRD conflict on insurance and hospital scope: FRD removed BIL-01..04 (eligibility/pre-auth workspace, claims board, denial management) and hospital modules; the tracker keeps T-274/275/276/292 and T-289. FIN-039..044, FIN-053..057 and FIN-058..060 follow the tracker and are Phase 4-5; they should be re-confirmed when DEC-28, DEC-15 and DEC-31 are decided.
Migration numbers are written as V1xx__name.sql; final numbers must be assigned at merge to avoid clashes with other domains (highest existing is V85).

epics.title: Money integrity fixes before real patients
epics.goal: Every rupee or riyal recorded at the desk is counted exactly once, priced by the server and cannot be bypassed or double-refunded.

epics.title: Invoice numbering, currency and money formatting
epics.goal: Invoices carry legally valid, gapless numbers per tax registration and financial year, and every amount has an explicit currency.

epics.title: Tax engine (GST now, VAT and ZATCA via adapters)
epics.goal: Every line is taxed correctly after discount, per market, and the result is proven by a signed golden-file pack.

epics.title: Invoices, receipts, refunds, credit notes and dues
epics.goal: Every bill produces a compliant printable invoice, mistakes are reversible with approval, and money owed is chased in under a minute per patient.

epics.title: Price master and discount control (FRD Clinical Charges Configuration)
epics.goal: The right price applies automatically for each doctor, visit type and urgency, and every discount is reasoned, approved above a threshold and visible to the owner.

epics.title: Payment gateway: links, QR, refunds, deposits and settlement
epics.goal: Patients and caregivers pay by UPI, card, mada or Apple Pay from WhatsApp or the desk, and every gateway rupee or riyal reconciles to the clinic's books.

epics.title: Treatment packages, estimates and memberships: the money features
epics.goal: Packages are taxed per component, can be paid in instalments or per session, moved, upgraded and refunded fairly, and memberships renew themselves.

epics.title: Doctor payouts, revenue share and referral tracking
epics.goal: Visiting consultants are paid an agreed share every month from real collections, and referral fees stay off until counsel approves them per market.

epics.title: Insurance: claim pack, shared insurance model and India cashless
epics.goal: Any insured patient leaves with a reimbursement-ready pack in seconds, and Indian nursing homes and polyclinics run cashless pre-auth and claims through a certified middleware partner.

epics.title: UAE: insurance at booking, DHPO claims, remittance, VAT and Peppol e-invoicing
epics.goal: Insured UAE patients spend zero minutes on insurance at the counter, clean claims go to DHPO the same day, and B2B invoices meet the 2027 Peppol mandate.

epics.title: KSA: nationality-aware VAT, ZATCA Fatoora and NPHIES
epics.goal: Every KSA invoice is VAT-correct by patient nationality and cleared or reported to ZATCA, and insured patients flow through NPHIES.

epics.title: Abu Dhabi: Shafafiya claims
epics.goal: Abu Dhabi clinics submit claims and pre-authorisations to Shafafiya on the same claim model as Dubai.

epics.title: Inpatient billing: running bill, interim bills and a fast discharge bill
epics.goal: Hospital and nursing-home stays accrue charges automatically so discharge never waits for billing.

domains.name: Hospital (inpatient, emergency, imaging, hospital services)
domains.summary: HOS delivers the hospital edition of Nabd: inpatient admissions and a live bed board, NEWS2/PEWS escalation, barcode MAR, operating theatres with the WHO checklist, discharge with a signed summary, the emergency department (ESI triage, live board, stroke/STEMI/sepsis clocks, medico-legal register), ambulance dispatch, radiology with DICOM MWL/PACS and structured reporting (incl. India PCPNDT), blood bank with two-person checks and haemovigilance, CSSD recall, dietary, central stores, medical records with birth/death registers, and duty rosters. All of it is Phase 5 and sits behind DEC-15 (build or partner): every module can run off, native, or in partner mode through one HL7 v2/FHIR/DICOM interface seam (HOS-002, HOS-003, HOS-031), so the month-12 decision does not waste the work. Total estimate 309 engineer-days across 55 stories vs 226 days of tracker effort for the 13 in-scope tasks (1.37x); the difference is the prototype scope that the tracker one-liners do not price (NEWS2/PEWS, barcode MAR, ER pathways, pre-arrival, DICOM gateway, PCPNDT, haemovigilance, CSSD recall, three-way match, ROI checks). If DEC-15 = partner for a module, drop its native stories and keep the seam.
open_questions: DEC-15 (build or partner, month 12): which modules go native vs partner? Recommendation in this spec: native IPD/OT/discharge/ER (EP41 core, NABH 3-hospital exit), partner-first for PACS image storage (HOS-031 gateway only) and optionally blood bank; HOS-002/HOS-003 make either answer cheap.

Inpatient encounter model: this spec reuses queue_entries (class='inpatient'/'emergency', V43 placeholder) as the encounter segment so clinical_notes/prescriptions/invoices FKs keep working. If the clinical/core domain splits ENCOUNTER from queue_entries first, admissions.encounter_id and er_visits.encounter_id should point there. Needs an owner decision before HOS-005/HOS-020.

T-289 (interim and consolidated IPD discharge bill, Area 'Billing & Tax') belongs to the billing domain; HOS-008 provides charge capture and HOS-018 consumes billing.discharge_bill.cleared.v1. Confirm the event contract with the billing PSE.

T-327 (complete prototype screens for hospital modules, Area 'Design & prototype') belongs to the design/frontend-foundation domain; HOS stories link to the existing ward/er/radiology/hospops screens.

T-214 (pharmacy purchase orders, GRN, suppliers) belongs to the pharmacy domain; HOS-044/HOS-046 assume one shared stock ledger and procurement model. Agree the schema with the pharmacy PSE before either is built.
T-247 (unified doctor calendar, 'busy' across facilities) belongs to the booking/identity domain; HOS-014 needs a read API (staff busy blocks) and to publish OT bookings into it.

Other cross-domain dependencies used here: T-002 break-glass (auth), T-179 secure links and T-250 Exchange custodian (consent & identity), T-206 Cedar PEP, T-224 ICD-10 search and T-303 consent capture (clinical), T-218 lab orders (lab), T-234 FHIR layer, T-237 DSR legal hold, T-094/T-095 SSE, T-123 entitlements, T-143 uploads, T-144 print, T-282 chain OLAP dashboard.
Flyway numbering: this spec uses V601-V660 for HOS migrations. Please confirm a reserved range per domain to avoid collisions.

Clinical content sign-off: NEWS2/PEWS tables, ESI/CTAS/MTS logic, pathway targets, cross-match rules and transfusion checks need the Clinical Safety Officer (T-021) and hazard-log entries before go-live. Who signs for each market?
Triage scale licensing: CTAS and MTS may need licences; ESI v4 is free. Which scales must be offered in India, UAE, KSA and Qatar?

Statutory forms (MLC, PCPNDT Form F, CRS birth/death, MCCD, HvPI, e-RaktKosh, GCC civil registration) differ by state and authority. Need counsel-confirmed form fields and whether any registry offers an API (else export/upload).

Bundled Orthanc PACS (HOS-031): if Nabd stores images, who owns image retention (UAE 25 years), storage cost and residency? Recommendation: gateway + customer/partner PACS by default; bundled Orthanc only for small nursing homes on a priced add-on.
Hardware: DEC-38 bans kiosks in clinics; confirm barcode scanners, wristband and label printers, and the on-premises DICOM gateway box are allowed in the hospital edition and who supplies them.
Roster labour rules (rest hours, max continuous hours, nurse ratios) per market and per facility: provide defaults for India and GCC, or make every facility configure them at onboarding?
Ambulance GPS: use the crew phone PWA location, a vehicle telematics partner, or manual status only for v1?

epics.title: Hospital setup and build-or-partner integration seam
epics.goal: A facility can switch on hospital modules, describe its wards and beds, and run each module natively or through a partner HIS/RIS/PACS without changing staff screens.

epics.title: Admissions, bed board and transfers (ADT)
epics.goal: Every inpatient is admitted, moved and tracked on one live bed board that updates in under 2 seconds.

epics.title: Inpatient nursing, early warning and medication safety
epics.goal: Ward nurses record observations and doses at the bedside, NEWS2/PEWS escalates deterioration automatically, and every dose is scanned against the order.

epics.title: Operating theatres
epics.goal: Theatre lists are booked against surgeons' unified calendars with zero double-booking, and every case passes consent and the WHO checklist.

epics.title: Discharge
epics.goal: Discharge runs against a visible checklist with blockers and a clock, and ends with a signed summary the patient receives in their language.

epics.title: Emergency department
epics.goal: ER patients are registered in seconds, triaged within 10 minutes on a standard scale, tracked on a live board with door-to-doctor time, and time-critical pathways run on the clock.

epics.title: Ambulance requests, dispatch and pre-arrival
epics.goal: Ambulance calls are taken, dispatched and tracked to hand-over, and the ER knows what is coming before it arrives.

epics.title: Radiology: orders, scheduling, PACS and reporting
epics.goal: Imaging is ordered safely, scheduled on modalities, acquired through DICOM worklists, reported in structured templates and critical findings are read back within minutes.

epics.title: Blood bank
epics.goal: Donors, components, cross-match and issue are tracked end to end with a two-person check and haemovigilance, and stock never expires unseen.

epics.title: CSSD sterilisation tracking
epics.goal: Every instrument set is traceable through decontamination, packing, sterilisation and issue, and a failed load can be recalled to the patients it touched.

epics.title: Dietary and kitchen
epics.goal: Diet orders flow from the ward to an allergy-aware kitchen list for every meal.

epics.title: Central stores and procurement
epics.goal: Non-pharmacy items are stocked across central and sub-stores, indented by departments, procured with a three-way match and charged to patients or cost centres.

epics.title: Medical records department and statutory registers
epics.goal: Charts are completed and coded, records are released only with consent or legal authority, and births and deaths are registered on time.

epics.title: Duty roster, leave and attendance
epics.goal: Wards and departments have a weekly roster that respects skill mix and rest rules, with leave and swaps handled in the app and attendance feeding payroll export.

epics.title: Hospital operations overview
epics.goal: The owner sees bed occupancy, ER flow, theatre use and discharge times for each hospital every morning.

domains.name: Identity, consent & data exchange
domains.summary: IDC delivers Nabd's trust layer for patients and clinicians: Phase 0 PHI read gates, tenant processing consent with versioned per-facility notices, the caregiver/guardian model, OTP secure links, ABDM M1-M3, data-subject rights with retention and legal hold, the Cedar policy engine for intra-hospital access and break-glass, and in Phase 3 the global Person/Practitioner identity plane with one-login facility switching and consented, time-boxed cross-facility sharing through the Exchange (never by widening RLS). It retires brand-wide data visibility and extends to NABIDH/Malaffi and a chain MPI in Phases 4-5. 64 stories total 498 engineer-days against 522 tracker days for the 32 tasks in scope (422 days for the 25 Consent & Identity tasks plus 100 for 7 claimed tasks from other areas; T-295 is claimed only for Malaffi, so the comparable figure is about 500).
open_questions: Legal (doc 07 App. B 1): is the founder's 'treating doctor must also approve' rule lawful when the PATIENT asks for a facility-to-facility transfer in each country? IDC-043 treats it as a release review with SLA and escalation, never an indefinite block; the patient's own export (IDC-021) is never doctor-gated.
Legal (App. B 2): age threshold and categories for adolescent confidential approvals per country (IDC-036 stores them in a per-market rules table so either answer works).
Legal (App. B 3): does NHA accept a HIP-side clinical review step within ABDM response times? If not, IDC-058 falls back to auto-release with post-hoc review for ABDM requests only.
Legal (App. B 4): is notice + opt-out enough for the chain demographics directory (IDC-054), or does any country need opt-in?
Legal (App. B 5): who is controller of the patient access-history view (IDC-047): Nabd as platform or each facility? Affects the notice wording and DSR routing.
Malaffi: confirm the current DoH consent standard (no published opt-out) before IDC-062; NABIDH opt-out handling is designed in IDC-061.

DPO / founder: emergency treatment for a patient who declines processing consent (IDC-006) needs a statutory basis per market; confirm wording. Also confirm the purpose list (processing, messaging, marketing, guardian_access, optional 'bought_where' per CEO-25).

Retention: FRD DPO-05A forbids clinic-authored retention, but the prototype's owner.privacy shows editable retention (T-327 already flags it as a contradiction). IDC-024 ships platform-owned market defaults only; KSA and Qatar periods are pending counsel.

DEC-33 (ABDM earlier than FRD, ABHA opt-in and off by default) is assumed in IDC-016..020, IDC-057..059. DEC-40 (custodian model on regional cloud) is assumed in IDC-044. DEC-41 keeps the patient app in Phase 3, so all patient surfaces here are patient-web and WhatsApp.

Sequencing: multi-branch lite (T-332, Phase 2) promises 'one patient identity across branches' and 'one login', but Person/Practitioner (IDC-032..039) are Phase 3. Either pull IDC-032/033/039 into Phase 2 for multi-branch tenants, or let T-332 use same-owner pending-workspace login and the chain directory (IDC-054) behind a flag. Needs a founder/CTO decision.
If the Cedar spike (IDC-026) is no-go on any regional base image, IDC-027 onward uses a hand-written Java PDP behind the same interface; ADR-08 would need an addendum.

Ownership boundaries (claimed here): T-133 (brand widening removal), T-237 (DSR engine), T-238 (retention and legal hold, patient-data part), T-334 (per-facility notice and grievance contact only; the health card is ADM-033), T-256 (caregiver roles, built as global relationships in IDC-036), T-357 (only the guardian age-18 review UI part, in IDC-012; ADM-019/ADM-020 cover delegations and tenant lifecycle), T-295 (only the Malaffi part, in IDC-062).

Belongs to PLT: T-010 (Sprint 0 brand-visibility containment, CONS M1; IDC-053 depends on it), T-002/T-003/T-204 (break-glass gate, delegation, device label; IDC-030 and IDC-050 build v2 on top), T-048 (phi_read_log; IDC-027 and IDC-047 write and read it), T-001 (token typ/aud; IDC-039 needs it), T-011/T-041 (roles and RLS).

Belongs to the WhatsApp/comms domain: T-103 (STOP into consent withdrawal; IDC-006 consumes it), T-331 (WhatsApp 'My records and privacy' menu; it calls the IDC-021..023 and IDC-047 APIs), T-165/T-166 (dependants picker, chat registration; IDC-005/009/010 extend them).

Belongs to front desk/patient access (ACC): T-128 (in-tenant duplicate merge UI; IDC-035 hooks tenant merges into person_links), T-279 (Emirates ID read) and T-294 (Iqama capture), which feed the L2 adapters in IDC-034.

Belongs to other domains: the Shafafiya half of T-295 (insurance/BIL), the delegations and tenant-lifecycle parts of T-357 (owner admin/PLT), T-373 (KSA PDPL pack, infra/residency; IDC-003 and IDC-024 provide Arabic notice and KSA retention hooks), T-257 (Expo patient app), T-316 (signed DPA, owner admin), T-303/T-299 (procedure and photo consent, clinical/specialty), T-332 (multi-branch lite, organisation).

T-179 (OTP secure links) is in the Consent & Identity area and is covered by IDC-015, but its patient-web app skeleton is shared with the frontend foundation owner. Agree who scaffolds apps/patient-web.

The tenants.region (AE/QA) and tenants.health_authority columns that the NABIDH/Malaffi connectors need are owned by the region model work (PLT/infra). The global login router hash(identifier) → region is in control-plane. IDC-039 and IDC-060..062 depend on both.

epics.title: Phase 0 PHI read gates on clinical reads
epics.goal: Every /v1/clinical/** read honours consent withdrawal, patient verification, own-patients scope and field grants before any real patient data arrives.

epics.title: Tenant processing consent and privacy notices (EP08)
epics.goal: Every patient gets an itemised, versioned privacy notice and separate consents from the first visit, captured in under 20 seconds, with processing default-deny.

epics.title: Caregiver and guardian model (tenant side)
epics.goal: Families are managed from one WhatsApp number with explicit adult consent, acted-by audit, age-18 handover and instant revocation.

epics.title: Secure document links
epics.goal: Nothing clinical sits in a chat body: Rx, invoices and reports open through OTP-protected, expiring, access-logged links.

epics.title: ABDM M1: ABHA at the desk and Scan & Share
epics.goal: Indian patients can create or verify ABHA at registration and check in by Scan & Share, never mandatory, Aadhaar never stored; M1 submitted in Phase 1 and certified in Phase 2.

epics.title: Data-subject rights, retention and per-facility notices (EP31)
epics.goal: Patients can export, correct and erase their data within statutory timers, with sectoral retention and legal hold respected, and each facility publishes its own notice and grievance contact before DPDP applies (May 2027).

epics.title: One policy decision point and intra-hospital access policy
epics.goal: Cedar becomes the single PDP: every clinical read is decided by versioned policy, hospitals set cross-department and sensitive-category rules, and break-glass is a reviewed, one-patient context flag.

epics.title: Global patient identity (Person) per region
epics.goal: Each region has one Person per human patient, linked to facility records through pairwise references, verified by OTP (L1) or national ID rails (L2), with safe exact-match merges.

epics.title: Global practitioner identity and one login

domains.name: Data, events, infrastructure & quality
domains.summary: OPS delivers the data, eventing, infrastructure and quality backbone every other domain stands on: indexed and RLS-forced Postgres with zero-downtime migrations, read models for the registry and owner reports, the transactional outbox relayed to Valkey Streams as PHI-free CloudEvents, Caffeine/Valkey caching with a PHI default-deny rule, SSE transport from core.realtime, OpenTelemetry/Prometheus/Grafana with SLO burn alerts and PHI-redacted logs, the CI pipeline and test suites (token misuse, concurrency, RBAC, tenant fuzzing, chaos, k6) with previews and release safety reports, phase gates, and per-country cells (India first, then UAE, KSA, Qatar) with backups, DR, KMS and egress proofs. It matters because the Phase 0 gate (no real patient data before it) and every Phase 1 'moment that matters' (live queue < 2 s, check-in < 300 ms, no duplicate WhatsApp) depend on it. 69 stories, 491.5 engineer-days. Tracker effort for the 72 in-scope tasks is 482 days; OPS covers 70 of them plus 7 Data & Infra / QA & CI squad tasks from other areas (501 tracker days), and cedes T-016 and T-095 (11 days) to FEF. The estimate is within about 2% of that: the 25-day items (T-094, T-096, T-255, T-272, T-290) were split into buildable stories, Playwright journeys and the WhatsApp provider stub are left to FEF and COM, and a 4-day Qatar readiness story with no tracker task was added.
open_questions: Belongs to FEF: T-016 (pause polling in hidden tabs, Caching & real-time area, Frontend team) is covered by FEF-004 and T-095 (shared SSE client patching TanStack Query) by FEF-020, so OPS dropped its duplicate stories; the OPS SSE transport and batch-read stories (T-094) are the backend half FEF-020 depends on.

Shared with FEF: T-067 and T-160 are QA & CI-owned, but FEF-049/FEF-050 write the Playwright harness and journeys J1-J15. OPS keeps the preview stage 7 gate (in the preview-environment story), the nightly stage 8 journey gate, the role-absence sweep, the hazard log as code and the per-release safety test report. Please confirm FEF-050's device projects satisfy the T-160 device-matrix note so OPS does not duplicate them.

Shared with COM: T-135 (WhatsApp chaos suite) uses COM-010's provider stub and virtual-patient driver; OPS owns the chaos scenarios, assertions and nightly gate. T-373 (Infrastructure & residency area, 25 d) is mostly KSA product scope: prayer-window/Friday-aware sends are in COM-024; Mada/Apple Pay/STC Pay via Tap/HyperPay belongs to the Money domain (FIN); the gender-of-doctor default belongs to Patient Access booking (ACC); the SDAIA registration wizard/RoPA export belongs to IDC. OPS covers only the NCNICC/PDPL infrastructure evidence, pen test and SDAIA infra appendix in the Saudi assurance story. Please confirm FIN, ACC and IDC pick up their parts.

Tenancy-area tasks T-011 (role split + FORCE RLS), T-041 (RLS on remaining tables) and T-132 (composite tenant FKs) are owned by the Data & Infra squad, so OPS covers them. T-010 (indexable array policy) and T-076 (tenant bound at transaction begin) are not covered by any domain spec seen so far (Core Backend / Platform & Trust); OPS lists them as dependencies only. Please assign them.

Audit-area tasks T-156 and T-209 (partitioning) are covered by OPS. T-053 (audit chain-head rebuild) and T-048 (partitioned phi_read_log) are dependencies and are not yet covered by any domain spec seen (Platform & Trust / Core Backend). OPS owns the chain performance verification, monthly seals and the optional async sealer.

Clinical-area tasks T-021 (appoint the CSO, hazard log v0) and T-072 (signed hazard log v1, safety test report) are QA & CI-owned; OPS covers the hazard-log-as-code and release safety report tooling. The CSO hire is a founder action (DEC-14) and the clinical content of the hazard log belongs to the Clinical domain with the CSO.

T-094 (25 d, Patient Access team) is split: OPS owns the SSE transport (core.realtime), the /queue/board and batch-read endpoints and the event-to-screen probe; the queue/ETA producers and ETA values on the board belong to ACC (T-105, T-141). Please confirm ACC does not also plan the SSE transport.
T-109 (regions reference model) and T-314 (secrets separation) are Platform & Trust-team tasks in the Infrastructure & residency area and are covered by OPS; confirm IDC/PLT do not also plan them.

DEC-04 (hosting: leave Render/Vercel; provider for IN now, AE/SA shortlist by month 8) and DEC-21 (managed container platform vs Kubernetes) are open and due 27 Nov / 14 Dec 2026. The cell module isolates provider-specific code so either answer works, but prod-in (S4) cannot start without DEC-04.

Retention periods per jurisdiction (audit_log online months and archive years, whatsapp_messages 24 months, sessions 30 days, login_attempts 90 days, phi_read_log 13 months) need DPO/counsel confirmation (DEC-22, T-238 in IDC-024, T-273) before any archive or purge job deletes data.
Qatar has no tracker task; OPS added a small readiness story (provider shortlist, plan-only cell). Should Qatar get a full cell task with a phase, or stay 'when sold' per ADR-09?

epics.title: Database performance, tenancy enforcement and migration safety

epics.title: Caching tiers (Caffeine L1 + Valkey L2) with a PHI default-deny policy

domains.name: Pharmacy & laboratory
domains.summary: Pharmacy and lab for Nabd, built as two core modules (`pharmacy`, `lab`) that run inside a clinic or hospital and are also sold as standalone editions (facility type + entitlement on the same Core, not separate services). Pharmacy closes the P0 safety hole first (prescription-only items sold over the counter, QA-14), then makes the module the single writer of stock, adds batches/FEFO/expiry, e-Rx dispense in under 20 s, partial dispense and substitution, statutory registers (H1/X, NDPS and GCC controlled drugs), purchasing with GRN and payables, reports, refills, the standalone edition with offline billing, and KSA Wasfaty/SFDA RSD. Lab adds a catalogue, digital orders from the consult (< 10 s), barcoded samples (< 60 s), results with ranges and delta checks, pathologist validation, critical-value escalation (ack < 15 min), secure report release, HIE sharing, HL7/ASTM analysers, Westgard QC, outsourcing and a lab-only edition. 58 stories, 387 engineer-days, against 265 tracker days for the 17 in-scope tasks; the difference is scope the brief adds that has no tracker task (pharmacist verification, substitution, NDPS/GCC registers, payables, network e-Rx, QC, outsourcing, HIE release, lab catalogue/ranges/validation as separate deliverables). All in-house pharmacy and lab features sit behind mode and entitlement gates so founder decisions DEC-32 (pharmacy sequencing) and DEC-30 (lab persona) change release flags, not code.
open_questions: DEC-32 (due 25 Jan 2027): the FRD rules External = MVP, Hybrid = Phase 2, In-house (batches, FEFO, registers, dispense queue) = Phase 3, while tracker tasks T-163/T-192/T-193/T-194 sit in Phase 1 (S7-S8). Specs keep the tracker phases but every in-house feature is behind `pharmacy_settings.mode` + the plan entitlement (PHL-004). Founder must confirm before S7 whether in-house features ship to pilots in Phase 1 or stay dark until Phase 3.

DEC-30 (due 1 Feb 2027): the FRD removed the lab persona for small clinics (they attach outside reports, DOC-08). All lab stories are behind the `lab` entitlement; confirm whether clinics may buy the lab module or only standalone labs and hospitals.

FRD PHR-09 says stock 'cannot go negative without an override reason' (i.e. allows negative with override); V51 CHECK (qty_after >= 0) and QA forbid negative stock (QA found no negative-stock defect today). PHL-018 keeps qty >= 0 and records a stock_discrepancy instead. Product to confirm.

NDPS: FRD PHR-04 marks India NDPS narcotics out of scope, but the prototype shows an NDPS register and the brief asks for it. PHL-024 is P3/Phase 4; confirm whether NDPS-licensed standalone chemists are a target segment.

CEO-27 (H1 without a licensed pharmacist = warning, no block) is applied to hybrid clinics. Confirm it also applies to standalone pharmacies (which must legally have a registered pharmacist) or whether the edition should require a pharmacist in charge at setup (PHL-032 currently requires one).

ASM-02 bans barcode scanners and other hardware for clinics. Lab labels (PHL-045) print on the existing thermal printer and samples are found by typing or phone camera; keyboard-wedge scanners work without integration. Confirm the ban does not apply to standalone labs/pharmacies, and that the GS1 DataMatrix scanning required by SFDA RSD (PHL-040) is acceptable in KSA.

Analyser connectivity (PHL-052) needs an on-premise 'Nabd Lab Bridge' agent on the lab PC (outbound HTTPS only). Platform/infra to confirm this is an edge agent and not a fifth service under ADR-01, and who owns its signing, updates and support.

Lab result release policy (PHL-049): auto-release normal results to patients vs doctor-review-first vs N-hour timer, and which tests are 'sensitive' (never auto-released). Needs CSO sign-off per market.

Network e-Rx at a non-affiliated Nabd pharmacy (PHL-034) is a cross-tenant flow through the exchange; it depends on doc 07 exchange delivery and counsel sign-off on pharmacy-routing neutrality (T-178). Confirm phase (spec says Phase 2).

Indian pharmacy prices are MRP-inclusive of GST and capped at MRP (DPCO). PHL-021 needs the billing tax engine (T-122) to support inclusive back-calculation; confirm with the Billing & Tax domain. Also confirm the GST tax point for offline bills is the sale time (PHL-036).
Offline billing (PHL-035..038, T-210) depends on the T-197 spike and DEC-37; the approach (PWA vs desktop wrapper) may change these estimates.
Wasfaty and SFDA RSD (PHL-039/040) need vendor accreditation with NUPCO/MOH and SFDA; lead time unknown and outside engineering control.
Migration numbers are written as V1xx__<name>.sql; final numbers must be allocated centrally at merge to avoid collisions with other domains.
Cross-domain dependencies are written as tracker task ids (e.g. T-122, T-152, T-079) in depends_on because the other domains' story ids are not known yet; map them once all specs are merged.

Related tracker tasks that touch pharmacy/lab but belong to other domains (not covered here): T-216 stock at prescribing time, T-178 clinic-default pharmacy routing, T-349 two-section hybrid e-Rx, T-363 bought-where capture, T-151 Rx PDF/QR (all belong to the e-Rx/clinical domain; PHL exposes stock/in-house read APIs they consume); T-280 DHA e-Rx and dispense-time eligibility (belongs to the insurance/UAE domain); T-129 CSV import of drugs and stock (belongs to the owner-admin/onboarding domain; PHL-032 reuses it); T-197 offline-sync spike (belongs to the platform domain); T-222 multi-station lab-before-consult journeys (belongs to the queue/ETA domain); T-378 general stores (belongs to the hospital-services domain).
Home sample collection and phlebotomist routing (LB-06, Could) and pharmacy home delivery (PH-08, Could) are not specified; confirm they stay out of scope.

epics.title: Pharmacy safety gate and module foundations

epics.goal: Stock is tracked by batch and expiry, the earliest-expiring good batch is always picked first, expired stock can never be sold, and the monthly expiry check drops from 3 hours to under 15 minutes.

epics.title: e-Rx dispense: queue, verify, dispense, partial and substitution
epics.goal: A signed e-Rx reaches the pharmacy within 5 seconds and becomes a correct, FEFO-picked bill in under 20 seconds with no retyping.

epics.goal: A walk-in counter sale takes under 30 seconds with correct tax and FEFO batches, and prescription-only medicines are sold only against a recorded prescription.

epics.title: Statutory registers and controlled drugs
epics.goal: Every restricted-medicine dispense writes its statutory register entry automatically, and the register is inspection-ready in each market.

epics.title: Purchasing: suppliers, purchase orders, goods receipt and payables
epics.goal: Stock-outs fall because reorders are suggested from real usage, deliveries are received against orders with batches in under 2 minutes, and what the pharmacy owes each supplier is always known.

epics.title: Pharmacy reports and patient engagement
epics.goal: Owners see stock value, margins and attach-rate, and patients are told when refills are due and when medicines are ready.

epics.title: Standalone pharmacy edition and offline billing
epics.goal: A chemist with no clinic can sign up, set up and sell in under 30 minutes on the same core, accept Nabd e-Rx from any clinic, and keep billing through power and internet cuts without losing or duplicating a bill.

epics.title: KSA national pharmacy integrations
epics.goal: KSA pharmacies accept Wasfaty prescriptions and report every serialised dispense to SFDA RSD within a minute.

epics.title: Lab module foundations and test catalogue
epics.goal: A clinic or standalone lab can switch on the lab module and maintain its tests, panels, prices, sample requirements and reference ranges.

epics.title: Lab orders, worklist and samples
epics.goal: Doctors order tests digitally in under 10 seconds and every sample is labelled and tracked from collection to bench with no mix-ups.

epics.title: Results, validation, release and critical values
epics.goal: Results are entered with automatic flags, validated by a pathologist, released to the doctor and patient by secure link, and every critical value is acknowledged within 15 minutes.

epics.title: Analysers, quality control and outsourcing
epics.goal: Analyser results land without retyping, every run is checked against Westgard QC rules before release, and tests sent to partner labs are tracked end to end.

epics.title: Standalone lab edition
epics.goal: A diagnostic lab with no clinic can sign up, register walk-ins, bill, collect, report and serve referring doctors on Nabd within 30 minutes of setup.

domains.name: Platform & Trust: authentication, privilege, tenant isolation, audit, encryption, privacy operations and the Control Plane
domains.summary: PLT makes Nabd safe to hold real patient data and keeps it that way: a PIN alone can no longer reach a session, break-glass and delegation cannot escalate privileges, RLS is enforced by the database with a migrator/runtime role split, every PHI read is logged and the audit chain is verified nightly, field encryption moves to per-tenant regional keys, patients can exercise DPDP rights before 13 May 2027, and the operator Control Plane becomes its own PHI-free service before the second cell. 63 stories in 8 epics, 478 estimate days; the 59 in-scope tracker tasks (Auth, Tenancy, Platform, Audit & privacy) carry 437 tracker days, plus 36 days for three control-plane tasks filed under Owner admin (T-087, T-123, T-207), so 473 tracker days against 478 planned. Phase 0 (P0) is 19 stories / 102 days and must pass before any real patient data enters any environment (doc06 Sprint 2 gate).
open_questions: Duplicate coverage found against specs already in the workbench (resolve at merge using the tracker's Team/Owner column): (a) T-011, T-041, T-132, T-156 and T-209 are Team 'Data & Infra' and are also built by OPS-003, OPS-005, OPS-068 and OPS-069. Recommend OPS keeps the build, and PLT-017, PLT-020 and PLT-042 (24 days) are dropped or kept only as security acceptance and review items. (b) T-087, T-123, T-207, T-305, T-332 and T-334 are Team 'Platform & Trust' but are also built by ADM-001, ADM-017/018, ADM-022..027 and ADM-033..040. Recommend PLT keeps them (PLT-016, PLT-022..025, PLT-050, PLT-058, PLT-059, PLT-061..063) and ADM keeps only the owner-facing screens it adds on top (e.g. ADM-018, ADM-037). (c) T-133, T-237, T-238 and T-334 are Team 'Platform & Trust' but are also built by IDC-021..025 and IDC-053. Recommend PLT keeps the engines (PLT-021, PLT-047..050) and IDC keeps the patient-facing consent and notice flows that depend on them.

Ownership overlap: T-087 (provisioning CAS), T-123 (seat limits and entitlements) and T-207 (Control Plane extraction) are filed under Area 'Owner admin' but owned by Platform & Trust and are control-plane work, so PLT covers them in PLT-058, PLT-059 and PLT-061..063. If the domain covering Owner admin also lists them, agree one owner (recommend PLT).

Dependencies owned by other domains that PLT stories rely on: T-020 prod-config CI job and T-090 RBAC-matrix tests and T-100 id-replay fuzzer (QA & CI); T-063 BFF with httpOnly cookies and browser CSP (Frontend foundation); T-080 Valkey and T-096 prod-in cell and T-109 regions model (Infrastructure & residency); T-058 licence-based signing / is_clinician (Clinical); T-047 clinical read gates, T-104/T-137 notice and consent capture, T-179 secure links, T-246 Practitioner identity (Consent & Identity); T-357 owner UI for delegations and tenant lifecycle, T-311 offboarding export (uses crypto-shred from PLT-045), T-320 self-serve plan change (Owner admin).

Belongs to CON (Consent & Identity) or needs a joint decision: the brand directory in PLT-024 is the CONS §7 M2 'chain directory'; the brand-level login in PLT-023 is a stepping stone to the Practitioner one-login (T-246); the privacy_notices table in PLT-050 may already be modelled by T-104. Agree a single endpoint/table before Phase 2.
DEC-39: build SAML/OIDC SSO (PLT-010, PLT-011, 25 days) only if the founder confirms an enterprise tier; the old plan NFR-06 forbade SSO.

Second factor and secrets policy: FRD NFR-06/NB-040 wants passwordless, clinic-simple access (WhatsApp OTP or authenticator, owner chooses), while doc06 MF-09 asks for a passphrase for Owner/operator accounts. PLT-003/PLT-005 ship 6-8 digit PINs plus mandatory TOTP for privileged identities and keep a flag for the passphrase and for WhatsApp OTP as a second factor. Founder decision needed.

Break-glass eligibility: which preset roles get clinical:breakGlass by default (PLT-012 proposes Doctor, Owner-doctor and ER; not Nurse or Receptionist). Confirm with the CSO, especially for ER nurses in hospital tenants.

DPO confirmations: phi_read_log online retention of 13 months (doc06 D8), DSR statutory periods per market (PLT-047), retention floors per data class and market (PLT-049, PLT-055), and whether CERT-In 180-day log retention covers app logs as well as security logs.

Hosting and KMS provider (doc06 D2) and Control Plane location plus GCC owner-contact transfer rules (D3) gate PLT-002 (secret manager adapter), PLT-045 (KMS port) and PLT-061. Stories are written against ports so S0 is not blocked.

Module placement: the service catalogue has no 'privacy' module, so DSR, erasure and retention (PLT-047..049, PLT-055) are placed in core 'patient', and the file pipeline (PLT-029) in core 'shared'. Confirm, or allow a new 'privacy' module.

Migration numbering: current max is V85. PLT uses 'V1xx__<name>.sql' placeholders; with ten domains adding migrations in parallel, pick a convention (per-domain ranges or timestamp versions with flyway outOfOrder off) before S0.
CONS M0 result needed: are any brands set to BRAND or TENANT data_visibility_scope in a real environment? If yes, those owners need PLT-024 or the CONS M2 directory before PLT-021 removes widening.

T-202 asks to remove the 'DRAFT' header from the applied V7 migration; editing an applied migration changes its Flyway checksum. Confirm a 'flyway repair' in every environment (pilot DB is fresh per doc06 D9) or leave the file and document the note instead.
