stories.title: Check-in refuses an appointment dated another day, and doctor delays stay bounded to the clinic day
stories.story: As a receptionist I want check-in to refuse an appointment that is not for today and delay announcements to stay sane, so that I cannot put the wrong patient in today's queue or leave a stale delay running for days.
stories.context: QA-07: QueueService.checkIn only checks status, patient and doctor, so an appointment booked for next week can be checked in today and later marked completed. QA-23: DelayAnnounceRequest has @Min(1) but no @Max (100,000 minutes accepted), ScheduleRepository.findActiveDelay is just cleared_at IS NULL with no day bound, so yesterday's uncleared delay is still active today, and two concurrent announcements hit uq_doctor_delays_active and return 500. Fix: check-in compares the appointment's clinic date (ClinicClock, tenant timezone) with today's clinic date; delays get @Max(240) and a clinic_date so they lapse at the end of the clinic day; the unique-violation on concurrent announce maps to 409. This is the quick win #12 from doc 06 and is a prerequisite for ACC-003. Cross-midnight sessions are handled later by ACC-005; this story uses ClinicClock.today() as-is.
acceptance: Given a doctor, when staff POST /v1/doctors/{id}/delay with delayMinutes 241, then the API returns 400 Problem+JSON with a field error on delayMinutes (max 240) and no row is written
Given an appointment dated tomorrow in the clinic timezone (Asia/Kolkata), when reception checks it in today, then the API returns 409 type appointment-not-today and no queue_entries row is created

Given a delay announced yesterday and never cleared, when the arrivals board loads today, then no active delay is shown for that doctor and GET /v1/doctors/{id}/delay lists yesterday's delay as lapsed
Given two staff announce a delay for the same doctor at the same moment, then exactly one gets 201 and the other gets 409 delay-already-active (never 500)
Given a Dubai clinic (Asia/Dubai) at 23:50 local, when reception checks in an appointment for 23:55 local the same day, then check-in succeeds (UTC date differs, clinic date matches)

api.summary: Announce a doctor delay (existing endpoint, tightened validation)
api.auth: permission queue:edit; staff JWT (typ=access) via BFF; tenant-scoped
api.response: 201 { id, doctorId, delayMinutes, clinicDate, active: true }

api.summary: Check in a patient (existing endpoint, new date rule)
api.auth: permission queue:create; staff JWT (typ=access) via BFF; tenant-scoped
api.request: { patientId, doctorId, appointmentId?, source?, presentingComplaint?<=500, paymentMode? }

db.detail: ADD COLUMN clinic_date date; backfill clinic_date = (announced_at AT TIME ZONE tenants.timezone)::date; SET NOT NULL; ADD CHECK (delay_minutes BETWEEN 1 AND 240); DROP INDEX uq_doctor_delays_active; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_doctor_delays_active_day ON doctor_delays (tenant_id, doctor_id, clinic_date) WHERE cleared_at IS NULL

ui.notes: Show the 409 appointment-not-today as an inline message with the appointment's real date and a 'book as walk-in instead' action
Delay ladder limited to 15/30/45/60 plus custom up to 240 min

nfr: no change to check-in p95 (< 300 ms)
date comparison uses ClinicClock only; ClinicClockUsageTest stays green
audit row for each delay announce/clear
tests: integration: delay announced with clock at day D is inactive at D+1 (injected Clock)

stories.title: Queue moves are compare-and-set, so two screens can never push a visit through the wrong steps
stories.story: As a doctor I want each queue move to apply only if the visit is still where my screen thinks it is, so that a stale screen or a double tap never skips vitals or billing.
stories.context: MF-28 / QA-32: QueueService.updateStatus validates the transition against a row it read earlier, then QueueRepository.updateStatus writes 'UPDATE queue_entries SET status = ?' with no status guard, so two concurrent edits can both succeed and bypass the department workflow. PATCH can also move checkout_pending -> completed with only queue:edit, so billing never runs, and no_show is allowed from in_consult. Fix: the client sends the status it saw (expectedStatus); the repository writes 'WHERE tenant_id = ? AND id = ? AND status = :expected' and 0 rows -> 409 with the current status. 'completed' is removed from the PATCH path: only billing's checkout (VisitCommands.completeAfterPayment, called by CheckoutService) may complete a visit. no_show is legal only before in_consult. transfer() uses the same CAS. This unblocks reliable stage timestamps (ACC-015) and the ETA engine.
acceptance: Given two screens both showing a visit in 'waiting', when both send PATCH status vitals_pending with expectedStatus waiting at the same time, then exactly one gets 200 and the other gets 409 STALE_STATUS with currentStatus vitals_pending
Given a visit in checkout_pending, when anyone sends PATCH status completed, then the API returns 403 COMPLETION_RESERVED_FOR_BILLING and only a successful checkout moves it to completed
Given a visit in in_consult, when staff send PATCH status no_show, then the API returns 400 ILLEGAL_TRANSITION
Given a stale screen gets 409, then staff-web refetches the entry and shows 'Already moved to <stage> by <name>' within 1 s, without a full page reload
Given 50 concurrent transitions on one doctor's queue, then p95 of the CAS write is < 200 ms and no entry skips a configured step (assert against resolveStatusSequence)

stories.title: An appointment can be checked in only once and then shows 'arrived'
stories.story: As a receptionist I want the system to refuse a second check-in of the same appointment and mark it 'arrived', so that one patient never gets two tokens and an appointment cannot be cancelled while the patient is in the consult room.
stories.context: QA-06 (S2, clinical safety): the same appointment can be checked in twice, including by two receptionists at once, giving two tokens and risking notes on the wrong visit (H-03). The appointment stays 'scheduled', so it can be cancelled or rescheduled mid-visit and the slot is re-offered to the waitlist. QA-08: transfer() leaves the original appointment 'scheduled' forever. Fix (MF-29): add 'arrived' to appointments.status; inside the existing per-doctor-day advisory lock, check-in runs UPDATE appointments SET status='arrived' WHERE id=? AND status='scheduled' and treats 0 rows as 409; a partial unique index on queue_entries(appointment_id) is the backstop; cancel and reschedule require 'scheduled'; markTerminal accepts arrived -> completed/no_show and runs when the encounter's last leg ends, so transfers no longer strand the appointment. Existing duplicate rows (from before the fix) are flagged legacy_duplicate rather than deleted, because notes or invoices may point at them. Also replaces the 32-bit hashtext advisory key with a two-key lock (T-201, MF-80) and wires the Idempotency-Key filter (MF-26) on check-in.
acceptance: Given two desks check in the same appointment at the same moment, then exactly one gets 201 with a token and the other gets 409 ALREADY_CHECKED_IN (CountDownLatch test, 50 repetitions, zero duplicates)
Given a checked-in appointment, when reception opens it in the calendar, then it shows 'Arrived' and the J2 journey (find by phone -> check in) completes in < 20 s
Given an arrived appointment, when staff try to cancel or reschedule it, then the API returns 409 APPOINTMENT_ARRIVED and the waitlist is not offered the slot
Given a visit transferred from General Medicine to Dermatology, when the Dermatology leg completes, then the appointment becomes completed (never left 'scheduled')
Given a check-in retried with the same Idempotency-Key after a network timeout, then the original 201 body is returned and no second token is issued
Given 20 desks checking in concurrently for 5 doctors, then check-in p95 < 300 ms (k6 profile from T-068)

stories.title: Overlapping or invalid bookings are impossible, and each refusal says why
stories.story: As a receptionist I want the system to block overlapping bookings and bookings on leave, outside hours, off the slot grid or in the past, with a specific reason, so that two patients never share a slot and I know what to fix.
stories.context: MF-30 / QA-09: the only guard is uq_appointments_doctor_slot (doctor_id, start_time) WHERE status='scheduled', so 10:00 and 10:05 can both be booked in a 15-minute grid. AppointmentService.book ignores doctor leave (availability hides it, POST does not), working hours (outside any block it silently uses 15 min and skips the cap), the slot grid and the past, and any DataIntegrityViolation becomes 409. Fix: an EXCLUDE USING gist constraint on (tenant_id, doctor_id, tstzrange(start_time, end_time, '[)')) for slot-holding statuses, plus one SlotValidator used by staff booking, reschedule, waitlist chosen slot and the Edge internal API, built on the same rules as ScheduleGrid so the grid and the API never disagree. Constraint and validation failures map to named Problem types. Overbooking is not done by overlapping slots: extra patients come in as walk-in tokens under the session cap (ACC-011/ACC-012). The constraint includes booking_kind='slot' so token-mode sessions (ACC-011) are not blocked.
acceptance: Given a doctor with 15-minute slots and a booking at 10:00, when staff book 10:05 for another patient, then the API returns 409 SLOT_TAKEN
Given 20 concurrent requests for overlapping times with the same doctor, then exactly 1 returns 201 and 19 return 409 SLOT_TAKEN

Given a doctor on leave today, when staff book 11:00 today, then the API returns 400 DOCTOR_ON_LEAVE; outside hours -> 400 OUTSIDE_HOURS; 10:07 on a 15-minute grid -> 400 OFF_GRID; a past time -> 400 IN_PAST; a clinic holiday -> 400 CLINIC_CLOSED
Given the same invalid inputs sent to reschedule and to waitlist accept with a chosen slot, then the same errors are returned (one validator)
Given a cancelled appointment, when another patient books the same time, then it succeeds immediately

Given 1,000 random slot requests per timezone (Asia/Kolkata, Asia/Dubai, Asia/Riyadh, Asia/Qatar), then every slot returned by GET /v1/doctors/{id}/availability books successfully and every other time is refused (property test)
Given normal load, then booking write p95 < 400 ms

stories.title: Evening sessions that cross midnight stay one clinic day, and doctors can take part-day leave
stories.story: As a doctor I want my 20:00-01:00 session to be one session and to block just an afternoon off, so that my calendar matches reality and the queue does not reset at midnight.
stories.context: QA-22 / MF-54: queue_date is the calendar date at check-in and doctor_working_hours requires end_time > start_time, so a Gulf clinic running to 01:00 gets two queues at midnight: tokens restart at 1, GET /v1/queue defaults to the new date so everyone checked in before midnight disappears from the board, walk-ins after midnight skip the session cap and day close for 'yesterday' breaks. Doctor leave (V4) is whole-day only. Fix: a session-based clinic day with a configurable day start per tenant (default 04:00): ClinicClock.clinicDate(tenant, instant) = local date of (instant - dayStart). Every 'today' in scheduling, visit and the day close uses clinicDate. Working hours may end after midnight (end_time < start_time means next calendar day, and must end before the day start). ScheduleGrid works in minutes from the clinic-day start so 00:30 is minute 1470 and shows as '00:30 (+1)'. doctor_leave gains optional start_time/end_time for part-day leave inside one clinic day. Depends on T-060 (injected java.time.Clock). Ramadan schedules are R4 (T-271).

stories.title: Patients are told automatically when staff move, cancel or block their booking, with the nearest alternatives
stories.story: As a patient I want a WhatsApp message with the change and two or three alternative times whenever the clinic moves or cancels my booking, so that I do not turn up for a slot that no longer exists.
stories.context: FRD RCP-09, DOC-03, SYS-04: when the desk reschedules or cancels, or a doctor adds leave, the affected patients must get the change automatically with the nearest alternatives, and the receptionist must not type free text. Today addLeave only returns names of package patients and does not flag existing bookings (V4 'ponytail' note). Design: staff reschedule/cancel publish events with the coded reason; the Edge turns them into utility templates (sent by comms-gateway, PHI-minimised). New leave lists affected bookings on the desk; each row shows the three nearest valid alternatives (same doctor first, then same-specialty doctors if the owner allows). One tap 'Offer alternatives' (per row or all) records an offer and the patient gets buttons; tapping one books it through the internal API (409 -> next alternative is re-offered) and cancels the old booking with reason clinic_initiated. Patients without WhatsApp consent go to the callback list (NB-116) instead.
acceptance: Given a confirmed booking, when reception reschedules it, then the patient receives a utility template with the new date, time and clinic name within 60 s, containing no diagnosis or visit-reason text
Given reception cancels with reason 'doctor unavailable', then the patient receives a cancellation template with a 'Book again' button within 60 s
Given a doctor adds leave covering 3 booked appointments, then the desk shows 3 affected rows, each with the 3 nearest valid alternatives, within 2 s of saving the leave

Given reception taps 'Offer alternatives to all', then each patient gets slot buttons; when a patient taps one, the new booking is confirmed and the old one cancelled with reason clinic_initiated; if the slot was taken meanwhile, the next alternative is offered
Given the whole flow, then the receptionist never types free text (UI test asserts no text input on the path)
Given a patient with no WhatsApp consent, then the affected row moves to the callback list with a 'call patient' action

stories.title: Owner sets booking and queue rules per facility and visit type and publishes them as an audited version
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want to choose, per visit type, whether bookings are auto-accepted, reviewed or hybrid, and set check-in, ETA display, walk-in and no-show rules, then publish them, so that the clinic runs the way I decided without staff improvising.
stories.context: Founder brief B-17/B-18/B-19/B-22 and EP10. The prototype owner.workflows screen is the target UX: per visit type (new, follow-up, procedure/package, teleconsult; walk-ins take tokens) choose acceptance (auto with daily cap per doctor, review by a designated role, or hybrid = auto for returning/follow-up, review for patients new to the doctor), the reviewer role and the cap; per facility choose solo mode, check-in modes (door QR, WhatsApp 'I'm here', geofence, desk), the default ETA display mode, leave-home margin, walk-in interleave (1 per 2/3/4, reserved slots only, none), no-show grace (10/15/20 min), auto-mark no-show and pull-forward. Settings are a versioned JSON document validated against a schema (booking-policy.v1); publishing needs TOTP step-up, writes an audit row with before/after and takes effect from the next booking; existing bookings keep the version they were made under (appointments.policy_version). The resulting patient-journey preview is computed client-side from the draft. This fits the existing 'owners pick templates and toggles, not a rules engine' principle (V40, CAD-06): owners choose from fixed options. Deposits after repeated no-shows belong to billing and are only a flag here.

stories.title: Bookings are auto-confirmed, held for review, or routed by visit type in under 2 seconds
stories.story: As a patient I want my booking either confirmed straight away or clearly marked as 'we will confirm within 10 minutes', so that I know where I stand without phoning the clinic.
stories.context: Today only staff create bookings and there is no 'requested' state (S04 §3.1). Add 'requested' and 'declined' to appointments.status; a requested booking holds its slot (it is covered by the EXCLUDE constraint) until decided. BookingDecisionService evaluates each incoming booking against the published policy: visit type (new / follow-up / procedure / tele, derived from the patient's history with that doctor and appointments.is_follow_up), acceptance mode, daily auto-accept cap per doctor and clinic date, session capacity, triage flags (red-flag phrases detected by the Edge, e.g. 'chest pain' -> always review, never auto), and sibling/group bookings (always review in hybrid). Outcome is CONFIRMED (status scheduled, decision_source auto) or REQUESTED (sla_due_at = now + review SLA, default 10 min, review_reason recorded). Requests past their SLA raise an escalation to the reviewer and owner rather than being silently dropped or auto-declined. Staff bookings are confirmed directly (staff are the reviewers) but still respect caps. Every channel (desk, WhatsApp, web, widget, app, call centre, aggregator) goes through this one path.
acceptance: Given a clinic in Hybrid mode, when a returning follow-up patient books on WhatsApp, then the booking is CONFIRMED within 2 s and the confirmation is sent only after commit
Given Hybrid mode, when a patient new to the doctor books, then the booking is REQUESTED, the slot cannot be booked by anyone else, and the patient is told 'we will confirm within 10 minutes'
Given Auto mode with a cap of 40 per doctor per clinic day, when the 41st auto-eligible booking arrives, then it is REQUESTED with review_reason over_cap
Given a booking note containing a red-flag phrase, then it is REQUESTED with a triage flag even in Auto mode, and it sorts first in the requests inbox
Given a REQUESTED booking not decided by its SLA, then an escalation event is raised to the reviewer role and the owner within 1 minute, and the patient gets a 'still checking' message once
Given 50 bookings per minute for one tenant, then decision p95 < 2 s end to end inside Core (k6)

stories.title: Each doctor session runs as booked slots, walk-in tokens, or both, with its own caps
stories.story: As a doctor I want to run my morning as timed appointments and my evening OPD as a token session with an online-booking cap, so that the calendar matches how I actually see patients.

Add session_mode (slot | token | hybrid) and online_cap to doctor_working_hours. Slot sessions behave as today. Token sessions sell numbered places, not times: an online token booking is an appointment with booking_kind='token', start/end = session window and a reserved token number; it is excluded from the EXCLUDE overlap constraint and limited by online_cap; the patient sees an expected range from the ETA engine. Capacity counting stays under the per-doctor-day advisory lock shared by booking and check-in (NB-098 rule). Changing a session's mode applies to future dates only.

Given a hybrid session, when bookings and walk-ins race for the last place, then exactly one gets it (same lock)

stories.title: Walk-ins are interleaved fairly with booked patients, with reserved walk-in capacity
stories.story: As a receptionist I want walk-ins placed by a clear rule, such as one walk-in after every three booked patients, and some slots kept for walk-ins, so that the queue feels fair and I can explain it.
stories.context: BQ-05 / RCP-13 / ASM-05 (walk-in-first clinics): walk-ins work but there is no ratio or reserved capacity. A pure CallOrderPolicy decides who is called next and is the single source of order for the desk, the doctor's call-next button and the ETA engine: priority flags first (with reason), then booked patients who have arrived within +/-10 min of their slot, then walk-ins interleaved by the configured ratio (1:2, 1:3, 1:4), or walk-ins only into reserved slots, or no walk-ins (desk override with reason). A booked patient arriving later than the no-show grace is placed as a walk-in, and the reason is shown. Reserved walk-in slots are grid slots that online channels never offer. Placement (position + expected range) is shown to the desk at check-in. Doctors call the next patient with one button that applies the policy and moves the entry with CAS.
acceptance: Given ratio 1:3 with 6 booked patients arrived on time and 3 walk-ins waiting, then the call order is B,B,B,W,B,B,B,W,W (deterministic unit test)
Given a reserved walk-in slot at 11:00, then no online channel offers 11:00 and a walk-in arriving at 10:55 is placed into it
Given a walk-in check-in, then the desk sees the position and expected range within 1 s
Given a booked patient arriving 25 min late with grace 15, then they are placed as a walk-in and the entry shows 'late arrival - placed as walk-in'
Given a priority flag with a reason, then that patient is called next regardless of ratio and the override is audited
Given 1,000 simulated sessions with pilot arrival patterns, then in 95% of them no walk-in waits more than (ratio + 1) x median consult time longer than under pure arrival order

stories.title: Each doctor has a learned consult-time distribution per visit type
stories.story: As the ETA engine I need each doctor's consult-time distribution per visit type, kept up to date after every consult, so that patients get realistic ranges instead of one clinic-wide average.
stories.context: DP §5.5: consult times are right-skewed, so model them as log-normal per (doctor, visit_type) where visit_type is new / follow_up / procedure / review (from appointments.is_follow_up, class and department). Seed from the doctor's slot_minutes, then the clinic median, then a specialty default. Update online at every in_consult -> * transition with an EWMA (alpha about 0.1) of log duration and its variance; recompute robust median and p80 nightly over a 30-day window. Doctors with fewer than 20 observations shrink toward the clinic prior (empirical Bayes, weight n/(n+20)). Consults longer than 4x the median (doctor forgot to close) are capped and flagged, not learned. This unblocks the patient-facing ETA (ACC-017) and gives owners per-doctor consult time for the ops dashboard (T-196).
acceptance: Given a consult ends, then the doctor's stats row for that visit type is updated within 5 s
Given a doctor with 5 observations, then the estimate equals the blend 5/25 doctor + 20/25 clinic prior (unit test with fixed numbers)
Given a consult of 4x the median, then it is capped, flagged in queue_entry_events, and the EWMA moves no more than a capped consult would move it
Given 1,000 doctors in a region, then the nightly robust recompute finishes in < 2 minutes
Given new and follow-up visits for one doctor, then they keep separate distributions

stories.title: Patients and staff see an honest ETA range that updates within 5 seconds of any change
stories.story: As a patient I want a range such as '10:40-10:55' and my position, updated whenever the queue changes, so that I can plan when to leave home.
stories.context: ETA engine v2 (EP11, DP §5.5) runs in the Core worker profile (module visit). For each doctor and clinic date: ETA_k = max(now, doctor_available_at) + E[remaining of current consult] + sum of E[D_i] for entries ahead (ordered by the CallOrderPolicy from ACC-012) + active delay + pre-stage times (vitals/billing per workflow template) + elapsed pause. Variance is summed for the p80. The range is p50 to p80 rounded to 5 minutes. Booked-but-not-arrived appointments also get an ETA (needed for leave-home alerts). Recompute triggers: any visit or scheduling event for that doctor-day, delay announce/clear, session start/pause/end, plus a 60 s tick while a consult is running. Results go to a Valkey hash t:{tid}:eta:{doctor}:{date} (ids only, TTL 12 h) and deltas are published to t:{tid}:q:{doctor}:{date} for SSE. The 2.25 s wait-estimate query is retired: /v1/queue/wait-estimate reads the projection. Accuracy target: +/-10 min for >= 80% of visits by week 6 live, measured by ACC-019.
acceptance: Given a checked-in patient, then their entry has a range like '10:40-10:55' and a position, and the range is never narrower than 5 minutes
Given any queue event for a doctor, then all of that doctor's ETAs are recomputed and published within 5 s (p95)
Given a 30-minute delay is announced, then every waiting and booked patient's p50 moves later by at least 30 min within 5 s
Given a consult running longer than its median, then the next patient's ETA moves out progressively on each 60 s tick
Given pilot data at week 6, then |actual call time - p50| <= 10 min for >= 80% of visits per clinic (ACC-019 metric)
Given GET /v1/queue/wait-estimate, then p95 < 50 ms (projection read) versus 2.25 s today
Given the Valkey ETA keys, then they contain only ids, positions and times (no names or phone numbers)

stories.title: Staff screens get queue, ETA, requests and doctor status pushed in under 2 seconds
stories.story: As a receptionist I want the board to update itself the moment anything changes, so that two desks never disagree and I stop refreshing.
stories.context: MF-41 / ADR-05: screens poll every 15 s with N+1 fan-out (nursing ~2N+6 requests per tick). Core module realtime serves GET /v1/events?topics=... on async servlets with Java 21 virtual threads: a snapshot on connect, then {type, id, v} deltas; Last-Event-ID resume from a short per-tenant-day Valkey stream; 25 s heartbeat. An sse-fanout consumer reads committed domain events from Valkey Streams (T-081 relay) and the ETA engine's deltas, and publishes per-topic deltas on Valkey pub/sub channels t:{tid}:q:{doctor}:{date}, t:{tid}:requests, t:{tid}:doctor-status; each SSE node subscribes only to channels for connected tenants. Topics are filtered by the caller's permissions (queue:view, nursing:view, scheduling:review). Deltas carry ids, statuses, tokens and versions; names come from the board/batch reads (ACC-022) so nothing PHI-heavy travels on the stream. The shared browser client (one EventSource per browser via BroadcastChannel, 60 s polling fallback, pause when hidden) is T-095 in the Frontend domain. A synthetic probe measures event-to-screen latency.

Given a client reconnects within 5 minutes with Last-Event-ID, then missed deltas are replayed without a new snapshot; after 5 minutes it gets a fresh snapshot
Given an idle connection, then a heartbeat arrives every 25 s and proxies do not close it
Given a user without nursing:view, then subscribing to topic nursing returns 403 and no nursing deltas are ever sent to that connection
Given tenants A and B on the same node, then a delta for A is never written to B's connections (isolation test with 100 tenants)
Given 1,000 concurrent connections per pod, then heap stays < 512 MB and delivery p95 stays < 2 s

stories.title: A doctor delay or queue pause reaches every affected patient within a minute, in two taps
stories.story: As a receptionist I want to tap 'Running late: 30 min' and have every affected patient told, so that I stop phoning 18 people.
stories.context: EP14 / BQ-06 / BQ-07 / FRD RCP-04: the delay is recorded staff-side (V33) but never expires, never reaches the ETA (QA-23) and is never broadcast. Delay ladder 15/30/45/60 in two taps from desk or phone; the receptionist can broadcast even if the doctor has not (the doctor cannot block it). The delay lapses at the end of the session. Broadcast: every patient booked for that doctor's remaining session today who has not yet been called and has messaging consent gets a utility template with the new expected time (shaped by the display mode) and buttons 'OK', 'Reschedule', 'Cancel'; replies are shown on the desk. Pause queue (solo doctor handling an emergency): two taps with a private reason code, a neutral patient message with no PHI ('The doctor is briefly unavailable; we will update you'), ETAs shift by the elapsed pause, and resume re-broadcasts only if anyone's time moved >= 10 min. A patient gets at most one delay message per 20 minutes. In KSA the delay template carries the operational flag that bypasses the prayer-window hold (V33 note); marketing never does.

stories.title: Waitlist offers only future slots, every booking path honours a live offer, and offers expire on time
stories.story: As a receptionist I want the waitlist to offer only slots that are still in the future, to protect a slot while it is on offer, and to pass it on when the offer runs out, so that the single-offer promise holds.
stories.context: QA-24 / MF-70: WaitlistService.onSlotFreed offers a slot even when it is in the past (a missed 10:00 cancelled at 14:00), plain accept then books a past appointment, AppointmentService.book never checks isSlotOnLiveOffer (so the desk can take a slot on offer and the waitlisted patient's accept fails), and expiry is lazy (only when someone opens the list). stories.title: A returning patient books on WhatsApp in five taps or fewer and under a minute
stories.story: As a returning patient I want to be recognised by my number and book with buttons, so that booking takes less than a minute and I never type.
stories.context: EP12 / PW-01 / FRD PAT-03 / B-01 / B-05. Flow: 'Hi' -> recognised by phone (household lookup) -> 'Book with Dr. Shah again?' or 'Another doctor' -> day buttons (next days with availability) -> time list (WhatsApp list message, max 10 rows) or, for token sessions, 'Evening OPD, expected 18:10-18:30' -> confirm card (doctor, date, time, clinic) -> booking request (ACC-009) -> confirmed or 'we will confirm within 10 minutes', sent only after Core commits. On 409 the bot re-offers the nearest alternative. The patient chooses a language once (EN/HI/KN/TE in India, AR/EN in the Gulf). On a clinic's own channel only that clinic is ever shown (T-167); on the shared Nabd number the clinic comes from the entry link. Templates and session messages carry no diagnosis or visit-reason text. Red-flag phrases in any free text are passed as triage flags.
acceptance: Given a returning patient, then booking completes in <= 5 interactions with no free text, median < 60 s (Playwright + WhatsApp sandbox journey, 20 runs)
Given the chosen slot is taken between offer and confirm, then the bot says so and offers the nearest alternative in the same message
Given Core returns CONFIRMED, then the confirmation is sent only after commit; if Core times out, the bot checks status with the same Idempotency-Key before saying anything
Given a clinic's own number, then no other clinic or doctor is ever mentioned (shared T-167 test list)
Given a token session, then the patient gets a token number and an expected range, not a fixed time
Given the patient leaves mid-flow and returns within 24 h, then the bot resumes from the last step

stories.title: Provisioning steps run exactly once, even when two workers advance the same job

stories.title: Leaving owner gets a signed deletion certificate within 30 days
stories.story: As an owner leaving Nabd I want to request deletion after downloading my export and receive a signed certificate that live data was erased within 30 days and backups purged on the backup cycle, so that I can show it to an auditor or regulator.
stories.context: NFR-18 promises a verified deletion certificate within 30 days. Deletion moves the tenant to 'offboarding' (V11 lifecycle) and requires: an export downloaded in the last 14 days (or an explicit waiver), owner step-up, and a 7-day cooling-off during which the owner can cancel. After cooling-off the worker crypto-shreds the tenant DEK, deletes rows tenant by tenant in dependency order, revokes WhatsApp media links and secure links, and records counts. Records the law makes the clinic keep (tax invoices 8 years in India under GST s.36, medical records per regulator) are handed over in the export, not retained by Nabd. The certificate (JCS + ES256 signed, DPO named) states erase date, backup purge date (erase + 35 days) and region; it is sent by email and WhatsApp and stored in the control plane without PHI.
acceptance: Given no export downloaded in the last 14 days, when the owner requests deletion, then they must download an export or tick a waiver that is recorded
Given a deletion request, when 7 days of cooling-off pass without cancel, then live data is erased and the certificate is issued no later than day 30 after the request
Given erasure completes, when an operator queries any tenant table for that tenant_id, then zero rows are returned and the tenant DEK is destroyed
Given the certificate, when verified with Nabd's public key, then the signature is valid and it lists tenant, branches, erase date, backup purge date, region and signer
Given the owner cancels during cooling-off, when they confirm, then the tenant returns to its previous status and nothing was deleted

stories.title: CSO-signed, versioned regional safety dictionary v1 with brand names
stories.story: As a doctor I want allergy, pregnancy and controlled-drug warnings to recognise the brand names my patients actually take so that 'Isotroin 20mg' or 'Mox 500' cannot slip past the safety checks.
stories.context: Today the lists live in code: RxSafetyChecks has 11 pregnancy-risk drugs and 6 controlled drugs per region, and AllergyDrugClasses has hand-written classes with a few brands (QA-16: 'Isotroin 20mg' for a 28-year-old woman gives no warning). Move the content into a versioned, region-scoped dictionary that the CSO approves, keep the matching algorithm in code, and stamp the dictionary version on every signed prescription so the printout and audit show what rules were applied. Version 1 covers India (generic + common Indian brands, Hindi transliterations where common) and a GCC draft (generic + SFDA/DHA brands, Arabic names). It keeps the current design rules: false positives over misses, class cross-reactivity in one direction, whole-word terms vs stems, NOT_THE_STEM_DRUG exclusions. The licensed knowledge base (CLN-018, CLN-019) later becomes the main source; this dictionary remains the CSO-owned override layer and the local fallback for the CDS service (ADR-13).

stories.title: Only a licensed clinician can sign a prescription or override a safety warning
stories.story: As a doctor I want prescription signing and override decisions to require a clinical licence so that a non-clinician owner, a nurse or a break-glass session can never put my name on a prescription or wave through a severe-allergy hard stop.
stories.context: QA-17: provisioning seeds Owner with fullGrant("clinical") (ProvisioningStepRunner.java:194) and PrescriptionService.mayActAsVisitDoctor treats clinical:approve as 'may sign any Rx'. The RBAC Matrix says Owner -> Clinical Records Create N, Edit N. Rule after this story: sign and record a requiresDecision decision only if (a) staff.is_clinician = true, (b) staff.professional_registration_no (V55) is present, (c) the licence is not expired (T-310 data when available), (d) the session is not break-glass, and (e) the caller is the visit doctor or holds clinical:approve. Add prescriptions.signed_by and signed_by_registration_no so the print no longer reads the signer from audit_log (PrescriptionPrintRepository.findHeader). Apply the same rule to clinical_documents issue (referral, certificate). Owner-doctors (an owner who is also a registered clinician) keep signing.
acceptance: Given an owner without a registration number, when they call POST /v1/clinical/prescriptions/{queueEntryId}/sign on another doctor's visit, then the response is 403 not-licensed-clinician and nothing is signed
Given an owner-doctor with is_clinician=true and a registration number, when they sign their own visit's Rx, then it signs and prescriptions.signed_by is their staff id
Given a nurse with clinical:edit, when they add a draft line, then it saves; when they try to sign or record a severe-allergy decision, then 403 not-prescriber
Given a break-glass session, when it calls sign, then 403 break-glass-cannot-sign and an audit row is written
Given a new tenant is provisioned, when the Owner role is inspected, then its clinical grants match the RBAC Matrix exactly (generated authz test green)
Given a signed prescription from before this migration, when the print header is requested, then signer comes from the backfilled signed_by and not from audit_log
Given a clinician whose licence expired yesterday, when they sign, then 403 licence-expired (owner can grant a time-boxed override, audited)

stories.story: As an engineer I want all Rx safety checks behind one RxSafetyService port with a local implementation and a remote Clinical Intelligence client so that doctors always get checks, even when the CDS service is slow or down.
stories.context: ADR-13 and doc06 §5.1: clinical/internal/rx/safety/RxSafetyService (port) -> LocalRules | ClinicalIntelligenceClient. Today detectLine in PrescriptionService calls RxSafetyChecks directly. Step 1: extract the port; LocalRules wraps dictionary (CLN-004), coded checks (CLN-021) and DDI (CLN-032). Step 2: the client calls POST /cds/rx-check with an 800 ms budget, Resilience4j circuit breaker, and on timeout/open circuit falls back to LocalRules and stamps cdsSource=local on the response and on prescriptions at signing. Context sent is pseudonymised and minimised: age band, sex, pregnancy status, eGFR/K+ values with dates, allergy and medicine ids, no names or identifiers (request hash for audit). Parity tests guarantee LocalRules and the service agree on the shared rule set. Unblocks doctor-facing CLN-037/038/040.

Given the service takes > 800 ms, when a line is checked, then LocalRules results are returned within 900 ms total and cdsSource=local is stamped
Given 5 consecutive failures, when the next check runs, then the circuit is open and no remote call is made for 30 s
Given a signed Rx, when read later, then it records cdsSource and rule versions used
Given the outbound request body, when inspected in tests, then it contains no patient name, phone, MRN, ABHA or national id
Given the shared rule fixtures, when run against both implementations, then results are identical (parity suite green)

stories.title: Doctor is warned when a dose is unsafe for the patient's kidney function or potassium
stories.story: As a cardiologist or physician I want renal dosing and hyperkalaemia risks flagged from the latest eGFR and potassium so that I adjust or avoid drugs without searching.
stories.context: AI-04 (condition- and lab-aware alerts). The prototype results inbox shows the motivating case: K+ rising to 6.1 on telmisartan with eGFR 52 -> 40. Rules in the CDS service (CLN-036) use the latest eGFR/creatinine and K+ results (lab module T-220, or manually entered values) with their dates: renal dose bands per drug from the KB (e.g. metformin contraindicated eGFR < 30, reduce < 45), potassium-raising drugs (ACEi, ARB, spironolactone, K supplements) when K+ >= 5.5, and stale-lab warnings when the last value is older than the rule's window. stories.title: Opt-in AI suggests a regimen from diagnosis, allergies, conditions and labs, with sources
stories.story: As a doctor who opts in I want suggested prescriptions (drug, dose, duration, alternatives) with reasons and sources for the diagnosis I chose, so that I can prescribe faster while I stay the decision-maker.

Engine: retrieval over the licensed KB and approved guideline snippets (clinic formulary, national guidelines) + an in-region LLM registered in CLN-038 that ranks and explains candidate regimens; deterministic post-filters remove anything that fails RxSafetyService checks or is outside the KB. Evaluation set (curated with the CSO, stored in restricted storage, not git) measures appropriateness, safety-filter catch rate and citation accuracy; release gate: >= 90% clinician-rated appropriate on the eval set, 0 unsafe suggestions passing filters.

stories.title: Store every WhatsApp webhook delivery before acknowledging it, and drop duplicates by wamid
stories.story: As a patient I want my WhatsApp reply to reach the clinic every time so that I am not ignored, even when Meta retries or the database is slow.
stories.context: Today WhatsAppWebhookController verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC (good) but then processes statuses and templates in-line and logs-and-drops inbound messages (QA-30, MF-48). A slow insert makes Meta retry the whole batch, causing redelivery storms. The fix is persist-then-ack: verify the signature, write the raw body once to an inbound event table keyed by a dedupe key, return 200 inside 100 ms, then process asynchronously. Dedupe keys are the message wamid for inbound messages, wamid+status for status callbacks, and template id+event+timestamp for template events. The raw body can contain patient free text, so it is stored AES-GCM encrypted (existing AesGcmCipher, key version prefix) and purged after 30 days. The same story brings V46/V47 tables up to ADR-07 (FORCE RLS, array policy, WITH CHECK) because they predate it. This is built in Core's messaging module first (S4) and moves unchanged into the Comms Gateway in COM-008.
acceptance: Given a correctly signed webhook POST, when it arrives, then the raw body is persisted and 200 is returned with p95 < 100 ms at 200 rps (QA §4.4 webhook storm)
Given the same inbound message (same wamid) delivered 3 times, when all three are processed, then exactly one inbound message row exists and downstream consumers see one event
Given a webhook with a missing or wrong X-Hub-Signature-256, when it arrives, then 401 is returned, nothing is stored, and a security metric is incremented (no body logged)
Given the processor crashes mid-batch, when it restarts, then unprocessed rows are re-claimed (lease expiry) and processed exactly once by effect
Given status callbacks arrive out of order (read before delivered), when processed, then message status only moves forward (existing apply_whatsapp_status rule kept)
Given an inbound event row older than 30 days, when the purge job runs, then its encrypted raw body is deleted and only the dedupe key and outcome remain
Given any tenant table touched here (whatsapp_messages, whatsapp_templates, whatsapp_inbound_events), when the boot self-check runs, then RLS is enabled and forced

stories.title: Meta calls fail fast and never send twice when the provider is slow
stories.story: As an engineer I want every call to Meta wrapped in timeouts, a circuit breaker and lease-fenced sends so that a provider outage never duplicates a reminder or blocks the clinic.

stories.title: One notification contract every module and service uses to ask for a message
stories.story: As an engineer I want a single 'notification requested' contract with a dedupe key, priority, send window and claim-check render data so that every feature can send messages without knowing the channel and the Comms Gateway can be extracted by swapping transport only.
stories.context: Unblocks every patient-facing message (reminders, recalls, delay broadcast, secure links, owner summaries). Today WhatsAppMessageService.queueTemplate is the only producer and has no production callers (F-33). Events must carry ids only (ADR-03), yet a template needs names and times. Design: the caller's module calls NotificationPort.request(...) inside its transaction; this writes a 'notification_requests' row in Core (render params encrypted, recipient patient id, purpose, dedupe key, priority, notBefore/notAfter) and an outbox event 'comms.notification.requested.v1' with ids only. The Comms side fetches render params at send time from GET /internal/v1/notification-requests/{id} (claim check); Core answers 410 when the subject changed (appointment cancelled), which doubles as late-cancel protection. Purposes map to template keys and consent purposes (care = 'messaging', promotions = 'marketing'). Priority lanes: OTP, TRANSACTIONAL (queue, delay, secure link), REMINDER, BULK (recall, review, feedback). In S4 the consumer runs in-process; in S5 it is the Comms Gateway.

stories.title: Deploy the Comms Gateway as its own service with its own database
stories.story: As an engineer I want services/comms-gateway running in prod-in with its own database, CI pipeline and runbook so that Meta credentials and the public webhook are isolated from Core's blast radius.
stories.context: Unblocks platform ops (separate on-call surface) and patients (bursts no longer compete with check-in for Core's pool). ADR-01 extracts Comms first because it already sits behind ports (WhatsAppClient, WhatsAppOtpSender, EmailSender) and the outbox. The service is Spring Boot on the same build conventions (/services/comms-gateway), modules whatsapp, sms, email, templates, webhooks. It has its own Postgres (T-113) with no grants on Core tables (tested), consumes the 'comms' consumer group on Valkey Streams (ADR-03), and calls Core only via /internal/v1 with mTLS and aud=internal. stories.title: Login and patient OTPs go through the Comms Gateway with a 3-second budget

stories.title: Messages come from the verified Nabd number but show the clinic's name, and replies reach the right clinic
stories.story: As a patient I want messages to come from a verified business sender that shows my clinic's name so that I trust they are not a scam, and my reply goes to that clinic.
stories.context: P12 fears scams; PW-02/AD-04 say Phase 1 uses one shared verified Nabd number with per-clinic branding and Phase 2 adds own numbers. Branding exists partly: V47 bakes the clinic name into each template header and prefixes meta_name with the tenant slug. Missing: a sender model and inbound routing on a shared number, where one patient phone may talk to two clinics. This story adds sender_accounts (the shared Nabd sender row plus, later, tenant senders) and a routing table that records, per patient phone, the clinic of the most recent outbound message and any open 24-hour window; inbound is routed to that clinic, and button payloads carry an opaque tenant-scoped token so a tap is always routed exactly. If ambiguous (two clinics messaged in the last 24 h and free text), the bot asks 'Which clinic?' with buttons. MetaWhatsAppClient changes from a singleton to a per-sender client resolved by sender_account_id.

Given a patient messaged by Clinic A and Clinic B in the last 24 h, when they send free text, then the bot asks which clinic with two buttons before routing
Given a button tap, when the payload token is resolved, then routing uses the token's tenant regardless of recency, and a forged token is rejected

stories.title: Template lifecycle with Meta: versions, rejection fixes, pauses and re-categorisation handled without breaking sends
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want to know when Meta rejects, pauses or re-categorises a template and have sends switch safely so that patients still get their reminders.
stories.context: V47 models pending/approved/flagged/paused/disabled/rejected and edits only rejected templates. Gaps: no versions (editing an approved template replaces it in review, so sends would stop), no handling of Meta's category change (utility re-categorised as marketing changes cost and consent class), paused templates fail sends immediately (WhatsAppSendHandler 'fail now'), and no one is told. This story adds template versions (new version submitted while the old approved one keeps sending, then swapped on approval), a 'paused_until' hold that defers non-urgent sends up to their window end instead of failing, a category-change handler that blocks a template whose new category needs marketing consent until the owner confirms, and owner/platform alerts via notifications. stories.title: Reminders and OTPs always go first, even during a 5x burst
stories.story: As a patient with an appointment I want my reminder and queue updates to arrive on time even when the clinic sends a recall batch so that I do not miss my visit.
stories.context: NFR-17: handle 5x normal volume without delaying reminders. Comms schedules sends through four lanes (OTP > TRANSACTIONAL > REMINDER > BULK) with weighted fair dequeue, and per-sender token buckets in Valkey sized to the sender's Meta messaging tier and throughput (80 mps default for Cloud API) with headroom. Per-tenant fairness inside BULK prevents one clinic's recall run from starving another on the shared number. The lane comes from the notification request priority (COM-004). Backpressure: when buckets are empty, BULK is deferred, never dropped.

Given an OTP during the burst, when requested, then send latency p99 < 3 s
Given two tenants on the shared sender, when one queues 10,000 bulk messages, then the other tenant's bulk throughput stays >= 30% of the lane
Given Meta returns 429 / error 130429, when received, then the sender's bucket is reduced for 60 s and messages retry, none lost

stories.title: Auto-throttle a sender before Meta restricts it, and alert the owner and platform
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want sending to slow down automatically when my number's quality drops so that Meta never blocks reminders for all my patients.
stories.context: FRD SSA-03 (MVP), CAD-07, RSK-05, NB-264. The webhook already stores template quality (V47) but nothing acts on phone-number quality. Comms subscribes to phone_number_quality_update and account_update, polls the phone number's quality_rating and messaging_limit_tier daily, and computes a local early-warning signal from block/report rate (user-initiated blocks visible as error 131049/131050 and STOP rate). stories.title: Notification scheduler sends inside the window and cancels anything that would arrive late
stories.story: As a patient I want reminders and 'leave now' messages to arrive on time or not at all so that I never get a reminder for a visit that already happened or was moved.
stories.context: doc06 §7.6 SLO: 99% of reminders and leave-now messages sent inside their window; a missed window is cancelled, never sent late (QA §4.9). Each notification request carries notBefore/notAfter (COM-004). Comms stores scheduled sends (status 'scheduled') and a scheduler (ShedLock leader per region, 15 s tick, Valkey sorted set index by due time) moves due ones into lanes. Before sending, Comms re-fetches render params (claim check), so a cancelled or moved appointment returns 410 and the send is cancelled. If the window passes during an outage, status becomes 'expired' and the caller gets a status event (so the desk sees 'reminder not sent' on the exceptions inbox, T-175). Reminder timing comes from clinic_policies.reminder_hours_before (V17) via the scheduling domain.

stories.title: Quiet hours for every clinic and prayer-time avoidance for KSA clinics
stories.story: As a patient I want non-urgent messages held during the night and, in KSA, during prayer times so that the clinic does not disturb me at the wrong moment.
stories.context: FRD SYS-03 (quiet hours, prayer-window avoidance), CMX-21 (KSA Meta policy: prayer-window and Friday-aware sends), NB-195, prototype note 'Quiet hours 21:00-09:00' (India) and 'never inside a prayer window, held during Eid closure days' (GCC). Each tenant has quiet hours (default 21:00-09:00 local, editable) and, for KSA tenants, prayer windows computed daily from the clinic's coordinates using Umm al-Qura times with a configurable buffer (default 20 min after adhan; Friday 11:30-13:30 block). Purposes are classed: URGENT (OTP, queue 'your turn', doctor delay, leave-now, secure link the patient just asked for) bypass both; everything else is deferred to the next allowed minute, but only if still inside notAfter, otherwise expired. Patients can extend quiet hours in their preferences (COM-025). Prayer windows are built now and switched on per tenant region, so either answer to DEC-27 works.

stories.title: OTPs and reminders fall back to SMS when WhatsApp fails
stories.story: As a patient I want my OTP or reminder to reach me by SMS when WhatsApp does not deliver so that I can still log in and turn up.
stories.context: FRD NFR-12: >= 95% of reminders delivered within 5 min; SMS fallback auto-fires on WhatsApp failure; zero duplicate sends. Rules (T-309): OTP with no 'delivered' status 30 s after send -> SMS; reminder 'failed' (or no delivery within 5 min for REMINDER lane) -> SMS within 5 min; secure-link messages fall back with the link only; BULK never falls back (cost and DND). The fallback creates a linked outbound_messages row (fallback_of) under the same request id, so idempotency holds: one fallback per request, never back to WhatsApp. Patients whose number is known not to be on WhatsApp (error 131026) are marked and later requests go SMS-first. India only (COM-026 region gate).

stories.title: Staff stay signed in all shift: silent single-flight token refresh with returnTo
stories.story: As a doctor I want my session to refresh silently in the background so that I never lose a half-written note or Rx to a forced logout.
stories.context: The backend issues 15-minute access tokens (application.yml:59) and 30-day rotating refresh tokens (POST /v1/auth/refresh, old token invalidated on use). The clinic app never calls refresh: ~20 copies of authedFetch treat 401 as 'remove token, router.replace(/login)'. app/platform/platformApi.ts:22-49 already does single-flight refresh correctly; port it. Because refresh tokens rotate, two tabs refreshing at once would trip reuse detection (sessions.family_id revoke) and log the user out everywhere, so refresh must be single-flight across tabs (Web Locks API `navigator.locks.request('nabd-refresh')` plus a BroadcastChannel that hands the new token to other tabs). Refresh proactively at 80% of `exp` and reactively on 401. If refresh truly fails, store a same-origin `returnTo` path (validated, never an absolute URL) and bring the user back after re-login. The idle-lock unlock call must refresh first, so an expired token is no longer reported as 'Incorrect PIN'. This is an interim client-side fix; FEF-009 moves tokens into httpOnly cookies.
acceptance: Given a doctor signed in at 08:00, when a scripted 8 h shift makes requests every 1-5 minutes across 3 tabs, then there are 0 redirects to /login and 0 reuse-detected revocations
Given 6 requests that all receive 401 at the same moment, when the client handles them, then exactly one POST /v1/auth/refresh is sent and all 6 requests are retried once with the new token
Given two tabs whose access tokens expire together, when both need a token, then only one tab calls refresh and the other receives the rotated token over BroadcastChannel within 500 ms

Given the refresh token is revoked (admin revoke or 30-day expiry), when the next request fails refresh, then the user lands on /login?returnTo=<current path> and after login returns to the same patient/visit page
Given a returnTo of `https://evil.example` or `//evil.example`, when login completes, then the user is sent to their role landing page instead

Given the idle lock is shown for 20 minutes, when the doctor enters the correct PIN, then the app refreshes first and unlocks; a wrong PIN shows 'Incorrect PIN', an expired session shows 'Session expired, sign in again' and a 429 shows 'Too many attempts, wait N s'

stories.title: Sessions move into httpOnly cookies behind an in-region same-origin BFF
stories.story: As a clinic owner accountable for patient data I want staff sessions held in httpOnly cookies behind our own domain so that a malicious script cannot steal a 30-day login.
stories.context: Access and 30-day refresh tokens sit in localStorage (login/page.tsx:45-46, accept-invite, owner/workspaces, account). The frontend is on Vercel and the API on Render, so they are cross-site. ADR-06: Next route handlers at /api/* act as a BFF, deployed in-region because PHI passes through it (Vercel keeps only public/static assets). The refresh token lives in `__Host-nabd_rt` (httpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/), the access token in `__Host-nabd_at` (httpOnly, 15 min), and the BFF proxies /api/v1/* to Core with the Authorization header. The browser never sees a token. CSRF: Origin check plus double-submit `__Host-nabd_csrf` cookie echoed as X-CSRF-Token on non-GET. Operator console uses separate cookie names. SSE (/api/events) streams through the same BFF so EventSource gets cookie auth. CORS on Core becomes nearly moot (closes MF-49). proxy.ts does optimistic auth redirects for (clinic)/(platform)/(owner) route groups.

Given the access cookie is expired, when the browser calls /api/v1/queue, then the BFF refreshes once (single-flight per session), sets new cookies and returns the data in the same response

stories.title: Strict nonce CSP and security headers on every staff page

stories.title: Payments are atomic and the invoice balance is always collectable, even after interim checkpoints
stories.story: As the billing desk I want every payment to add exactly once to the invoice and the invoice status to follow its real balance, so that a dental visit paid at an interim stop can still collect the later procedure charge and two cashiers can never lose a payment.
stories.context: Today CheckoutService.recordPayment reads invoices.paid, adds in Java and writes an absolute value (QA-11), so two simultaneous payments lose one. CheckoutRepository.updateInvoiceTotals changes totals at a later billing checkpoint but never recomputes status, so an invoice paid in full at billing_pending stays 'paid' after a procedure is appended and the next payment is refused with invoice-already-paid (QA-10, journey J11). The fix: lock the invoice row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) or use UPDATE invoices SET paid = paid + :amt ... RETURNING, derive paid from SUM(invoice_payments.amount) and recompute status (unpaid / partial / paid) on every change of total or payments. Overpayment is rejected (no change-giving through the system; change is a cash-drawer matter). A payment against a cancelled or fully-refunded invoice is refused. Unblocks the reception and solo personas for the pilot; prerequisite for refunds, payment links and day close accuracy.
acceptance: Given a 500 INR invoice, when two cashiers post 300 and 200 at the same instant, then invoices.paid = 500, status = 'paid' and SUM(invoice_payments) = invoices.paid

Given an invoice fully paid at an interim billing_pending checkpoint, when a 1,200 INR procedure is appended at checkout_pending, then status becomes 'partial', balance = 1,200 and a further payment of 1,200 is accepted (J11 green, < 90 s end to end)
Given an invoice with balance 200, when a payment of 250 is posted, then the API returns 422 overpayment with the current balance and no payment row is written
Given any invoice, when totals or payments change, then status is recomputed in the same transaction from paid vs total (never stored stale)
Given a nightly consistency job, when it compares invoices.paid with SUM(invoice_payments.amount) per tenant, then mismatches = 0 and any mismatch raises an alert

stories.title: Gapless invoice, credit-note and receipt series per GSTIN/VAT number, branch and financial year, with currency on every money header
stories.story: As the billing desk I want each invoice to take the next number in its own series for our GSTIN (or VAT number) and financial year, with the currency printed, so that our invoices pass a GST or VAT audit.
stories.context: Today invoices.invoice_number defaults to a global sequence 'INV-' || invoices_number_seq shared by all tenants (gaps and cross-tenant interleaving), package credit notes use another global sequence, and the invoice_series table (V41, keyed by tenant + tax_registration + kind + fiscal_year) is unused. GST rule 46 needs consecutive serial numbers unique per financial year (max 16 characters); ZATCA needs a sequential counter per device too (handled in FIN-050). Numbers are allocated by UPDATE invoice_series SET next_number = next_number + 1 ... RETURNING inside the invoice transaction (row lock = gapless, numbers allocated only on commit). The series is per facility (tenant = branch) and per tax registration, so a 3-branch owner with one GSTIN gets three independent series (multi-branch lite T-332). The Indian FY rolls on 1 April; GCC series roll on 1 January (configurable). Monetary headers (invoices, invoice_payments, package_instances, package_refunds, day_closes) get currency char(3) derived from the tax registration's jurisdiction, and amounts move to minor-unit bigint columns (expand/contract: dual-write, then switch reads) so KWD/BHD/OMR 3-decimal currencies work. Per-tenant MRN (T-107 AC) is delivered by the patient domain; this story only consumes it.

stories.title: Tax engine core: discount allocated to lines before tax, market rounding and a stored tax breakdown
stories.story: As the billing desk I want tax computed per line on the discounted value with the right rounding for our currency, so that we never over-collect tax and invoices add up exactly.
stories.context: QA-13: computeTotals charges tax on unitPrice x qty and then subtracts an invoice-level discount, so INR 1,000 at 18% with INR 100 discount gives tax 180 instead of 162; totals round to whole units even for SAR. The engine (billing/internal/tax) takes a cart (lines with taxable category, rate inputs, place of supply, patient attributes) and returns per-line taxable value, tax components and totals. Invoice-level discounts are allocated across discountable lines pro rata to line value (largest-remainder to keep minor units exact); line discounts apply first. Rounding: per-line tax rounded half-up to minor unit; INR invoice total may round to the nearest rupee with a round-off line (allowed under GST); SAR/AED/QAR keep 2 decimals with no whole-unit rounding. The engine is a port (TaxEngine) with jurisdiction adapters: IndiaGst (FIN-009), UaeVat (FIN-045), KsaVat (FIN-048), QatarNoVat; the tax rule tables are versioned reference data with effective dates so rate changes (e.g. GST rationalisation of 22 Sep 2025) apply to new bills only. Each invoice line stores its tax components so reprints never recompute.
acceptance: Given INR 1,000 at 18% and an INR 100 invoice discount, then taxable value = 900 and tax = 162 (QA-13 regression)
Given three lines (exempt 500, 18% 1,000, 5% 200) and a 170 discount, then the discount is allocated 50 / 100 / 20 and taxes are computed on the reduced values, sum of allocations = 170 exactly
Given a SAR invoice, then the total keeps 2 decimals and no whole-unit round-off line is produced
Given a rate change effective tomorrow, when a bill is created today, then today's rate is used; a reprint of yesterday's invoice shows the stored rate
Given any invoice, then SUM(line taxable + line tax) + round_off = total to the minor unit (invariant checked in tests and nightly)

stories.title: India GST rules: exempt clinical services, HSN/SAC on every head, CGST+SGST or IGST by place of supply
stories.story: As an Indian clinic I want consultations billed GST-exempt, cosmetic services at 18% and medicines at their HSN rate with CGST/SGST split, so that my invoices are correct without me knowing tax law.
stories.context: Healthcare services by a clinical establishment are exempt (SAC 9993), cosmetic and aesthetic procedures are taxable at 18% (reconstructive stays exempt), and medicines/consumables carry HSN-wise rates (commonly 5%, 12% or 0%; after the Sep 2025 rationalisation most medicines are 5% or nil). charge_catalogue today has tax_code (label), tax_rate_percent and hsn_code (pharmacy only). The clinic's GSTIN and state code come from tax_registrations; an unregistered clinic (below threshold) issues a 'Bill of Supply' with no tax lines. HSN-wise summary is kept for the invoice and returns export.

stories.title: One-click refund to the original payment source, and optional no-show deposits taken in chat
stories.story: As the billing desk I want an approved refund to go back to the patient's UPI or card in one click, and as an owner I want the option to take a deposit for bookings, so that refunds are instant and no-shows cost less.
stories.context: FRD PAT-10, SYS-08, CEO-12 and NB-209. Gateway refunds: when a refund request (FIN-013) is approved and the original payment was a gateway payment, the approver can 'Refund to source' which calls the gateway refund API (full or partial), tracks status (processed / failed) via webhook and records the negative payment only on success; cash refunds stay manual. Deposits: a tenant policy toggle (default OFF, CEO-12) and amount; when on, WhatsApp/booking-page bookings show a deposit payment link; the deposit is held as an advance on the patient (patient_advances) and applied to the visit invoice at checkout; a cancellation inside the policy window (clinic_policies.cancellation_window_hours) auto-refunds the deposit to source; a no-show forfeits it as a no-show fee invoice (taxed per jurisdiction rules). Package and estimate refunds reuse the same path.

Given deposits OFF (default), then no deposit is ever requested
Given deposits ON at INR 200 and a patient cancels 30 h before with a 24 h window, then the deposit is refunded to source automatically and the patient gets a WhatsApp confirmation
Given a no-show, then the deposit becomes a no-show fee invoice and is not refunded
Given a visit with a deposit, then checkout applies the advance and shows the remaining balance

stories.title: Package invoices split the bundle price across components with each line's own tax, and refunds reverse per line
stories.story: As the billing desk I want a mixed package (exempt consults plus a taxable peel and cream) invoiced line by line at its list-price share with the correct tax per line, so that GST or VAT on bundles is right and refunds reverse the right tax.
stories.context: PKG-09, PT-02, WE-01, CEO-07/08, RSK-03. Today package_instance_items stores allocated_price by list-price ratio but sellPackageInvoice creates the invoice from the request lines and package_items.tax_rate_percent is a single number; package_refunds produce one credit note number with no per-line tax reversal. Change: the package sale invoice is generated from the instance items — one invoice line per component with allocated taxable value (bundle price x component list value / sum of list values, largest remainder to the minor unit), tax category from the component's charge head via the tax engine (FIN-008), and the 'you save' line shown as an informational discount (PR-01). Tax-inclusive bundle prices (KSA WE-02) are back-calculated per line. Refund credit notes (FIN-004 + FIN-013) reverse per component: consumed sessions at full single-session list price (PKG-08), remainder refunded with per-line tax reversal; no processing fee by default (CEO-11). Release gate: the written GST opinion on bundle splitting is recorded in the Decisions sheet (CEO-07).

Given a refund after 3 of 6 sessions, then the credit note values used sessions at full single-session price and reverses tax line by line, with no processing fee
Given the release checklist, then the feature flag cannot be turned on for India until the GST opinion decision id is recorded
Given a package line on the printed invoice, then the 'Total if bought separately / you save' text is shown (PR-01)

Enrolment links the plan holder and family-linked members (T-297). stories.title: A running IPD bill accrues bed-days, nursing, visits and consumables automatically
stories.story: As a hospital billing officer I want every admission to have a running bill that adds room rent per night, nursing, consultant visits, procedures, lab and pharmacy issues automatically, so that the bill is always current.

stories.title: Owner sets up wards, beds and bed classes for a hospital facility
stories.story: As a hospital owner/admin I want to define wards, bays and beds with their class, sex policy, isolation and tariff so that admissions, the bed board and bed-day billing all use one bed master.
stories.context: Today departments.kind already allows 'ward' (V41) and service_points.kind allows 'bed', but nothing describes a bed's clinical attributes. This story adds a beds table keyed to service_points so the org hierarchy stays the single tree, and extends departments.kind with 'emergency' and 'theatre'. Each bed has a class (general, semi-private, private, ICU, HDU, NICU, PICU, day-care), a sex policy for bays (male, female, any), isolation capability, oxygen/monitor flags and a bed-day charge code from charge_catalogue. Beds can be blocked for maintenance with a reason. Deleting a bed that has ever held an admission is not allowed; it is retired instead. Bulk import by CSV covers a 50-200 bed nursing home in one go. Market variants: tariff currency comes from the regions table (INR/AED/SAR/QAR).

Given a bed that has held an admission, when the owner tries to delete it, then the API returns 409 BED_HAS_HISTORY and offers 'retire' instead
Given a CSV of 120 beds with 3 invalid rows, when imported in dry-run, then the preview shows 117 valid and 3 errors with row numbers and nothing is written until confirmed

Given a facility without the hospital entitlement, when any /v1/inpatient/setup endpoint is called, then the API returns 403 MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED

stories.title: Interface engine connects a partner HIS, RIS or PACS through HL7 v2 and FHIR R4
stories.story: As the hospital engineering team we want one inbound/outbound interface layer for ADT, orders and results (HL7 v2.5.1 and FHIR R4) so that any hospital module can run in partner mode and Nabd stays the patient-facing record.
stories.context: This is the seam that makes DEC-15 cheap either way. It unblocks ward, ER and radiology users in facilities that already run a HIS or PACS, and is the base for DICOM MWL in HOS-031. Inbound: ADT A01/A02/A03/A04/A08/A11/A13 and ORM/ORU (or FHIR Encounter/ServiceRequest/DiagnosticReport) are mapped onto Nabd admissions, orders and reports through the FHIR mapping layer (T-234). Outbound: Nabd events (admission, order, report) are rendered as HL7/FHIR messages. The engine runs as an integration adapter inside core (module 'integration' under shared/integration rules: HTTP clients only there, no open transaction) with an MLLP listener exposed only on the hospital's VPN/private link. Messages are stored encrypted with tenant keys, idempotent on message control ID, and retried with a dead-letter queue visible to platform ops. PHI never enters logs; message bodies are redacted in traces. Patient matching from partner MRN uses the existing patient registry with exact-identifier match only; anything fuzzy goes to a reconciliation queue for the MRD clerk.
source_refs: doc01 HIE table (HL7 v2.5.1 / FHIR R4)
acceptance: Given a partner HIS sends ADT^A01 for MRN SUV-IP-2288, when the message is received, then an admission is created or updated in Nabd within 5 s and ACK AA is returned
Given the same message control ID is delivered twice, when processed, then only one admission change is applied and the second gets ACK AA with no side effect
Given an inbound patient whose partner MRN does not exactly match a Nabd identifier, when processed, then a reconciliation item is created and no new patient is auto-created
Given a Nabd imaging order in partner mode, when it is signed, then an ORM^O01 (or FHIR ServiceRequest) is sent to the RIS within 10 s with the accession number
Given the partner endpoint is down, when 5 retries with backoff fail, then the message moves to dead-letter, an alert fires, and the owner's integrations card shows 'not sending'
Given any message, when logged, then logs contain only message type, control ID and tenant, never patient names or identifiers

stories.title: Ward nurse admits a patient into a suggested bed and prints the wristband
stories.story: As a ward nurse I want the system to suggest the best free bed and let me admit in a few taps, print a barcode wristband and notify the family, so that the patient is in bed fast and identified for every dose.

The wristband carries name, MRN, DOB, allergy flag and a Code 128/QR barcode of the admission id (no diagnosis). General admission consent is captured on a tablet (reuses T-303/T-138). stories.title: Ward nurse records observations and NEWS2/PEWS is scored and escalated automatically
stories.story: As a ward nurse I want to enter observations at the bedside and get the NEWS2 (adults) or PEWS (children) score, risk level and required response instantly so that deterioration is escalated without mental arithmetic.
stories.context: NEWS2 follows the Royal College of Physicians chart with SpO2 scale 1 by default and scale 2 selectable per patient by a doctor (hypercapnic respiratory failure). Bands are as in the prototype ipd.js: total >= 7 high (emergency response, continuous monitoring), 5-6 medium (urgent review, hourly obs), any single parameter scoring 3 low-medium (urgent ward review), 1-4 low (4-6 hourly). PEWS is used for patients under 16 (age cut-off configurable) with a facility-chosen PEWS chart. Scoring logic lives in packages/domain (shared TS) and is mirrored server-side in Java with a shared fixture table so UI preview and stored score never disagree. The score is never produced by an LLM. A high score pages the rapid response team via the in-app notification and SMS fallback through comms-gateway with no patient name in the SMS. Observation frequency due times drive an 'obs overdue' flag on the board. Existing vitals table is OPD-only (unique per queue_entry), so inpatient observations get their own time-series table.

Given a total NEWS2 >= 7, when saved, then the rapid response team is paged within 30 s and the escalation is logged with who was paged and when they acknowledged
Given a 4-year-old patient, when observations are entered, then PEWS is calculated and NEWS2 is not shown
Given the 300-case fixture table, when run against both the TS and Java scorers, then all 300 scores match exactly
Given observations are due 4-hourly and none recorded for 4 h 30 min, when the board refreshes, then the bed shows 'obs overdue'
Given a doctor switches the patient to SpO2 scale 2, when the next observation is saved, then scale 2 bands apply and the change is audited

stories.title: Ward nurse sees a medication round (MAR) built from the doctor's inpatient orders
stories.story: As a ward nurse I want the MAR to list every scheduled, PRN and STAT dose per patient by time slot, with overdue and held doses highlighted, so that I know exactly what to give on this round.

stories.title: OT coordinator books theatre cases against surgeons' unified calendars with zero clashes
stories.story: As the OT coordinator (ward persona, in-charge) I want to book a case into a theatre slot that checks the theatre, the surgeon's and the anaesthetist's calendars across facilities, so that no theatre or surgeon is ever double-booked.
stories.context: Theatres are departments of kind 'theatre' with rooms as service_points. A case has procedure, side/site, anaesthesia type, surgeon, anaesthetist, planned start/end, turnover time, blood requirement (links to HOS-037), implants and instrument sets (links CSSD HOS-040). Double-booking is prevented in the database by exclusion constraints on (theatre room, time range) and (staff, time range); surgeons' calendars at other facilities are read through the unified 'busy' calendar (T-247), which shows only busy blocks. Emergency add-on cases may bump elective cases with reason; bumped cases notify the surgeon and patient. Elective cases create an elective admission request (HOS-004) for the day before.

stories.title: ER nurse triages with ESI (or CTAS/MTS) in under 10 minutes with built-in stroke, chest-pain and sepsis screeners
stories.story: As the triage nurse I want a guided triage that takes vitals, chief complaint and expected resources and returns the ESI level, with automatic stroke (BE-FAST), chest-pain and sepsis (qSOFA) screeners, so that the sickest patient is seen first and pathways start at triage.
stories.context: ESI v4 decision points as in the prototype: A needs immediate life-saving intervention -> ESI 1; B high-risk / confused / severe pain or distress -> ESI 2; C number of expected resources (0 -> 5, 1 -> 4, 2+ -> 3, with danger-zone vitals bumping to 2). The scale is configurable per facility (ESI, CTAS or MTS; India often uses a 3-colour scale) and the facility must pick one; levels map to a common 1-5 priority. Screeners: BE-FAST positive suggests code stroke; chest pain with ECG request within 10 min; qSOFA >= 2 with suspected infection suggests sepsis bundle. Screeners suggest; the nurse activates. Re-triage timer (default 30 min) for waiting patients. Logic is deterministic in packages/domain with server mirror and fixtures; not an LLM. Target: triage within 10 min of door.
source_refs: T-375 AC 'triage with a standard scale (ESI/MTS)'

Given a patient with new confusion, fever and BP 92/56 and RR 24, when triaged, then qSOFA = 3 and the 'start sepsis bundle' suggestion appears with time zero = triage time
Given a stable patient needing 2+ resources with HR 112 (danger zone), when triaged, then ESI 2 is suggested with the reason 'danger-zone vitals'
Given the facility is configured for CTAS, when triaging, then CTAS questions are used and the result is stored with scale='CTAS'
Given a waiting ESI 3 patient triaged 30 min ago, when the re-triage timer fires, then the board highlights the patient for re-triage
Given the day's arrivals, when the report runs, then % triaged within 10 min of door is shown

Contraindication checklists (e.g. thrombolysis eligibility, antiplatelet allergy) read allergies live.

stories.title: ER doctor disposes a patient: admit, transfer out, discharge or LAMA
stories.story: As the ER doctor I want to record the disposition in one step (admit with a bed request, transfer to another facility with records shared, discharge with summary and Rx, or leave against medical advice with witness) so that the patient moves on and the board clears.
stories.context: Admit creates an admission request (HOS-004) with ESI, isolation needs and payer, and shows on the ward Admissions screen. Transfer-out books an ambulance (HOS-026) when needed and shares transfer note, vitals and results with the receiving facility through a time-limited Nabd consent (Exchange, CONS flow (a)) or a printed note if the receiver is not on Nabd. Discharge issues an ER summary (clinical_documents) and e-Rx, sends a secure link on WhatsApp, and passes to billing. LAMA requires capacity assessment, risks explained, patient signature or two staff witnesses if they refuse to sign; police are informed if MLC. Disposition time feeds ER length-of-stay metrics.

Given 'Transfer out' to a facility on Nabd, when confirmed, then a time-limited consent artefact is created and the receiving facility can read the transfer note, vitals and results only within the window
Given 'Discharge', when confirmed, then the ER summary and Rx are issued, a secure link is sent, and the visit leaves the board
Given 'LAMA' and the patient refuses to sign, when two staff witnesses confirm, then the disposition is saved with both witnesses and the risks text
Given an MLC patient leaving LAMA, when saved, then the MLC record is updated and the police-intimation task is created
