stories.title: Doctor orders imaging from the consult, ward or ER with contrast, renal, pregnancy and implant checks
stories.story: As a doctor I want to order X-ray, USG, CT or MRI from the consult, ward round or ER with clinical indication and priority, and have the system check contrast allergy, renal function, pregnancy and MRI implants, so that unsafe studies are caught before the patient reaches the scanner.
stories.context: Order chips already exist in the prototype consult. Checks: contrast allergy from patient_allergies (live, never cached); eGFR from the last creatinine within 30 days (threshold configurable, e.g. < 30 flags), with 'life-threatening: do not wait for creatinine' override for STAT; pregnancy status from patient_pregnancy_status (V52) for women 12-50 and ionising studies; MRI safety screening (implants, pacemaker) as a questionnaire. Obstetric USG in India is PCPNDT-gated (HOS-034). An accession number is assigned at order (per-facility series) and is the key across RIS/PACS. Priority: STAT, urgent, routine. Charges go to the bill (OPD) or charge capture (IPD, HOS-008). In partner mode (HOS-002) orders go to the partner RIS via HOS-003.

Given a 28-year-old woman with pregnancy status 'pregnant', when ordering CT, then the warning suggests USG/MRI alternatives and needs acknowledgement

stories.title: Modalities pull the worklist over DICOM MWL and studies open in the PACS viewer from Nabd
stories.story: As a radiographer I want the CT/X-ray/USG console to pull patient and study details from Nabd over DICOM Modality Worklist and report completion via MPPS, and as a radiologist I want to open the study in the PACS viewer from the report screen, so that nobody retypes demographics and images stay in PACS.
stories.context: Nabd never stores images (prototype: 'images stay in PACS'). Integration options, both behind the imaging PACS port so DEC-15 works either way: (a) bundled open-source PACS (Orthanc with the DICOMweb and worklist plugins) per regional cell, or (b) the hospital's existing PACS/RIS. Nabd provides MWL C-FIND (via Orthanc worklist plugin fed by Nabd or a lightweight MWL SCP in the integration gateway), receives MPPS N-CREATE/N-SET to mark in_progress/acquired, and queries studies by accession via DICOMweb QIDO-RS to store the StudyInstanceUID. Viewer launch builds a URL for the configured viewer (OHIF or vendor) with a short-lived token; no PHI in URL query beyond study UID. The DICOM gateway runs on-premises or in a private link at the hospital because modalities speak DIMSE on the LAN; it connects outbound to the regional cell over mTLS. Patient name/ID in MWL uses the Nabd MRN; character set ISO_IR 192 for Arabic/Indic names.

stories.title: Radiologist communicates a critical finding with read-back and automatic escalation
stories.story: As a radiologist I want to flag a critical finding (category 1/2/3), call the responsible clinician, record their read-back, and have the system escalate if nobody acknowledges in time, so that no critical result is missed.

Categories and time limits configurable (example: Cat 1 within 30 min by phone, Cat 2 within 2 h, Cat 3 incidental within 24 h by inbox). Escalation chain: ordering doctor -> covering doctor -> department head/ER in-charge. Nabd pages via in-app and SMS without PHI; the call itself happens by phone and is documented.

stories.title: Clinical reads stop returning a patient who withdrew consent or is outside the doctor's own-patients scope
stories.story: As a patient I want my clinical record to disappear from every clinical screen once I withdraw processing consent, and to be visible only to the doctors allowed to see it, so that my choice and the clinic's access rules are enforced by the server and not by the UI.

stories.title: Migrations follow an expand/contract playbook enforced by a CI migration lint, with a generated ERD
stories.story: As an engineer I want every migration checked against zero-downtime rules in CI so that a deploy during OPD hours never locks queue_entries or breaks the running pods.
stories.context: DP-12 found CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY (V83, V43, V53, V60), CHECK swaps without NOT VALID on the hottest table (V5, V37, V39), full-table backfills inside the migration transaction followed by SET NOT NULL, destructive drops in the same release (V5, V39, V40) and version gaps (V49, V56-59, ...) with out-of-order disabled. The playbook (docs/architecture/migration-playbook.md) states the rules; a lint in CI stage 4 enforces them; versions are allocated centrally (next free number reserved in a VERSIONS file checked by CI) so parallel squads never collide. The schema doc and ERD are generated from the catalog on every main build, replacing the PDF that covers 12 of 86 tables (DP-31). stories.title: Tenant isolation is enforced by the database: split roles, FORCE RLS with per-command policies, timeouts and a prod-config CI job
stories.story: As a clinic owner (and DPO) I want the database itself to refuse cross-tenant access so that a single coding mistake can never show my patients to another clinic.
stories.context: MF-03: the app role runs Flyway and owns every table, so RLS is inert in deployment; no policy is FORCEd; seven tenant tables have no RLS and brand policies are USING-only (MF-63, QA-40). ADR-07 fixes this: nabd_migrator owns schemas and runs Flyway as a separate job, nabd_app is DML-only NOBYPASSRLS with statement_timeout=5s, lock_timeout=3s, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=15s, nabd_reports is read-only with 60 s. Every tenant_id table gets FORCE RLS with per-command policies: USING tenant_id = ANY(app.visible_tenant_ids) and WITH CHECK tenant_id = app.tenant_id. The app refuses to boot if the invariant is broken, and a prod-config CI job migrates as nabd_migrator and runs the whole API suite as nabd_app. Hikari gets explicit settings (15-20 connections, 3 s connection timeout, leak detection 10 s) so pool exhaustion fails fast. Unblocks the Phase 0 exit gate (B-25 isolated tenant records) and every later story that relies on RLS.

stories.title: Synced tables carry change_seq and updated_at so screens and apps can fetch only what changed
stories.story: As an engineer I want every table that a cache, SSE projection or app syncs to carry a monotonic change_seq so that ETags, SSE version gates and delta sync are possible.
stories.context: DP-19: 39 tables lack updated_at, including mutable invoices, prescriptions, procedure_orders, waitlist_entries and vitals, which blocks ETag/304, the SSE 'apply only if v > current' rule and the patient app's delta sync. A per-table change_seq from one sequence is assigned by a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger with an index (tenant_id, change_seq). stories.context: QA-36/QA-34/MF-35: there is no CI, the Dockerfile builds with -DskipTests, Testcontainers 1.19.8 fails on Docker Engine 29 (459/560 tests error), tsc fails on a fresh checkout before next typegen, and test-consult-flow.mjs is not wired. doc06 §7.1 stages: 1 Static (Spotless/Checkstyle, SpotBugs, next typegen + tsc + ESLint, gitleaks, Semgrep/CodeQL; <= 3 min), 2 Unit (JUnit, Vitest/node test incl. consult flow, ArchUnit; <= 2 min), 3 Integration (Testcontainers parallel by class, JaCoCo; <= 6 min), 6 Build and scan (non-root distroless image, Trivy, OWASP Dependency-Check, npm audit --audit-level=high, CycloneDX SBOM, cosign signature; <= 4 min). Path filters per area. Branch protection: required checks, CODEOWNERS review for clinical/, auth/iam, db/migrations and infra/, signed commits, no direct pushes (old NB-297). Images are built once and promoted by digest (ADR-15). T-014 (Frontend) adds the Next.js upgrade and npm SBOM; this story owns the pipeline that runs it.
acceptance: Given Docker Engine 29, when mvn test runs in CI, then all 560+ tests pass without docker-java overrides (Testcontainers >= 1.21 pinned in backend/pom.xml)
Given a fresh checkout, when stage 1 runs, then next typegen && tsc --noEmit passes and scripts/test-consult-flow.mjs runs in npm test
Given a PR, when stages 1, 2, 3 and 6 run, then they finish within 3, 2, 6 and 4 min respectively and all are required checks on main
Given a committed secret pattern (AWS key, private key, Meta token), when gitleaks runs, then the PR fails
Given a new High or Critical finding from Semgrep/CodeQL, Trivy, Dependency-Check or npm audit, when stage 1/6 runs, then the PR fails (existing findings baselined with owners and dates)
Given a merge to main, when the image is built, then tests ran in the same pipeline, the image is cosign-signed with an attached CycloneDX SBOM and deploys reference it by digest
Given a direct push to main or a PR touching clinical/ without a clinical CODEOWNER approval, when attempted, then it is rejected
nfr: Runners use OIDC to the cloud; no long-lived secrets in CI
Flaky policy: >= 2/20 reruns failing -> quarantined with owner, 5-day SLA
tests: CI self-test: a seeded failing test and a seeded secret on a canary branch must fail the pipeline

stories.title: Coverage and mutation gates prove safety and billing rules are really tested
stories.story: As an engineer I want coverage reported on every PR and nightly mutation testing on the safety and billing rules so that a green suite actually means the allergy, pregnancy and tax rules are checked.
stories.context: There is no coverage measurement and no mutation testing. JaCoCo baseline first (S1), reported per PR with new-code >= 80%; gates later: backend >= 75% overall and >= 90% line / 85% branch on RxSafetyChecks, AllergyDrugClasses, PrescriptionService, CheckoutService and iam.*. PIT runs nightly on the safety and billing rule classes with a score >= 85% (>= 90% on AllergyDrugClasses per QA §4.6) and a drop of more than 2 points blocks the next merge to those packages.

Given the safety/billing class list, when coverage is below 90% line or 85% branch, then the build fails (gate enabled when baseline reaches it, date recorded)
Given the nightly PIT job, when it runs on RxSafetyChecks, AllergyDrugClasses, PrescriptionService rules, CheckoutService.computeTotals and tax classes, then the score is published and >= 85%
Given the PIT score drops more than 2 points from the last green run, when the next PR touches those packages, then it is blocked until the score recovers

stories.title: Module boundaries and the tenant-predicate rule are enforced in CI (report-only, then blocking)
stories.story: As an engineer I want module boundaries, SQL table ownership and 'tenant_id in every statement' checked automatically so that the modular monolith does not decay and no query relies on RLS alone.
stories.context: ADR-02: ApplicationModules.verify(), ArchUnit rules from ARCH §11.2 (no cycles; internal reachable only from its own module; controllers never touch repositories or JdbcTemplate; @Transactional only in services; HTTP clients only in integration; shared kernel is a leaf; platform isolated), a SQL-ownership scan (a module writes only its own tables and reads only its allow-list from docs/architecture/table-ownership.yaml) and a tenant-predicate scan (every SQL on an RLS table has tenant_id = ? — DP-02 found QueueRepository.java:42 and ScheduleRepository.java:135-151 without it). Report-only from S2 with a published violation trend; blocking for new code at S5; blocking for all code by the Phase 1 exit (S8).
acceptance: Given stage 2, when it runs in S2-S4, then a violations report (Modulith, ArchUnit, SQL ownership, tenant predicate) is published per PR with counts by module and does not fail the build
Given a PR in S5-S7 that adds a new violation, when stage 2 runs, then it fails; existing violations are listed in a frozen baseline file
Given the Phase 1 exit (S8), when stage 2 runs, then the baseline is empty and any violation fails the build
Given a repository SQL string on queue_entries without a tenant_id predicate, when scanned, then it is reported with file and line
Given docs/architecture/table-ownership.yaml, when a module writes a table it does not own, then the SQL-ownership scan reports it

CI: baseline shrink tracked weekly at the architecture review

stories.title: The API spec is generated from code, cleaned of phantom operations and diffed on every PR

ADR-10 bootstrap: add springdoc-openapi, generate the spec in CI, review it module by module, commit it as api/openapi/core.yaml (plus internal.yaml), remove phantom operations, and run oasdiff on every PR in report mode (comment only). Enum values become string-literal unions; Problem+JSON error schemas shared.

stories.title: Every PR gets a preview environment with synthetic tenants, destroyed after 72 hours
stories.story: As an engineer and reviewer I want a disposable environment per PR seeded with realistic synthetic clinics so that ZAP, Playwright and Schemathesis run against the real stack and reviewers can click through changes.
stories.context: ADR-15 / doc06 §7.1 stage 7. Each PR deploys Core (+ BFF, + Comms/Edge stubs) into an ephemeral namespace or app with its own Postgres (Testcontainers-style managed instance or a schema-per-preview on a shared non-prod cluster), seeded by a synthetic data generator: IN/AE/SA/QA tenants, staff per RBAC role, patients with Indian/Arabic names, test-range phones, fake ids with checksum disabled (QA §5.3). A pre-load scanner rejects anything that looks like a real national id or a phone outside test ranges. URL and role logins posted to the PR; destroyed after 72 h or on merge; no backups of non-prod.
acceptance: Given a PR, when stage 7 starts, then a preview with Core, BFF and stubs is reachable within 8 min and its URL plus per-role test logins are posted on the PR

Given the preview is up, when the Playwright smoke (J1 < 45 s, J5 sign < 2 s, J6 warning < 500 ms, J9 < 60 s) and axe run, then failures or critical/serious axe violations on changed pages block the merge
Given the synthetic seed, when loaded, then each preview has 4 tenants (IN, AE, SA, QA), one staff per RBAC role, 2,000 patients and a day of appointments; all phones are in reserved test ranges
Given a dataset containing a real-looking Aadhaar (valid Verhoeff) or a non-test phone, when the pre-load scanner runs, then the load is rejected
Given a preview older than 72 h or a merged/closed PR, when the reaper runs, then all its resources are destroyed and cost tags show zero
Given preview credentials, when inspected, then they are short-lived and the preview cannot reach prod networks or prod secrets

stories.title: Token-misuse matrix: every token type against every endpoint returns 401 unless it is the token's own endpoint

First suite in doc06 §7.4.

stories.title: Two receptionists at once can never create two tokens, two bookings or lost payments (concurrency suite v1)
stories.story: As a receptionist working beside a colleague I want the system proven safe when we act on the same appointment, slot or invoice at the same moment so that we never double check-in a patient or lose a payment.
stories.context: Only 3 of 64 test classes use threads. doc06 §7.4 #3: CountDownLatch suites verifying the Sprint 1 integrity fixes (T-030 atomic payments, T-034 queue CAS, T-035 arrived status, T-036 booking EXCLUDE): double check-in -> exactly one 201; concurrent payments keep paid = SUM(payments); overlapping bookings -> one success; concurrent status transitions -> one success; plus audit chain under 50 parallel writes (no fork) and refund approve race. Runs in stage 3 with a fixed thread pool and deterministic barriers.

Given two payments of 300 and 200 on a 500 invoice recorded concurrently, when both complete, then paid = 500 = SUM(invoice_payments) and status = paid
Given two bookings overlapping 10:00 and 10:05 for one doctor (15 min slots), when concurrent, then exactly one succeeds
Given 10 concurrent status transitions from the same state, when executed, then exactly one succeeds and the rest get 409
Given 50 parallel audited writes in one tenant, when complete, then verify_audit_chain returns NULL (no fork)
Given the suite, when run 20 times in CI, then it is never flaky (0/20 failures)

stories.title: Audited writes never queue behind each other: audit chain head is indexed and load-verified
stories.story: As a doctor saving notes and prescriptions during a busy clinic I want audited writes not to wait on each other so that signing stays under 2 seconds even when the whole clinic is writing.
stories.context: DP-05: audit_log_chain() finds the previous hash with ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE filtered only by RLS — 5,041 ms for a quiet tenant at 3M rows — and holds the lock until the business transaction commits, serialising every audited write within a tenant. RETURNING, UTC hashing and nightly verify. This story verifies performance under load and, if contention remains above budget, implements DP-05's next step: insert unchained rows in the business transaction and have one per-region sealer chain them asynchronously within seconds (keeping verify_audit_chain semantics) — the same batch-sealing model DEC-22 recommends for phi_read_log.

stories.title: Counter refuses to sell a prescription-only item unless it is linked to a signed prescription
stories.story: As a pharmacist (or the receptionist who dispenses in a hybrid clinic) I want the counter sale and the visit checkout to refuse any prescription-only line that is not linked to a signed prescription line so that we never hand out alprazolam or antibiotics over the counter by mistake.

stories.title: Analyser results arrive over HL7 v2 or ASTM through a small lab bridge
stories.story: As a lab technician I want results from our analysers to arrive in Nabd automatically by sample barcode so that I never retype numbers and transcription errors disappear.

stories.title: Only full access tokens open the API: separate token types and audiences
stories.story: As a clinic owner responsible for patient data, I want challenge and purpose tokens to be useless as bearer credentials so that a stolen or guessed PIN can never bypass MFA.
stories.context: Today every token AuthService mints (staff access, mfa_pending, mfa_setup_required, step_up), OwnerService's owner_pending_workspace and PlatformAuthService's operator tokens are signed by the same key and accepted by the resource server (SecurityConfig.java:94). SessionRevocationJwtDecoder passes through any token without sid+tenantId, so an mfa_pending token issued after the PIN step reaches MFA enrol, break-glass activate and unlock (MF-01, Critical). The fix adds a mandatory `typ` claim (access | mfa_pending | mfa_setup | step_up | owner_select) and an `aud` claim (staff-api | platform-api | mfa | step-up | owner-select) to every mint site, makes the resource-server decoder accept only typ=access, and decodes challenge tokens only inside the controller that consumes them with a dedicated decoder. Every non-public endpoint must also see either a `sid` claim or a granted authority. Tokens minted before the deploy lack `typ` and are rejected; access tokens live 15 minutes and refresh still works, so users see at most one silent refresh. This is a prerequisite for break-glass gating (PLT-012), MFA hardening (PLT-004/005) and ADR-08.
acceptance: Given a staff member with MFA enabled who has entered a correct PIN, when the returned mfa_pending token is sent as `Authorization: Bearer` to any of the authenticated endpoints, then every call returns 401 (TokenMisuseMatrixTest enumerates all request mappings).
Given an mfa_pending challenge token, when it is posted to /v1/auth/mfa/verify with a valid TOTP, then a token pair with typ=access, aud=staff-api and a sid is returned.

Given a step_up token or an owner_select token, when used as a bearer token, then 401; when sent in X-Step-Up-Token to a step-up-protected action, then it is accepted only if its sub matches the caller.
Given a token without a typ claim (minted before the deploy), when presented, then 401 and the client's single-flight refresh obtains a new typed token without sending the user to /login.
Given an authenticated endpoint with no @PreAuthorize (/v1/auth/logout, /v1/auth/sessions, /v1/owners/me/workspaces), when called with a typ=access token lacking sid, then 401.
Given the CI pipeline, when any new controller method is added, then TokenMisuseMatrixTest discovers it automatically and fails the build if a non-access token is accepted.

stories.title: Signing keys survive deploys: keys from the secret manager, JWKS with two active kids
stories.story: As a receptionist I want to stay signed in when Nabd deploys or restarts a server so that a release in the middle of the morning rush never logs the desk out.
stories.context: config/JwtConfig.java generates a fresh RSA-2048 key pair with a random kid on every boot (MF-13). Every deploy logs everybody out, a second replica rejects the first replica's tokens, there is no JWKS, and iss/aud are not validated. The fix loads the signing keys from the cell's secret manager (KMS-protected), publishes a JWKS containing the active and the next/previous kid so rotation overlaps, and validates iss/aud/typ on every decode. The dev profile may still generate an ephemeral key, but the prod profile fails to boot without configured keys. This unblocks two replicas behind a load balancer (Phase 0 exit gate) and the separate issuers in PLT-009.
acceptance: Given two replicas behind the load balancer, when a user signs in on replica A and the next request lands on replica B, then it succeeds (restart/refresh test QA-37).

Given a rolling restart of both replicas, when a signed-in receptionist keeps working, then nobody is logged out and no request returns 401 except a normal 15-minute expiry followed by a silent refresh.
Given GET /.well-known/jwks.json, then it returns exactly 2 active keys (current and next/previous kid) and no private material.
Given a token with the wrong iss, wrong aud, unknown kid or missing typ, then decode fails with 401.
Given SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod and no JWT key configuration, when the app boots, then startup fails with a clear error naming the missing secret.
Given the rotation runbook, when the next key is promoted, then tokens signed with the previous kid stay valid until they expire (overlap >= refresh TTL of the access token, 15 min).

stories.title: Brute-force limits on TOTP and unlock, 6-digit PINs, and a client IP that cannot be forged
stories.story: As a receptionist on a shared desk PC I want my account protected against someone guessing my PIN or authenticator code so that nobody can sign in as me.
stories.context: TOTP verification (AuthService.verifyMfa, issueStepUpToken, confirmMfa) has no attempt counter, so once a PIN is known the second factor can be guessed across re-issued challenges (MF-09). /v1/auth/unlock is an unthrottled PIN oracle, PINs are 4-6 digits, and RequestMeta.clientIp() returns the first X-Forwarded-For value, so the per-IP throttle (20/min) and audit IPs can be forged and a malformed header causes a 500 on the ::inet cast (MF-10). The fix counts failed PIN, OTP, TOTP, unlock and recovery-code attempts per account in `login_attempts` and drives the existing exponential lockout (capped at 30 min, non-renewing) from all of them; adds TOTP replay protection (a used time-step cannot be reused); raises the PIN policy to 6-8 digits with a forced change at next login for shorter PINs; and derives the client IP from Tomcat's RemoteIpValve with a trusted-proxy list. Owner and operator passphrases are behind a decision (see risks).
acceptance: Given an account with a known PIN, when 5 wrong TOTP codes are submitted across any number of fresh challenges, then the account is locked with the same backoff as PIN failures and further correct codes are refused until the lock expires (TotpLockoutTest).
Given /v1/auth/unlock, when 5 wrong PINs are posted, then the session is locked and the 6th attempt returns 423 without verifying the PIN (UnlockBruteForceTest).
Given a valid TOTP code already used for a sign-in, when it is replayed within its 30 s window, then it is rejected.

Given a staff member whose PIN has 4 or 5 digits, when they sign in successfully, then they must set a 6-8 digit PIN before any other call succeeds; invite accept and PIN reset reject PINs shorter than 6 digits with 400.
Given a request carrying `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4` from a non-trusted hop, then rate limits and the audit_log ip_address use the real peer address (XffSpoofTest).
Given `X-Forwarded-For: not-an-ip`, then the request never returns 500 and the audit row stores the validated peer IP.

stories.title: MFA re-enrolment needs the current factor, recovery codes work, and an owner can reset a lost authenticator
stories.story: As a doctor who lost my phone I want to sign in once with a recovery code, and have my owner reset my authenticator safely, so that I am not locked out of my clinic and nobody else can silently replace my MFA.
stories.context: MFA re-enrolment overwrites the active secret without proof of the current factor, recovery codes accumulate on every enrolment and are never consumed (consumeRecoveryCode has no caller), and there is no admin reset (MF-08). The fix stores a pending secret alongside the active one, so the old secret keeps working until the new one is confirmed; re-enrolment of an enabled account requires the current TOTP or a step-up token; confirming rotates the recovery-code set (old unused codes are revoked); the MFA challenge accepts a single-use recovery code; and an owner (staff:edit + step-up) can reset another staff member's MFA, which is audited, revokes that person's sessions and forces enrolment at next sign-in. Operators get the same flow on master.operators.

Given re-enrolment started, when the user signs in before confirming, then the old authenticator still works (pending secret is not active).
Given confirmation of a new secret, then exactly 8 new recovery codes are shown once and all previously unused codes stop working.
Given an MFA challenge, when a valid recovery code is submitted, then the session is issued, the code is marked used and cannot be reused, and the owner sees an audit entry 'recovery code used'.
Given an owner with step-up, when they reset a doctor's MFA, then an audit row `staff.mfa_reset` is written, the doctor's sessions are revoked within 60 s and the next sign-in forces enrolment.
Given a receptionist (no staff:edit), when they call the reset endpoint, then 403.

stories.title: OTP requests are limited per phone number and never reveal whether a number exists
stories.story: As the Nabd platform team I want OTP sends limited per phone number with a silent response so that nobody can pump paid WhatsApp/SMS messages or discover which numbers are registered.
stories.context: POST /v1/auth/otp/request has no per-number limit (MF-24 S2 part); only the forgeable per-IP limit applies, which enables message pumping (each OTP costs a WhatsApp authentication template) and account enumeration through response differences. The fix adds a Postgres counter keyed by an HMAC of the normalised phone number (no raw phone stored) with SYS-01 rules: at most 3 sends per 15 minutes and 10 per 24 hours per number, resend no sooner than 60 s, and a per-tenant hourly cap. The endpoint always returns 202 with the same body and similar latency whether the number exists, is limited, or is unknown. PLT-008 later moves the counters to Valkey token buckets; this Postgres version is the Phase 0 control and the fallback if Valkey is unavailable.

Given a resend within 60 s of the previous send, then no message is sent and the response is 202.

Given a pumping script that rotates 1,000 numbers against one tenant within an hour, then sends stop at the per-tenant cap (default 200/h, configurable per plan) and an alert is raised to the platform team.

stories.title: Sessions end when they should: suspension, role change, operator logout and a 12-hour cap
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want suspending a staff member, changing their role, or suspending the clinic to end their sessions within a minute so that access stops the moment I decide it should.
stories.context: Revocation has gaps (MF-60): operator tokens carry sid but no tenantId so SessionRevocationJwtDecoder skips the liveness check; tenant suspension/offboarding (TenantLifecycleService ~L44-56) revokes nothing; refresh() and owner workspace select do not check tenant status; PATCH /v1/staff/{id} role changes do not revoke; refresh rotation gives a fresh 30-day expiry forever (no absolute lifetime); and step-up tokens are not bound to the session or tenant. The fix checks operator tokens against master.sessions, revokes all tenant sessions on suspension/offboarding, rejects refresh and workspace select for non-active tenants, revokes a staff member's sessions on any role/scope/field-grant change, caps each refresh family at about one shift (12 h, configurable per tenant later by SSO policy), and binds step-up tokens to sid and tenantId. Revocations publish an event so open tabs are signed out via SSE.
acceptance: Given an operator who logs out, when their access token is used 10 s later, then 401 (liveness checked against master.sessions).

Given a tenant moved to suspended or offboarded, then every staff session in that tenant is revoked within 60 s, refresh returns 401 TENANT_INACTIVE and owner workspace select returns 403 TENANT_INACTIVE.
Given an owner changes a receptionist's role or scope, then the receptionist's open tabs are signed out within 60 s and the next sign-in carries the new permissions.
Given a refresh family started 12 h ago, when refresh is attempted, then 401 SESSION_MAX_AGE and the user signs in again (idle-lock unlock does not extend the cap).
Given a step-up token minted in session A, when presented with session B's access token, then 403 STEP_UP_INVALID.
Given suspension of one staff member via one tap, then all their sessions on all devices end (NB-047).

stories.title: Rate limits per tenant, user, phone and IP that hold across replicas
stories.story: As the Nabd platform team I want token-bucket rate limits per tenant, user, phone and IP shared across replicas so that one abusive client or tenant cannot degrade every clinic's morning rush.
stories.context: Rate limits cover auth only and the per-IP counter was forgeable (MF-24 S3 part, NB-288). With Valkey in-region (T-080, Data & Infra), this story adds Bucket4j-style token buckets in Valkey keyed `rl:{dim}:{id}`: per tenant for the whole API (default 600 req/min, burst 1,200, raised per plan), per user/session (120 req/min), per IP for pre-auth and public endpoints (20 req/min), and per phone HMAC for OTP (migrating PLT-006 rules). Limits return 429 Problem+JSON with Retry-After, except OTP endpoints, which stay silent 202. If Valkey is unavailable the tenant/user limits fail open with an alert, while OTP limits fall back to the Postgres counter from PLT-006 (fail closed). Patient Access Edge applies the same library at its own ingress.
acceptance: Given a tenant exceeding 1,200 requests in a burst, when the next request arrives, then 429 with Retry-After and a Problem type `rate_limited`, and other tenants on the same replica are unaffected.
Given two replicas behind the load balancer, when a load test drives one user at 300 req/min split across both, then the user limit of 120 req/min holds within 5%.
Given OTP requests over the per-number limit, then the response is still 202 and nothing is sent.
Given Valkey is stopped, then API calls continue (tenant/user limits fail open, alert fires within 2 min) and OTP limits are enforced from Postgres.
Given a plan with a higher API quota (PLT-059), then the tenant bucket uses the plan's limit within 60 s of the plan change.

ui.notes: api-client honours Retry-After with jittered backoff; shows a non-blocking 'Busy, retrying' toast.

nfr: Limiter adds < 2 ms p95 (one Valkey round trip, pipelined)
Keys never contain raw phone numbers or user names
Limits configurable per plan without deploy
tests: load: k6 two-replica limiter accuracy test
chaos: Valkey down => fail-open/closed behaviour per dimension
stories.risks: Depends on managed Valkey in the India region (T-080, doc06 D5).

stories.title: Separate issuers, keys and filter chains for staff, owner and operator tokens
stories.story: As the Nabd platform team I want staff, owner and operator tokens signed by different keys with different issuers and audiences, each accepted only on its own URL prefix, so that a token from one population can never be replayed against another.
stories.context: Staff, owner and operator tokens share one key, issuer and authority namespace, and the control plane shares the clinic ingress (MF-61 S5 part, ARCH-17, ARCH-39). After PLT-001 and PLT-002 this story gives each population its own key set and issuer (…/staff, …/owner, …/platform), defines per-prefix Spring Security filter chains (/v1/platform/** accepts only aud=platform-api from the platform key set; /v1/** accepts only aud=staff-api; /internal/v1/** is reserved for service identity with aud=internal), prefixes operator authorities with `platform:` so the two permission vocabularies cannot overlap, and moves platform package data access to a separate DataSource role (nabd_control) so the clinic runtime role nabd_app loses all DML on master.*. This is the last step before the Control Plane is extracted (PLT-061).
acceptance: Given an operator access token, when it calls any /v1/** clinic endpoint, then 401 (cross-population matrix test).
Given a staff access token, when it calls any /v1/platform/** endpoint, then 401.
Given an owner_select token, when used anywhere other than /v1/owners/workspaces/select, then 401.
Given the database, then nabd_app has no privileges on schema master and the platform package connects as nabd_control (RlsSchemaInvariantTest extended).

Given JWKS, then each population publishes its own two active kids at /.well-known/jwks.json?population=staff|owner|platform (or separate paths), and rotating one population's key does not affect the others.

stories.title: Enterprise sign-in with OIDC single sign-on per tenant
stories.story: As the IT head of a hospital chain I want my staff to sign in to Nabd with our company identity provider over OIDC so that joiners and leavers are controlled in one place and our MFA policy applies.
stories.context: Enterprise review requires SSO (EP40, PS-04, persona P16). This story adds per-tenant OIDC (Azure AD/Entra, Google Workspace, Okta) using authorization code + PKCE, with state and nonce, through the staff-web BFF. Staff are matched by a stable external subject (or verified email on first link), optionally just-in-time provisioned into a default role, and the IdP's MFA claim (amr/acr) is accepted only if the tenant's policy says so; otherwise Nabd TOTP is still required. A tenant can enforce SSO, which disables PIN sign-in for everyone except one designated owner break-glass account. Phase 5 only, and only if the founder confirms the enterprise tier (DEC-39: the old plan NFR-06 forbade SSO).
acceptance: Given a tenant with OIDC configured and enforced, when a staff member opens the sign-in page and enters their work email, then they are redirected to the IdP and land in Nabd signed in within 10 s of IdP approval.
Given the IdP returns amr without mfa and the tenant policy is 'idp_mfa_required', then sign-in stops with a clear message and no session is created.
Given SSO is enforced, when anyone except the designated owner break-glass account tries PIN sign-in, then 403 SSO_REQUIRED.
Given a user disabled in the IdP, then their next refresh fails within the session cap (PLT-007) and back-channel logout (if supported) revokes sessions within 60 s.
Given JIT provisioning on, when a new IdP user signs in, then a staff row is created in the configured default role (never Owner) and an audit row is written.
Given state or nonce mismatch, or an id_token from an issuer not configured for the tenant, then 401 and an audit row `auth.sso_rejected`.

stories.title: Enterprise sign-in with SAML 2.0 and back-channel deprovisioning
stories.story: As the IT head of a hospital group that only runs a SAML IdP I want Nabd to accept SAML sign-in and remove access when we disable someone so that enterprise procurement passes.
stories.context: Many GCC and Indian hospital groups run ADFS or older IdPs that speak only SAML 2.0. This story extends PLT-010 with SP-initiated SAML (signed AuthnRequests, signed assertions required, audience and recipient checks, replay cache of assertion IDs), IdP metadata upload with certificate rollover, and a deprovisioning path: either SCIM 2.0 Users PATCH active=false or a scheduled IdP-side check, which suspends the staff row and revokes sessions. The same enforce-SSO, JIT and MFA-policy rules from PLT-010 apply.
acceptance: Given a tenant with SAML metadata uploaded, when a staff member signs in, then a signed assertion with the correct audience and recipient creates a session; an unsigned or wrongly-audienced assertion returns 401.
Given the same assertion ID is replayed within its validity, then 401 SAML_REPLAY.
Given the IdP rotates its signing certificate with overlap, then sign-in keeps working during the overlap after metadata refresh.
Given a SCIM PATCH active=false for a user, then the staff row is suspended and all their sessions are revoked within 60 s.
Given SCIM requests without the tenant's bearer secret, then 401 and an audit row.

stories.title: Break-glass is an eligible clinician's 30-minute, read-only emergency access that the owner hears about at once
stories.story: As an emergency doctor I want to open a patient's record in an emergency outside my normal scope with one justified, step-up-confirmed action, and as the owner I want to be told within a minute, so that emergencies are never blocked but break-glass is never a back door to Owner rights.
stories.context: POST /v1/auth/break-glass/activate has no @PreAuthorize (AuthController ~L126-130); any authenticated caller, including an mfa_pending token, gets the tenant's full built-in Owner grant set folded into a new token for 30 minutes (AuthService.mintTokenPair ~L560-572 via repo.findBuiltInOwnerRole), and can then create a 30-day self-delegation. Deactivate is also ungated (MF-02, SEC-36). The fix adds a dedicated `clinical:breakGlass` authority (new ModuleGrant action, seeded only for Doctor, Owner-doctor and ER roles), requires a step-up token with purpose break_glass, requires a reason code plus free text (text stored, never logged), replaces the Owner grant merge with a fixed BREAK_GLASS_GRANTS set (clinical:view, patients:view; no create/edit/delete/approve/staff), lets the token bypass own-patients and department scoping for reads only, hard-expires at 30 minutes, and notifies every Owner in-app and on WhatsApp (no PHI in the body) within 60 s. Deactivate is limited to the grant holder or staff:edit (quick win #11). Break-glass v2 (per-patient Cedar context flag, ADR-08) replaces the scope later.
acceptance: Given a receptionist, when they call break-glass activate, then 403 (BreakGlassAuthzTest).

Given a doctor with clinical:breakGlass but no step-up token, then 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED; with a valid step-up token and reason code, then 201 and a token whose permissions are exactly the base grants plus clinical:view and patients:view (no staff:edit, no billing, no :approve).

Given an activation, then every Owner of the tenant receives an in-app alert and a WhatsApp utility message ('Emergency access used by <staff name> at <time>. Review in Nabd.') within 60 s, with no patient name or diagnosis.

Given the break-glass token, when a write endpoint (POST/PATCH/DELETE on clinical, staff, roles, billing) is called, then 403; a clinical GET on a patient outside own-patients scope succeeds and is logged with purpose break_glass (PLT-039).
Given 30 minutes after activation, then the grant is expired, the elevated session is revoked and further calls with that token return 401 (J14).
Given a staff member who is not the holder and lacks staff:edit, when they deactivate someone else's grant, then 403.

stories.title: Owner reviews every break-glass use with what was read, and the device is recorded
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want a review queue of every emergency access, showing who, why, from which device and exactly which records were opened, so that I can confirm it was justified or escalate it within a day.
stories.context: Founder brief B-31 asks for break-glass 'with justification and review'. PLT-012 gates and notifies; this story closes the loop. Each grant appears in an owner review queue with the reason, the device label, and the list of records read during the window (from phi_read_log, PLT-039). The owner marks it justified or not justified; 'not justified' opens an incident note and can revoke the clinician's breakGlass permission in one step. Unreviewed grants trigger a reminder after 24 h. The client now sends a real device label header (X-Device-Label, e.g. 'Front desk PC 2') instead of the User-Agent (T-204, MF-80/QA-41), and it is stored on sessions and break-glass grants.
acceptance: Given a break-glass grant that ended, then it appears in the owner's review queue within 1 minute with reason, device label, start/end and the list of patients and record types read during the window.
Given the owner marks a grant 'not justified', then the outcome is audited, an incident note is created, and the owner can remove clinical:breakGlass from that staff member in the same dialog.
Given a grant unreviewed for 24 h, then the owner gets one reminder in-app and on WhatsApp.

Given the staff-web client, when it signs in or activates break-glass, then it sends X-Device-Label (max 64 chars, sanitised) and the value is stored in sessions.device_label and break_glass_grants.device_label instead of the User-Agent.
Given a receptionist, when they open the review queue, then 403 (permission compliance:view or staff:edit required).

stories.title: Nobody can delegate rights to themselves or pass on rights they only borrowed
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want delegations to be granted only by someone else, only from their own permanent role, so that no one can turn a temporary or emergency right into a 30-day Owner role.
stories.context: RoleService.createDelegation (~L101-115) checks the delegated role against the caller's token grants, which include delegated and break-glass grants, and does not stop a staff member delegating to themselves; combined with break-glass this gave about 30 days of Owner rights (MF-02, QA-03, QA-26). The fix rejects self-delegation, computes the grantor's grantable set from their base role only (not from token grants), blocks chained delegation (a delegate cannot re-delegate borrowed grants), requires step-up when the delegated role is the built-in Owner, and revokes the target's sessions on create and revoke so the new grant set takes effect immediately. The 30-day cap stays.
acceptance: Given a staff member with staff:edit, when they create a delegation to themselves, then 403 SELF_DELEGATION (DelegationEscalationTest).
Given a staff member currently holding a break-glass or delegated grant, when they delegate a role whose grants exceed their base role, then 403 GRANT_EXCEEDS_BASE_ROLE.
Given a delegate, when they try to re-delegate the delegated role, then 403 CHAINED_DELEGATION.
Given a delegation of the built-in Owner role, when no step-up token is sent, then 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED.
Given a delegation is created or revoked, then the target's sessions are revoked within 60 s and an audit row role.delegation_created / role.delegation_revoked exists.

stories.title: Assigning a role can never give more than the assigner has, and every change is audited
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want staff who can invite or edit colleagues to be unable to hand out roles richer than their own, with every role change audited and applied immediately, so that nobody can make themselves or a friend an Owner.
stories.context: Role create/update enforces 'no grant beyond your own' (RoleService ~L77-97), but PATCH /v1/staff/{id} and the invite flow accept any roleId, including the built-in Owner role, check only that it exists (StaffService ~L85-96, ~L116-118), do not audit role/scope changes and do not revoke sessions (MF-11, SEC-08, AD-02). The fix extracts the subset check into one iam GrantAuthority helper used by role edit, staff patch and invite; only an Owner may assign the built-in Owner role; scope (own_patients_only vs all_clinic_patients) and field-grant changes are subject to the same rule; every change writes an audit row with before/after; and the target's sessions are revoked (PLT-007 reason role_changed).

Given a non-Owner with staff:create, when they invite someone with the built-in Owner role, then 403.
Given any role, scope or field-grant change, then an audit row staff.role_changed with before/after role id, scope and field grants is written.
Given a role change, then the target's sessions are revoked within 60 s.
Given an Owner, when they assign any role, then it succeeds (Owner holds all grants).

stories.title: Every new clinic starts with the preset role bundles, and doctors are found by a clinician flag
stories.story: As a new clinic owner I want my clinic to come with ready role bundles (Owner, Owner-doctor, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Front-desk + Vitals) that match the RBAC matrix, so that I can invite my team in minutes and doctor pickers never go empty because someone renamed a role.
stories.context: Provisioning seeds only the Owner role, and doctors are found by role name ILIKE 'doctor', so renaming a role empties every doctor picker (FRD F-08/CAD-02, old RBAC matrix). ProvisioningStepRunner will seed six preset roles exactly as the RBAC matrix (10 modules x 7 actions) with a preset_code and preset_version; owners may edit presets and reset them to the current preset. A staff.is_clinician flag (set when a clinical licence/registration is recorded, coordinated with T-058 in the Clinical domain) drives doctor pickers, schedules and queue assignment via ActorDirectory (PLT-033) instead of role names. Existing tenants are backfilled. Generated RBAC-matrix tests (T-090, QA) verify the seed.
acceptance: Given a newly provisioned tenant, then it has exactly the roles Owner, Owner-doctor, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist and Front-desk+Vitals with grants equal to the RBAC matrix (T-090 matrix test green).
Given an owner renames the Doctor role to 'Consultant', then every doctor picker (calendar, queue assignment, Rx signer list) still lists the same clinicians.
Given an owner edits a preset and then clicks 'Reset to preset', then grants return to the current preset version and an audit row is written.

Given existing tenants, after the backfill migration, then staff with a role named like doctor and a registration number have is_clinician=true and a report lists any ambiguous rows for owner confirmation.
Given the Owner preset, then it does not include clinical:approve unless the owner is also a clinician (Owner-doctor), per MF-52.

stories.title: RLS is real: migrator owns the tables, the app runs as a NOBYPASSRLS role, every tenant table has forced per-command policies, and boot fails otherwise
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want the database itself to refuse to show or change another clinic's rows, even if application code forgets a tenant filter, so that one bug cannot leak my patients' data.
stories.context: Flyway runs as the app user (application.yml has no spring.flyway.user; Dockerfile and scripts/dev-up.sh migrate at app boot), so nabd_app owns every table and Postgres skips RLS for owners; no table has FORCE RLS; no policy has an explicit WITH CHECK; and login_attempts, workflow_definitions, package_eligible_doctors, owners, brands, legal_entities and tax_registrations have no RLS (MF-03 Critical, MF-63). Tests pass only because ApiTestBase migrates as superuser and connects as a different role. The fix: a roles bootstrap (nabd_migrator owns schemas and runs Flyway as a separate job; nabd_app is DML-only NOBYPASSRLS with statement_timeout 5s, lock_timeout 3s, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 15s; nabd_reports read-only; nabd_definer owns SECURITY DEFINER functions); a generated migration that sets FORCE RLS and replaces each USING-only policy with ADR-07 per-command policies on every tenant table (the 20 brand-widened tables are handled in PLT-018); RLS for the remaining tables (workflow_definitions allows tenant_id IS NULL rows for read only; package_eligible_doctors gains tenant_id; owner PIN hashes become reachable only through SECURITY DEFINER functions); and an RlsInvariantVerifier that fails application start if the runtime role owns a tenant table, has BYPASSRLS, or any tenant_id table lacks forced RLS or a WITH CHECK policy. The prod-config CI job (T-020, QA) boots exactly this topology.
acceptance: Given the deployed topology, then `SELECT relname FROM pg_class WHERE relowner = 'nabd_app'::regrole` returns no rows and nabd_app has rolbypassrls = false (RlsSchemaInvariantTest).

Given every table in public with a tenant_id column, then relrowsecurity and relforcerowsecurity are true and pg_policies shows a SELECT policy and INSERT/UPDATE policies with WITH CHECK (or the table is listed in an explicit, reviewed exemption file).
Given the app connects as a role that owns a tenant table or has BYPASSRLS, when it boots, then startup fails with a message naming the offending table or role.
Given a repository query that omits the tenant predicate, when run under tenant A's context, then it returns only tenant A's rows; an INSERT with tenant B's tenant_id fails with an RLS violation.
Given scripts/dev-up.sh, then local development runs Flyway as nabd_migrator and the app as nabd_app, and the existing 560 RLS tests are green under that topology.
Given the CI prod-config job (T-020), then Flyway runs as migrator, the app as nabd_app, and the suite passes.

stories.title: Contain brand-visibility widening and switch to the fast array policy
stories.story: As a clinic owner in a group I want sibling clinics unable to read or write my patients through a database setting, and as a receptionist I want check-in to stay fast, so that sharing happens only with consent and the morning queue never stalls.
stories.context: TenantContext.set populates app.accessible_tenant_ids from brands.data_visibility_scope, and 20 tables (patients, staff, sessions, roles, appointments, queue_entries, consents, patient_merges, doctor_working_hours, doctor_leave, clinical_notes and nine setup tables in V6, V17, V19) use OR-shaped USING policies with no WITH CHECK: reads widen without consent, writes into siblings are allowed, TENANT scope is unilateral, and the OR defeats indexes (nextTokenNumber 933 ms inside the check-in lock) (MF-04 Critical, CONS §7 M0/M1). This story runs CONS M0 (inventory of brands with scope <> FACILITY and owner contact) and M1: rewrites the 20 policies to the ADR-07 per-command form (indexable `tenant_id = ANY(uuid[])` read, single-tenant WITH CHECK), removes widening on staff, sessions and roles unconditionally, and makes TenantContext set app.visible_tenant_ids to the single tenant unless the `nabd.legacy-brand-visibility` flag is on and the brand is on an allow-list (default off). It also adds explicit tenant_id predicates to QueueRepository.nextTokenNumber, ScheduleRepository.countSessionOccupancy, the PatientRepository registry subqueries and AuthRepository lookups.
acceptance: Given a brand with data_visibility_scope=BRAND and the legacy flag off, when facility A's staff query patients, then only facility A's rows are returned.

Given any widened table, when tenant A's session inserts or updates a row with tenant B's tenant_id, then the statement fails with an RLS WITH CHECK violation (CrossFacilityVisibilityTest extended to writes).
Given staff, sessions or roles, then no flag value widens them.
Given a 500k-patient fixture, when nextTokenNumber runs, then EXPLAIN shows an index scan and execution is <= 5 ms (was 933 ms) (plan-regression test).
Given the M0 inventory, then a report lists every brand not on FACILITY with its owner, and each owner is contacted before the flag default changes in prod.
Given the flag on and the brand on the allow-list (test only), then reads widen but writes into siblings still fail.

stories.title: Tenant context is bound when a transaction starts and can never silently change
stories.story: As an engineer on any module I want the tenant to be bound automatically from the signed-in user at transaction start, and any attempt to switch it mid-transaction to fail loudly, so that I cannot introduce a cross-tenant bug by forgetting or misusing TenantContext.
stories.context: TenantContext.set is called by hand at about 240 sites, nothing asserts a transaction is active, and AuditService.record calls TenantContext.set(tenantId) inside the caller's transaction, silently replacing app.tenant_id for the rest of it (MF-62, ARCH-19, SEC-32). A forgotten call today fails closed (no rows) only by luck of set_config semantics. The fix binds the tenant from the SecurityContext (JWT tenantId) when a Spring-managed transaction begins (TransactionSynchronization on a tenant-aware DataSource), makes TenantContext.set throw if no transaction is active or if a different tenant is already bound, makes AuditService assert the tenant is unchanged, and provides an explicit TenantScope.run(tenantId, ...) API for workers and system jobs. @CurrentTenant/@CurrentStaff argument resolvers replace tenantId(Jwt) helpers; the tenantId parameters are removed module by module by S6. This unblocks every squad and the Modulith boundary work.
acceptance: Given a repository call on an RLS table outside a transaction, then it throws IllegalStateException in tests and is flagged by an ArchUnit rule.
Given a request authenticated for tenant A, when a @Transactional service method starts, then app.tenant_id and app.visible_tenant_ids are already set to A without any explicit call.
Given a transaction bound to tenant A, when code calls TenantContext.set(B) or AuditService.record(B, ...), then it throws TenantMismatchException and the transaction rolls back.
Given a worker job (outbox handler, ETA engine), then it must use TenantScope.run(tenantId, ...) and an ArchUnit rule forbids TenantContext.set outside shared/tenancy.
Given the codebase at S6, then the count of explicit tenantId method parameters on service methods has dropped to 0 in modules migrated so far (CI metric reported per sprint).

stories.title: Composite tenant foreign keys on the clinical spine
stories.story: As an engineer I want foreign keys that include tenant_id so that a row in clinic A can never reference clinic B's patient, staff member or visit, even if an id is replayed.
stories.context: Single-column foreign keys are checked by Postgres without RLS, so tenant A can insert a row referencing tenant B's patient or staff id (MF-64, DP-18, QA-28). The fix adds UNIQUE (tenant_id, id) on parent tables (patients, staff, queue_entries, appointments, invoices, prescriptions, clinical_notes, departments) and replaces child FKs on the clinical spine with composite (tenant_id, x_id) FKs: vitals, clinical_notes, prescriptions, patient_allergies, chronic_conditions, clinical_documents, vaccine_records, dental_chart_entries, queue_entries, appointments, invoices, consents. Migrations follow expand/contract: unique indexes CONCURRENTLY, FKs added NOT VALID, then VALIDATE in a separate migration with lock_timeout. The cross-tenant id-replay fuzzer (T-100, QA) proves it.
acceptance: Given tenant A's session and tenant B's patient id, when a vitals, note, prescription, allergy, document, queue entry, appointment, invoice or consent row is inserted referencing it, then the insert fails with a foreign-key violation mapped to 404 NOT_FOUND (not 500).
Given the id-replay fuzzer (T-100) run nightly, then it finds 0 cross-tenant references.
Given production-size data (500k patients), then each VALIDATE CONSTRAINT completes without blocking writes for more than lock_timeout (3 s) and the migration lint passes.
Given the existing data, then a pre-check query finds 0 rows whose child tenant_id differs from the parent's; any found are reported before VALIDATE.

stories.title: One login and a branch switcher for staff and owners who work across branches
stories.story: As a doctor who works mornings at one branch and evenings at another I want one login and a branch switcher so that I do not juggle two accounts and every action still lands in the right branch.
stories.context: Owners already pick a workspace after login (OwnerService); staff exist per facility with separate credentials. For branch-lite, this story adds a brand-level login identity that links the staff rows a person has in each branch of the same brand. stories.title: Retried POSTs never double-charge or double-register: Idempotency-Key everywhere it matters
stories.story: As a receptionist on flaky clinic Wi-Fi I want a payment, check-in or registration that I retry to happen exactly once so that no patient is charged twice or gets two tokens.
stories.context: Retried POSTs (Wi-Fi drops, double taps) can double-charge or double-register; submitPayment has no catch (MF-26, ARCH-25, FE-11). This story adds a shared IdempotencyFilter and an idempotency_keys table: for endpoints annotated @Idempotent (payments, check-in, registration, booking, refunds, Rx sign, and every Core /internal/v1 command from Edge and Comms), the first request stores an in-progress row keyed by (tenant, actor, key) with a hash of method, path and body; a retry with the same key and body replays the stored status and body with Idempotent-Replayed: true; the same key with a different body returns 422; a concurrent duplicate while the first is in flight returns 409 IN_PROGRESS. Failed (5xx) attempts release the key. Stored responses are encrypted (they may hold PHI) and purged after 24 h. The generated api-client (Frontend) sends a UUIDv7 key per user action.
acceptance: Given a payment POST with Idempotency-Key K that succeeded, when the same request is retried with K, then the original 201 body is returned with Idempotent-Replayed: true and exactly one payment row exists.
Given two identical check-in requests with the same key arriving 5 ms apart, then exactly one queue entry is created; the loser gets 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS or the original response.
Given key K reused with a different body, then 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
Given the first attempt failed with 500, when retried with K, then it is processed again.
Given an @Idempotent endpoint called without the header, then 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED (staff-web and Edge always send it).
Given 24 h after creation, then the key row is purged by the purge job.

api.response: original status/body; header Idempotent-Replayed: true on replay

stories.title: Every error is clean Problem+JSON, every list is bounded, and API responses carry security headers
stories.story: As an engineer I want every failure mapped to a Problem+JSON response, every list endpoint capped at 100 rows, and safe headers on every API response, so that clients handle errors predictably and no request can dump the patient table.
stories.context: Only two exception types are handled: a missing claim gives 500, limit=0 or -5 gives 500, limit=1000000 returns every patient, and 59 list endpoints are unbounded (MF-38, ARCH-23, ARCH-24, QA-19, QA-42). The API also sends no security headers (F-15 backend part, NB-291). The fix enables spring.mvc.problemdetails, makes GlobalExceptionHandler extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler with typed Problem types (validation, not_found, conflict, forbidden, rate_limited, internal with traceId only), introduces a shared PageRequest (@Min(1) @Max(100), default 25) and cursor resolver used by every list endpoint, and sets Cache-Control: no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, Strict-Transport-Security and a deny-all CSP with frame-ancestors 'none' on API responses. Given GET /v1/patients?limit=1000000, then 400; without limit, then at most 25 rows and a nextCursor.
Given a request with a token missing an expected claim, then 401 Problem, never 500.
Given any unhandled exception, then 500 Problem with traceId and no stack trace or SQL text.

Given any /v1 response, then headers include Cache-Control: no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, Strict-Transport-Security max-age >= 31536000 and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'.
Given the Schemathesis smoke on all list endpoints, then 0 server errors (not_a_server_error).

stories.title: Secure upload pipeline: type check, size limit, antivirus scan and tenant-scoped regional storage
stories.story: As a doctor I want patients' outside reports and photos uploaded safely so that I can rely on them in the consult without risking malware or another clinic seeing them.
stories.context: There is no binary upload, object store or file handling anywhere (MF-23, F-19, NB-292); this must exist before any upload feature ships (EP19, DOC-08, DENT-02, GYN-02). The pipeline: the client asks Core for an upload slot (purpose, declared type and size), gets a pre-signed PUT to a quarantine bucket in the cell's region, then calls complete. A worker sniffs magic bytes (allow-list: PDF, JPEG, PNG, HEIC converted to JPEG, later DICOM), enforces size (20 MB default), strips EXIF location, scans with ClamAV in the cell, computes SHA-256, and moves clean files to the tenant prefix of the regional bucket (server-side encryption with the tenant key once PLT-045 lands). Infected or mismatched files are quarantined and the uploader and owner are told. Inbound WhatsApp media from Comms Gateway enters the same pipeline.
acceptance: Given a PDF of 3 MB, when uploaded and completed, then it becomes available within 30 s p95 with status 'available' and a stored SHA-256.
Given a file whose magic bytes are an executable but declared as PDF, then it is rejected with status 'rejected_type' and never leaves quarantine.
Given the EICAR test file, then status 'infected', the uploader sees 'File blocked', and the owner gets an in-app alert.
Given a JPEG with GPS EXIF, then the stored version has no location metadata.
Given storage keys, then every object lives under tenant/{tenantId}/ in the tenant's region bucket and no bucket is public.
Given a 25 MB upload when the limit is 20 MB, then init returns 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE.

stories.title: Tamper-evident audit chain that does not fork, does not serialise the clinic, and is verified every night
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want the audit trail to be provably untampered, checked every night, with an alarm if anyone alters it, so that I can show an auditor that the record of who did what is intact.
stories.context: The audit hash chain (V14) finds the previous row with `SELECT row_hash FROM audit_log ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE`, which forks under concurrency, depends on RLS to scope to the tenant (global when RLS is inert), hashes created_at::text (timezone-dependent), serialises all writes of a tenant behind a backward scan (5 s), and is never verified (MF-31, ARCH-07, DP-05, SEC-27). The fix adds an audit_chain_heads row per tenant updated with `UPDATE ... RETURNING` inside the insert trigger (a short row lock per tenant, independent of RLS), hashes the UTC epoch in microseconds and canonical jsonb, versions the hash formula (hash_v=2; v1 rows verify with the old formula), runs an incremental nightly verify per tenant from the last checkpoint, writes a signed checkpoint (KMS asymmetric key) to object storage with object lock (off-box), and raises a security incident on any failure (SLO: 100%, zero budget). The trigger functions are owned by nabd_definer so the app role cannot disable them.
acceptance: Given 50 parallel audit writes for one tenant, then verify_audit_chain returns intact (no fork) (AuditChainConcurrencyTest).
Given writes for 10 tenants in parallel, then they do not wait on each other (p95 audit insert < 10 ms).
Given the session TimeZone is changed to Asia/Dubai, then hashes of new rows equal those computed under UTC.

Given the nightly job, then every tenant's chain is verified incrementally from its last checkpoint and a signed checkpoint (tenant, last_id, last_hash, signature) is written to the off-box bucket with object lock.
Given a superuser alters an audit row in staging, then the next verify fails, an alert pages the on-call as a security incident within 15 minutes, and the platform health screen shows the failure.
Given nabd_app, then it cannot DISABLE TRIGGER or UPDATE/DELETE audit_log (owner is nabd_migrator; functions owned by nabd_definer).

stories.title: Every read of patient data is recorded in an append-only, batch-sealed read log
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want every view of a patient's record logged with who, when, what and why so that I can answer 'who looked at this patient' and detect someone browsing records they should not.
stories.context: PHI reads are not audited at all (MF-18 High, SEC-09, F-09), which blocks DPDP, CERT-In, the owner audit screen and the patient 'who accessed my record' view. Per doc06 D8 the read log is separate from audit_log: a monthly-partitioned, append-only phi_read_log written synchronously in the request (one cheap insert, no chain), then sealed asynchronously in batches (batch hash chained to the previous batch). A PhiReadRecorder aspect records reads on every /v1/clinical/** GET, patient detail, timeline, documents, exports, support views, brand-directory lookups and signed-URL issuance, with actor, session, patient, resource type/id, purpose (treatment, billing, support, break_glass, export, directory) and request id. A read-volume rule alerts the owner and security when one actor reads more than N distinct patients per hour (defaults 60 non-clinician, 150 clinician). Online retention is 13 months pending DPO confirmation, then archive (PLT-042).
acceptance: Given every clinical GET endpoint, then exactly one phi_read_log row per request is written with actor, patient, resource type and purpose (PhiReadAuditTest enumerates /v1/clinical/** mappings).
Given a list endpoint returning 25 patients, then one row per patient returned is written (batched insert) without exceeding +15 ms p95.
Given a request that fails (4xx/5xx), then no read row is written.
Given phi_read_log, then UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE raise, partitions are monthly, and a sealing job seals each minute's rows into phi_read_batches with batch_hash chained to the previous batch.
Given a receptionist who opens 61 different patients' clinical records within an hour, then the owner receives an in-app alert and a security event is emitted.
Given a consult screen load (timeline + notes + vitals + Rx), then total added latency is < 20 ms p95.

stories.story: As the Nabd platform team I want audit_log, phi_read_log, sessions and outbox partitioned by month and old partitions archived to regional storage so that the database stays fast and cheap as audit grows by 300-500 GB a year, without breaking verification or retention.

stories.story: As the IT head of a polyclinic group I want Nabd's security and audit events streamed to our SIEM in a standard format so that our security team monitors Nabd with the rest of our systems.

stories.title: Encrypted fields carry a key version and are bound to their tenant and row
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want encrypted fields such as national IDs and MFA secrets tied to my clinic and to their row, with keys that can be rotated, so that one leaked key or copied ciphertext cannot expose other clinics' data.
stories.context: One global AES key (APP_CRYPTO_KEY) encrypts every tenant's national IDs and TOTP secrets across regions, with no key version and no associated data, so rotation is impossible and a ciphertext copied to another row decrypts fine (MF-20 S2 part, SEC-11, ARCH-36, F-11). This story replaces AesGcmCipher with a FieldCipher: ciphertext format = version byte + key id + 96-bit IV + ciphertext+tag; AAD = tenantId:table:column:rowId; keys come from a keyring in the secret manager with one active kid. A resumable re-encrypt job migrates existing values (staff.mfa_secret_enc, master.operators.mfa_secret_enc, owners.mfa_secret_enc, patients national id columns, idempotency response bodies) table by table with a progress checkpoint. Regional KMS with per-tenant keys follows in PLT-045.
acceptance: Given a new encrypted value, then it starts with the format version and key id and decrypts only with AAD tenantId:table:column:rowId.

Given a ciphertext copied from patient A's row to patient B's row (same tenant or another), then decryption fails and the API returns 500-free handling (field shown as unavailable, error logged without values).
Given the re-encrypt job, then all legacy values are rewritten in the new format, the job can stop and resume from its checkpoint, and a verification pass decrypts 100% of rows.
Given a new active kid in the keyring, then new writes use it and old values still decrypt; re-running the job rotates them.
Given the prod profile without a keyring, then boot fails.

stories.title: Per-tenant data keys wrapped by the region's KMS, with rotation and crypto-shredding
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want my clinic's data encrypted with its own key held in my country's KMS so that my data stays in-region and can be made permanently unreadable when I leave Nabd.
stories.context: After key versioning (PLT-044), the target is per-tenant data encryption keys wrapped by a regional KMS key in the cell (MF-20 S6 part, NB-283 go-live blocker, EP09, PS-01). Each tenant gets a DEK at provisioning, stored wrapped in tenant_data_keys; Core unwraps through a KmsClient port (cloud KMS in the India region; provider per doc06 D2) and caches unwrapped DEKs in memory only (Caffeine, max 15 minutes, never in Valkey). FieldCipher selects the tenant DEK by kid. A rotation job re-wraps DEKs when the KMS key rotates and can rotate DEKs (re-encrypting via PLT-044's job). Offboarding can crypto-shred: destroying the wrapped DEK makes all of that tenant's field ciphertext unreadable, including in backups. Object storage (PLT-029) uses the same tenant key for server-side encryption.
acceptance: Given a newly provisioned tenant, then a DEK is generated, wrapped by the IN-region KMS key and stored before any patient row is written (provisioning step 'Tenant, keys & backups').
Given two tenants, then their encrypted fields use different DEKs (test decrypts with the wrong DEK and fails).
Given KMS key rotation, then the rotation job re-wraps all DEKs without downtime and records rotated_at.
Given crypto-shred of a test tenant, then all its encrypted fields (and a restored backup copy) are unreadable, while other tenants are unaffected.
Given KMS is unreachable, then cached DEKs keep working up to 15 minutes, after which requests needing decryption return 503 TENANT_KEY_UNAVAILABLE and an alert fires.
Given the platform regions screen, then each region shows its KMS key age and last rotation.

stories.title: Patient asks for their data on WhatsApp and gets a complete export within the legal deadline
stories.story: As a patient I want to ask my clinic for a copy of all my data from WhatsApp or the patient web page and receive it as a secure download so that I can exercise my rights without visiting or emailing anyone.
stories.context: DPDP applies from 13 May 2027 (EP31, MF-22, PS-09, CMP-03, DPO-02, NB-243/244, PAT-14, B-02). This story builds the DSR engine's intake, queue and export: requests arrive from WhatsApp (bot flow on Patient Access Edge) or patient-web after OTP verification (L1), or are logged by the desk for walk-ins; types are access/export, correction and erasure (erasure executes in PLT-048); each request gets statutory due dates per market (configurable; defaults to be confirmed by the DPO) and appears in the owner's privacy queue with countdowns. Access/export builds a machine-readable package (JSON plus a readable PDF summary) by calling each module's export API (patient, visits, clinical, prescriptions, invoices, consents, messages metadata, read log entries about the patient), encrypts it and delivers it through a secure link (T-179) valid for 72 h. stories.title: Erasure requests are executed safely: 48-hour notice, sectoral retention respected, nothing half-deleted
stories.story: As a patient I want my erasure request honoured for everything the clinic is not legally required to keep, with notice before it happens, so that I keep control without the clinic breaking medical-record law.
stories.context: Erasure must respect sectoral retention: medical records must be kept for legally required periods (e.g. IMC Regulations require at least 3 years in India; FRD market defaults), so 'erase' becomes: delete marketing and messaging data, withdraw processing consents, de-identify contact data where allowed, and restrict (not delete) clinical records under retention or legal hold, with a clear explanation to the patient. The engine sends a pre-erasure notice 48 h before execution (T-237 acceptance; DPDP Rules), then runs per-module ErasureHandlers in a saga with idempotent steps and a final verification. Audit and read logs are not erased (legal basis) but stop showing the patient's name once erased (pseudonymous ref). Legal hold (PLT-049) blocks execution. Must be live before 13 May 2027.

Given a legal hold on the patient, then execution is blocked and the patient is told why within the due date.
Given the patient record after erasure, then staff search no longer finds the patient by name or phone, and audit views show a pseudonymous reference.

stories.title: Retention clocks per data class and market, with legal hold
stories.story: As a clinic owner I want data deleted or anonymised automatically when its legal retention period ends, and frozen when there is a legal hold, so that I comply without configuring anything.
stories.context: No retention or legal-hold machinery exists (EP31, MF-22, CMP-05, DPO-05, NB-245/246/247). The FRD removed custom retention authoring (DPO-05A): clinics get market-default schedules only, and can never set retention below the legal floor. This story seeds retention_policies per market and data class (clinical OPD records, inpatient/medico-legal, invoices per tax law, messages, marketing leads, audit logs, security logs with 1-year retention for app logs and 180 days CERT-In minimum in India), a nightly job that finds records whose clock has run out (trigger: last visit, creation, account closure), sends the India 48 h pre-deletion notice where required, and executes via the ErasureHandlers from PLT-048. legal_holds (per patient, per tenant or per case) block both retention and erasure until released.

Given a patient whose clinical retention ends, then a 48 h notice is sent (India) before anonymisation.
Given an owner places a legal hold on a patient, then retention and erasure skip that patient and the hold is audited; releasing it resumes clocks.
Given an attempt to set a retention below the market floor, then the API rejects it (no custom retention below legal floors).
Given the nightly job, then a report per tenant shows items deleted, anonymised, skipped by hold, and errors.

stories.title: Provisioning steps run exactly once, even when two operators click at the same time
stories.story: As a Nabd onboarding operator I want each provisioning step to run once and be safe to retry so that a double click or a crash never creates two tenants or a half-built clinic.

Given 200 jobs, then listJobs runs one query and returns in < 200 ms.
Given a failing step, then rollback compensations run in reverse order and the job ends rolled_back.

Given login_routes, then it holds only HMACs and region codes (no names, phones or emails).
Given the operator fleet view, then data comes from regional aggregates only and no patient-level field is returned (contract test).
Given a cell is unreachable, then the console shows that region as unavailable and other regions still load.
